data.title: Show HN: ClickStack – Open-source Datadog alternative by ClickHouse and HyperDX
data.author: mikeshi42
data.article_summary: HyperDX 是一个开源的可观测性平台，集成了会话回放、日志、指标、 traces 和错误监控，基于 ClickHouse 和 OpenTelemetry 构建，帮助工程师快速解决生产环境问题。它支持在 ClickHouse 集群上轻松搜索和可视化日志及 traces，提供直观的全文本搜索和属性搜索，支持设置警报和分析异常趋势。HyperDX 可以通过 Docker 快速部署，兼容 OpenTelemetry，支持多种语言和平台的应用监控。平台文档、贡献指南和部署选项详见其官网和文档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕HyperDX及其相关技术栈（如ClickHouse、OTel、Grafana等）的比较与选择，功能特性、性能、成本以及用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• [theogravity] 认为HyperDX相对于DataDog成本更低，并表示有兴趣将HyperDX与自己开发的LogLayer集成，以丰富其多logger支持能力。
• [readdit] 赞赏HyperDX的性价比，并关注HyperDX是否会因为Clickhouse的合并而逐步淘汰原产品，并需要迁移到ClickStack。
• [Omnipresent] 质疑为何不使用Grafana作为前端，而是开发自定义前端，认为Grafana已经足够好用。
• [hosh] 对OTel的指标功能持保留态度，认为其过于复杂。关注ClickStack是否支持statsd数据摄入、跨 traces、logging 和 metrics 的关联，以及Elixir SDK为何使用hyperdx库而非otel库，并询问Notebooks是否在产品路线图中。
• [wiradikusuma] 和 [codegeek] 都将HyperDX与Signoz进行比较，指出两者都是基于ClickHouse的观察性工具，询问两者之间的区别。
• [JimDabell] 提到在使用过程中遇到的UI/UX问题，包括字体和颜色搭配，认为阅读体验较差，影响使用意愿。
• [bilalq] 关心Clickhouse是否为唯一的状态组件，并希望与Rotel兼容，以支持无服务器环境的使用，同时提到Datadog在性能上的优势。
• [gigatexal] 认为Datadog虽然昂贵，但功能强大，能够节省工程时间，并通过丰富的集成（如Slack通知）带来便利。
• [regnerba] 使用Grafana全栈（Loki, Tempo, Prometheus等），认为组件较多但稳定，询问HyperDX与其现有方案的比较。
• [dustedcodes] 关心如何在k8s上自托管HyperDX，询问具体部署方式。
• [user3939382] 表示对众多日志聚合工具感到困惑，认为Datadog价格高且UI复杂。
• [ensignavenger] 关注HyperDX是否依赖MongoDB，并询问是否有其他开源的兼容文档存储方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是HyperDX与Datadog的性价比对比，部分用户认为Datadog虽然昂贵但功能和性能优越，而HyperDX提供了一种更具成本效益的选择。
• 另一个讨论点是与Signoz的比较，用户希望了解两者在功能和使用场景上的差异。
• 技术实现方面，用户关心ClickStack对不同数据格式和传输协议的支持，如statsd、OTel、以及与Rust的Rotel兼容性。
• UX/UI问题也被提出，部分用户对HyperDX的界面设计表示不满，认为需要改进以提高可读性和易用性。
• 自托管和集成问题也被多次提及，用户希望了解如何在现有技术栈（如k8s、Grafana）中集成和部署HyperDX。

总体而言，讨论围绕HyperDX的功能、成本、技术实现和用户体验展开，用户对其与Datadog、Signoz等竞争产品的差异以及具体技术实现细节表示关注。

HyperDX
HyperDX
, a core component of
ClickStack
, helps engineers
quickly figure out why production is broken by making it easy to search &
visualize logs and traces on top of any ClickHouse cluster (imagine Kibana, for
ClickHouse).
Documentation
•
Chat on Discord
•
Live Demo
•
Bug Reports
•
Contributing
•
Website
🕵️ Correlate/search logs, metrics, session replays and traces all in one place
📝 Schema agnostic, works on top of your existing ClickHouse schema
🔥 Blazing fast searches & visualizations optimized for ClickHouse
🔍 Intuitive full-text search and property search syntax (ex.
level:err
),
SQL optional!
📊 Analyze trends in anomalies with event deltas
🔔 Set up alerts in just a few clicks
📈 Dashboard high cardinality events without a complex query language
{
Native JSON string querying
⚡ Live tail logs and traces to always get the freshest events
🔭 OpenTelemetry supported out of the box
⏱️ Monitor health and performance from HTTP requests to DB queries (APM)
Spinning Up HyperDX
HyperDX can be deployed as part of ClickStack, which includes ClickHouse,
HyperDX, OpenTelemetry Collector and MongoDB.
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 4317:4317 -p 4318:4318 docker.hyperdx.io/hyperdx/hyperdx-all-in-one
Afterwards, you can visit
http://localhost:8080
to access the HyperDX UI.
If you already have an existing ClickHouse instance, want to use a single
container locally, or are looking for production deployment instructions, you
can view the different deployment options in our
deployment docs
.
If your server is behind a firewall, you'll need to open/forward port 8080,
8000 and 4318 on your firewall for the UI, API and OTel collector
respectively.
We recommend at least 4GB of RAM and 2 cores for testing.
Hosted ClickHouse Cloud
You can also deploy HyperDX with ClickHouse Cloud, you can
sign up for free
and get started in
just minutes.
Instrumenting Your App
To get logs, metrics, traces, session replay, etc into HyperDX, you'll need to
instrument your app to collect and send telemetry data over to your HyperDX
instance.
We provide a set of SDKs and integration options to make it easier to get
started with HyperDX, such as
Browser
,
Node.js
,
and
Python
You can find the full list in
our docs
.
OpenTelemetry
Additionally, HyperDX is compatible with
OpenTelemetry
, a vendor-neutral standard for
instrumenting your application backed by CNCF. Supported languages/platforms
include:
Kubernetes
Javascript
Python
Java
Go
Ruby
PHP
.NET
Elixir
Rust
(Full list
here
)
Once HyperDX is running, you can point your OpenTelemetry SDK to the
OpenTelemetry collector spun up at
http://localhost:4318
.
Contributing
We welcome all contributions! There's many ways to contribute to the project,
including but not limited to:
Opening a PR (
Contribution Guide
)
Submitting feature requests or bugs
Improving our product or contribution documentation
Voting on
open issues
or
contributing use cases to a feature request
Motivation
Our mission is to help engineers ship reliable software. To enable that, we
believe every engineer needs to be able to easily leverage production telemetry
to quickly solve burning production issues.
However, in our experience, the existing tools we've used tend to fall short in
a few ways:
They're expensive, and the pricing has failed to scale with TBs of telemetry
becoming the norm, leading to teams aggressively cutting the amount of data
they can collect.
They're hard to use, requiring full-time SREs to set up, and domain experts
to use confidently.
They requiring hopping from tool to tool (logs, session replay, APM,
exceptions, etc.) to stitch together the clues yourself.
We hope you give HyperDX in ClickStack a try an

data.title: How Common Is Multiple Invention?
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了多个发明家独立同时发明相同技术或产品的现象，如贝尔和格雷的电话专利之争，以及爱迪生和斯旺的灯泡发明。这种“多重发现”在科技史上很常见，William Ogburn和Dorothy Thomas记录了150个案例，Robert Merton则发现了261个例子。

文章探讨了多重发明的发生频率，Matt Clancy估计约2-3%的科学发现是同时发生的，而一项发明在未来十年内被重新发明的概率约为8%。不过，不同研究的结果存在差异。低频率可能意味着技术进步依赖少数“天才”发明家，而高频率则暗示进步是由广泛历史力量推动的。

作者通过分析维基百科的历史发明时间线，研究1800至1970年间的190项发明，发现多重发明现象并不罕见，但具体频率因定义和研究方法而异。最终，多重发明的频率可以帮助我们理解技术进步的本质及其历史依赖性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多重发现与独立发明的现象及其背后的原因

不同观点：
• **灵感与偶然性**：milliams引用Terry Pratchett的观点，认为许多伟大发现源于一瞬间的灵感，但这些灵感往往错过正确的接收者，导致错失潜在的重大发明。这种现象被视为一种悲剧，因为灵感常常被浪费或错配。
• **资源与实验**：Animats认为发明不仅仅是灵感的结果，还需要大量的实验和资源支持。以爱迪生为例，说明通过系统性实验和团队合作才能实现从概念到产品的转化。
• **材料科学与时机**：dlcarrier强调发明是否可行取决于材料科学的发展。Lillienfeld虽然描述了晶体管的概念，但受限于材料科学，未能实现。发明的实现需要时机，当科学条件成熟时，多重独立发明会几乎同时出现。
• **社会与科技发展的必然性**：paulorlando引用了Charles Fort的观点，认为科技发展如同植物生长，有其必然性。社会和技术发展到一定阶段，某些发明就会自然而然地出现，不依赖于个别人的灵感或努力。
• **形态共振理论**：myflash13介绍了形态共振理论，认为想法如同无线电波存在于环境中，不同的人可能同时接收到相同的想法，导致多重独立发明的出现。该理论还提出了一些实验证据支持这一观点。
• **历史与偶然性**：theendisney和ryao提到历史上多次出现多人几乎同时发明相同技术的情况，如望远镜和快速傅里叶变换（FFT）。这些例子显示了历史中的偶然性和竞争性。

补充讨论：
• **执行力与历史书写**：chvid和raymondgh提到，在“大创意”上，多人竞争或互相借鉴是很常见的。历史往往由胜利者书写，影响了发明的归属。执行力和时机对发明能否成功进入市场至关重要。
• **多重发现的统计**：david-gpu引用文章数据，指出独立发现的现象虽然不普遍（约2-3%的科学发现和8%的发明），但确实存在。
• **有趣的巧合**：ljsprague和somat提到一些有趣的历史巧合，如Rubik's Cube的独立发明和铝 refinement过程的独立同时发现，增加了讨论的趣味性和复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 灵感和资源对发明的重要性：milliams和Animats的观点代表了两种极端，一个强调灵感，另一个强调系统性实验和资源支持。
• 历史书写的公正性：chvid认为历史往往由胜利者书写，影响了发明的实际归属和认知。

Patent sketches of Gray’s (top) and Bell’s (bottom) telephones, via
Hounshell
.
When Alexander Graham Bell filed a patent for the telephone on February 14th, 1876, he beat competing telephone developer Elisha Gray to the patent office by just a few hours. The resulting legal dispute between Bell Telephone and Western Union (which owned the rights to Gray’s invention) would consume millions of dollars before being resolved in Bell’s favor in 1879.
Such cases of multiple invention are common, and some of the most famous and important modern inventions were invented in parallel. Both Thomas Edison and Joseph Swan patented incandescent lightbulbs in 1880. Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce patented integrated circuits in 1959. Hans von Ohain and Frank Whittle independently invented the jet engine in the 1930s. In a
1922 paper
, William Ogburn and Dorothy Thomas documented 150 cases of multiple discovery in science and technology. Robert Merton
found 261 examples in 1961
, and observed that the phenomenon of multiple discovery was itself a multiple discovery, having been described over and over again since at least the early 19th century.
But exactly how common is multiple invention? The frequency of examples suggests that it can’t be particularly rare, but that doesn’t tell us the rate at which it occurs. In “
How Common is Independent Discovery?
,” Matt Clancy catalogues several attempts to estimate the frequency of multiple discovery, and tentatively comes up with a frequency of around 2-3% for simultaneous scientific discoveries, and perhaps an 8% chance that a given invention will be reinvented in the next decade. But the evidence for inventions is somewhat inconsistent, and varies greatly between studies. Clancy estimates a reinvention rate of around 8% per decade, but
another study
he found that looked at patent interference lawsuits between 1998 and 2014 suggests an independent invention rate of only around 0.02% per year.
The frequency of multiple invention is a useful thing to know, because it can give us clues about the nature of technological progress. A very low rate of multiple invention suggests that progress might be driven by a small number of “genius” inventors (what we might call the
Great Man Theory
of technological progress), and that it might be highly historically contingent (if you re-rolled the dice of history, maybe you get a totally new set of inventions and a different technological palette). A high rate of multiple invention suggests that progress is more a function of broad historical forces (that inventions appear when the conditions are right), and that progress is less contingent (if you re-rolled the dice of history, you’d get a similar progression of inventions). And if the rate of multiple invention is changing over time, perhaps the nature of technological progress is changing as well.
I wanted to create my own estimate of the rate of multiple invention, so I started with Wikipedia’s
Timeline of historic inventions
, which lists "nonincremental inventions that are widely recognized by reliable sources as having had a direct impact on the course of history that was profound, global, and enduring.” I narrowed this list down to inventions between 1800 and 1970, both to trim the list to a manageable number, and to restrict it to inventions where I could expect a decent amount of available documentation (earlier efforts may have more gaps in the history, and more recent efforts may not have had time to get the historian’s treatment). This yielded a list of around 190 inventions. For each one, I looked to see whether the invention had multiple inventors.
This required specifying what exactly we mean by “multiple.” I ended up using three different categories of multiple invention.
First, there may be multiple
descriptions
of the same basic idea. When Bell Labs went to file a patent for the transistor in 1948, it was discovered that physicist
Julius Lillienfeld
had filed a patent for a similar idea in 1926. Lillienfeld likely never actually built his transistor (it would have almost certainly been impossible to build a working one due to material limitations), but he nevertheless described the concept. Similarly, concepts for
airships
were described many years before a working one was built. I counted these descriptions as multiple inventions only if the description included a basic functional mechanism that could have plausibly worked: So Lillienfeld’s patent counts as a multiple invention, but someone idly stating that “it would be great if there was a solid state amplifier” wouldn’t. • **材料科学与时机**：dlcarrier强调发明是否可行取决于材料科学的发展。Lillienfeld虽然描述了晶体管的概念，但受限于材料科学，未能实现。发明的实现需要时机，当科学条件成熟时，多重独立发明会几乎同时出现。
• **社会与科技发展的必然性**：paulorlando引用了Charles Fort的观点，认为科技发展如同植物生长，有其必然性。社会和技术发展到一定阶段，某些发明就会自然而然地出现，不依赖于个别人的灵感或努力。
• **形态共振理论**：myflash13介绍了形态共振理论，认为想法如同无线电波存在于环境中，不同的人可能同时接收到相同的想法，导致多重独立发明的出现。该理论还提出了一些实验证据支持这一观点。
• **历史与偶然性**：theendisney和ryao提到历史上多次出现多人几乎同时发明相同技术的情况，如望远镜和快速傅里叶变换（FFT）。这些例子显示了历史中的偶然性和竞争性。

补充讨论：
• **执行力与历史书写**：chvid和raymondgh提到，在“大创意”上，多人竞争或互相借鉴是很常见的。历史往往由胜利者书写，影响了发明的归属。执行力和时机对发明能否成功进入市场至关重要。
• **多重发现的统计**：david-gpu引用文章数据，指出独立发现的现象虽然不普遍（约2-3%的科学发现和8%的发明），但确实存在。
• **有趣的巧合**：ljsprague和somat提到一些有趣的历史巧合，如Rubik's Cube的独立发明和铝 refinement过程的独立同时发现，增加了讨论的趣味性和复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 灵感和资源对发明的重要性：milliams和Animats的观点代表了两种极端，一个强调灵感，另一个强调系统性实验和资源支持。
• 历史书写的公正性：chvid认为历史往往由胜利者书写，影响了发明的实际归属和认知。

data.title: I made a search engine worse than Elasticsearch (2024)
data.author: softwaredoug
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者尝试用自制的搜索库 *SearchArray* 与 *Elasticsearch* 在信息检索基准 *BEIR* 上进行性能对比，结果 *SearchArray* 在相关性（NDCG@10）和性能（查询与索引吞吐量）上均不如 *Elasticsearch*。作者深入分析了原因，指出像 *Elasticsearch* 这样的成熟搜索引擎使用了诸如 *WAND*（弱AND）等优化算法，能快速筛选出高分文档，避免不必要的计算。而 *SearchArray* 则是简单地对所有文档进行 BM25 评分并直接求和，导致性能低下。此外，*SearchArray* 使用位置索引和位图来处理短语匹配，而非传统倒排索引，这也影响了其效率。文章最终揭示了成熟搜索引擎在处理大规模数据时的优化技巧和高效性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对搜索功能和搜索引擎工具（如ElasticSearch等）的评价和使用体验

不同观点：
• [sh34r] 认为改进网站的搜索功能需要很长时间，且自制的搜索引擎几乎肯定不如ElasticSearch。他们强调了搜索问题的复杂性和ElasticSearch的优势。
• [intalentive] 提出在特定情况下，可以优化自制的搜索引擎，并给出了一些技术细节，如不需要通过长度或频率进行归一化处理，以及使用NLP提取关键词。
• [nchmy] 推荐Manticoresearch，认为它比ElasticSearch更容易使用且速度更快，并提到其历史和在Craigslist等网站上的应用。
• [fucalost] 支持使用Elasticsearch，认为其功能强大且生态系统健康，特别是在生产环境中，AWS的新实例类型可以显著节省成本。
• [0xB0UNCE00] 认为即使自制的搜索引擎不如Elasticsearch，但通过尝试和学习是有价值的。

补充讨论：
• [Alifatisk] 表示对Elasticsearch的存在感到感激。
• [niazangels] 感谢了评论提供的知识。
• [neuroelectron] 夸张地表示该讨论内容价值极高。
• [stuaxo] 表示不喜欢使用Elasticsearch，并认为在一些项目中使用ES是不必要的。

争议焦点：
• 自制搜索引擎是否值得以及是否能优于现有工具（如ElasticSearch）存在不同看法。一些评论认为特定情况下可以优化自制引擎，而多数人认为ElasticSearch已经非常强大和高效。

总结：讨论围绕搜索功能实现的难度、ElasticSearch的优劣以及其他替代工具的推荐，参与者分享了各自的技术见解和使用体验。

44194468.article_content:
I want you to share in my shame at daring to make a search library. And in this shame, you too, can experience the humility and understanding of what a real, honest-to-goodness, not side-project, search engine does to make lexical search fast.
BEIR
is a set of Information Retrieval benchmarks, oriented around question-answer use cases.
My side project,
SearchArray
adds full text search to Pandas. So naturally, to see stand in awe at my amazing developer skills, I wanted to use BEIR to compare SearchArray to Elasticsearch (w/ same query + tokenization). So I spent a Saturday integrating SearchArray into BEIR, and measuring its relevence and performance on MSMarco Passage Retrieval corpus (8M docs).
… and 🥁
Library
Elasticsearch
SearchArray
NDCG@10
0.2275
0.225
Search Throughput
90 QPS
~18 QPS
Indexing Throughput
10K Docs Per Sec
~3.5K Docs Per Sec
… Sad trombone 🎺
It’s worse in every dimension
At least
NDCG@10
is nearly right, so our BM25 calculation is correct (probably due to negligible differences in tokenization)
Imposter Syndrome anyone?
Instead of wallowing in my shame, I DO know exactly what’s going on… And it’s fairly educational. Let’s chat about why a
real
, non side-project, search engine is fast.
A Magic WAND
(Or how SearchArray is top 8m retrieval while Elasticsearch == top K retrieval)
In lexical search systems, you search for multiple terms. You take the
BM25
score of each term, and then finally, combine those into a final score for the document. IE, a search for
luke skywalker
really means:
BM25(luke) ??? BM25(skywalker)
where ??? is some mathematical operator.
In a simple “OR” query, you just take the SUM of each term for each doc, IE, a search for
luke skywalker
is
BM25(luke) + BM25(skywalker)
like so:
Term
Doc A (BM25)
Doc B (BM25)
luke
1.90
1.45
skywalker
11.51
4.3
Combined doc score  (SUM)
13.41
5.75
SearchArray just does BM25 scoring. You get back big numpy arrays of
every document
’s BM25 score. Then you combine the scores – literally using
np.sum
. Of course, that’s not what a search engine like Elasticsearch would do. Instead it has a different guarantee, it gets
the highest scoring top N
of your specified OR query.
This little bit of seemingly minute wiggle room gives search engines a great deal of latitude. Search engines can use an algorithm called
Weak-AND or WAND
to avoid work when combining multiple term scores into the final top N results.
I won’t get into the full nitty gritty of the algorithm, but here’s a key intuition to noodle over:
A scoring system like BM25 depends heavily on document frequency of a term. So rare terms - a high (1 / document frequency) - have a higher likelihood of impacting the final score, and ending up in the top K. Luckily these terms (like
skywalker
) occur on fewer documents. So we can fetch these select, elite few docs quickly in the data structure that maps
skywalker -> [... handful of matching doc ids...]
(aka postings). We can reach deeply into this list.
On the other hand, we can be much more circumspect about the boring, common term,
luke
. And that’s useful because
luke
has a very extensive postings list
luke -> [... a giant honking list of documents...]
. We’d prefer to avoid scanning all of these.
We might imagine that these lists of document ids, also is paired with its
term frequency
how often that term occurs in that document - the other major input of BM25. And if its SORTED from highest -> lowest term frequency, we can go down this list until its impossible for the BM25 score of a term to have any chance of making the top K results. Then exit early.
While WAND - and similar optimizations - helps Elasticsearch avoid work, SearchArray, gleefully does this work like an ignoramus happily giving you a giant idiotic array of BM25 scores.
When you look at this icicle graph of SearchArray’s performance doing an “OR” search, you can see all the time spent
summing
a giant array and also needlessly BM25 scoring many many documents.
SearchArray doesn’t directly store postings
Unlike most search engines, SearchArray doesn’t have postings lists of terms -> documents.
Instead, under the hood, SearchArray stores a positional index, built first-and-foremost for
phrase matching
. You give SearchArray a list of terms
['mary', 'had', 'a', 'little', 'lamb']
. It then finds every place
mary
occurs one position before
had
, etc. It does this by storing, for each terms, the positions as a
roaring bitmap
.
In our roaring bitmap, each 64 bit word has a header indicating where the positions occur (document and region in the doc). Each bit position corresponds to a position in the document. A 1 indicates this term is present, a 0 missing.
So to collect phrase matches, for
mary had
we can simply find places where one term’s bits occur adjacent to another. This can be done very fast with simple bit arithmetic.
mary
<Roaring Headers (doc id, etc)>  00000010000000    | 00000000000010
had
<Roaring Headers (doc id, etc)>  00000001000000    | 00000000000001      #< Le

data.title: Defending adverbs exuberantly if conditionally
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于写作中使用副词的建议及其有效性

不同观点：
• **支持副词的使用**：[mcv] 认为副词是语言的有效组成部分，如果使用得当，可以非常有效。比如 "angrily" 比 "trembling, red in the face" 更清晰地传达了心理状态。
• **反对僵化的规则**：[topaz0] 指出基于语法结构的写作建议无法替代个人的品味，品味需要通过多年阅读各种散文来培养。虽然新手作家常常滥用副词，但解决方案不是完全避免副词，而是通过仔细阅读和修改来提高写作质量。
• **强调努力和修改**：[SoftTalker] 主张写作时不应懒惰，每个句子都应付出努力。规则只是建议，可以接受或拒绝，关键是要不断重写和修改。
• **副词的节奏感**：[Charon77] 认为副词可以增加句子的节奏感，比如 "She grins happily" 比 "She grins" 更符合某些上下文需求，且不一定是不好的写法。

补充讨论：
• **副词的幽默用法**：[Bjartr] 提到 "Tom Swifty" 这种以副词为基础的双关语，展示了副词在特定语境下的幽默效果，但也暗示了副词可能被滥用。
• **美式英语中的副词省略**：[gadders] 注意到许多美式英语使用者会省略副词的 "ly" 后缀，并质疑这是否符合语法规范。
• **对副词建议的反讽**：[ofalkaed] 和 [tempodox] 以讽刺的口吻表达了对“避免使用副词”这一建议的无奈或调侃。
• **对标题的幽默回应**：[throwanem] 和 [elbear] 以幽默的方式回应了讨论的标题，表现出对副词讨论的轻松态度。

争议焦点：
• **副词使用的必要性和有效性**：一些评论者（如 [mcv] 和 [Charon77]）认为副词在传达意义和节奏上有其独特价值，而另一些人（如 [topaz0] 和 [SoftTalker]）则强调应通过品味和努力修改来避免副词的滥用。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **副词在不同写作风格中的角色**：讨论中涉及了副词在不同写作风格和语境中的不同作用，以及如何根据具体需求决定是否使用副词。
• **语法规范与语言变体**：[gadders] 提出了美式英语中副词省略现象的语法正确性问题，扩展了讨论的范围。

data.title: How much energy does it take to think?
data.author: nsoonhui
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了大脑在思考时的能量消耗。研究显示，尽管我们在进行专注的认知任务时感觉耗费大量精力，但实际上这些任务只比休息时多消耗约5%的能量。大脑的大部分能量用于维持生理系统的平衡，而非纯粹的认知功能。进化塑造了大脑的这种能量分配模式，以保存资源。大脑仅占身体重量的2%，却消耗约20%的能量，婴儿更是高达50%。ATP（三磷酸腺苷）是大脑能量的主要来源，通过葡萄糖和氧气生成，维持神经元间的通讯和膜电位。虽然直接测量人脑ATP消耗非常侵入性，但通过PET扫描和功能磁共振成像等方法可以间接估算能量使用。文章指出，大脑不仅是思考工具，更是复杂的生物系统，受进化限制和资源管理需求的制约。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大脑疲劳、能量消耗与思考效率之间的关系

不同观点：
• **mellow_observer** 认为现代高能量环境可能为解决大脑疲劳提供了机会，并提出如果能克服疲劳问题，将极大提高生活质量。虽然能量供应不是导致疲劳的唯一原因，但该话题受到的关注太少。
• **nameless_me** 指出，大脑需要通过休息或睡眠来排出废物，因此休息是必要的，隐含对"完全消除疲劳"可能性的质疑。
• **pmayrgundter** 提供了数据支持，指出大脑的能量消耗仅比基础代谢率略高，思考所消耗的能量相对较小，暗示思考并不是大脑能量消耗的主要因素。
• **teleforce** 强调大脑占身体质量的2%却消耗20-25%的能量，指出讨论中忽视了线粒体的重要性，认为这是理解能量消耗的关键。
• **gleenn** 通过个人经历说明高强度思考确实会导致更快的能量消耗，即使是在无糖饮料情况下，身体依然渴望糖分补充能量。
• **jonplackett** 提出在高压下感受到的时间膨胀是否与神经元最大化发射频率有关，暗示大脑在极限情况下的运作机制可能与日常状态不同。
• **Perz1val** 半开玩笑地询问是否可以通过药物将神经元发射频率从4Hz提升到100Hz，认为即使增加能量消耗，也能通过食物补充。
• **chvid** 质疑“思考”的定义，认为社会互动等复杂任务对大脑的负荷远高于简单任务，因此思考的能量消耗不能一概而论。

- 讨论中多次提到能量消耗的具体数据和生理机制，如线粒体和神经元发射频率，显示出对大脑能量消耗细节的关注。
- 争议焦点在于是否有可能通过外部手段克服大脑疲劳以及思考对大脑能量消耗的真实影响。一些观点认为高强度思考确实消耗更多能量，而另一些观点则强调大脑的基础代谢已经占据了大部分能量消耗。
- 对思考的定义和不同类型的思考对能量消耗的影响也有不同看法，尤其是社会互动与单纯任务之间的对比。

Studies of neural metabolism reveal our brain’s effort to keep us alive and the evolutionary constraints that sculpted our most complex organ.

You’ve just gotten home from an exhausting day. All you want to do is put your feet up and zone out to whatever is on television. Though the inactivity may feel like a well-earned rest, your brain is not just chilling. In fact, it is using nearly as much energy as it did during your stressful activity, according to recent research.
Sharna Jamadar
, a neuroscientist at Monash University in Australia, and her colleagues reviewed research from her lab and others around the world to estimate the
metabolic cost of cognition
— that is, how much energy it takes to power the human brain. Surprisingly, they concluded that effortful, goal-directed tasks use only 5% more energy than restful brain activity. In other words, we use our brain just a small fraction more when engaging in focused cognition than when the engine is idling.
It often feels as though we allocate our mental energy through strenuous attention and focus. But the new research builds on a growing understanding that the majority of the brain’s function goes to maintenance. While many neuroscientists have historically focused on active, outward cognition, such as attention, problem-solving, working memory and decision-making, it’s becoming clear that beneath the surface, our background processing is a hidden hive of activity. Our brains regulate our bodies’ key physiological systems, allocating resources where they’re needed as we consciously and subconsciously react to the demands of our ever-changing environments.
“There is this sentiment that the brain is for thinking,” said
Jordan Theriault
, a neuroscientist at Northeastern University who was not involved in the new analysis. “Where, metabolically, [the brain’s function is] mostly spent on managing your body, regulating and coordinating between organs, managing this expensive system which it’s attached to, and navigating a complicated external environment.”

The neuroscientist Sharna Jamadar compiled data from simultaneous MRI and PET imaging to estimate the brain’s energy use.
Emma Liang
The brain is not purely a cognition machine, but an object sculpted by evolution — and therefore constrained by the tight energy budget of a biological system. Thinking may make you feel tired, then, not because you are out of energy, but because you have evolved to preserve resources. This study of neural metabolism, when tied to research on the dynamics of the brain’s electrical firing, points to the competing evolutionary forces that explain the limitations, scope and efficiencies of our cognitive capabilities.
The Cost of a Predictive Engine
The human brain is incredibly expensive to run. At roughly 2% of body weight, the organ gorges on 20% of our body’s energetic resources. “It’s hugely metabolically demanding,” Jamadar said. For infants, that number is closer to 50%.
The brain is not purely a cognition machine, but an object sculpted by evolution.
The brain’s energy comes in the form of the molecule adenosine triphosphate (ATP), which cells make from glucose and oxygen. A tremendous expanse of thin capillaries — an estimated 400 miles of vascular wiring — weaves through brain tissue to carry glucose- and oxygen-rich blood to neurons and other brain cells. Once synthesized within cells, ATP powers communication between neurons, which enact the brain’s functions. Neurons carry electrical signals to their synapses, which allow the cells to exchange molecular messages; the strength of a signal determines whether they will release molecules (or “fire”). If they do, that molecular signal determines whether the next neuron will pass on the message, and so on. Maintaining what are known as membrane potentials — stable voltages across a neuron’s membrane that ensure that the cell is primed to fire when called upon — is known to account for at least half of the brain’s total energy budget.

data.title: Czech Republic: Petition for open source in public administration
data.author: harvie
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了一份关于公共事务门户网站用户满意度的调查问卷。主要问题包括：

1. 用户如何得知该门户网站（通过电视、互联网、亲友、政府机构或其他途径）。
2. 访问网站的目的（获取公共事务信息、好奇浏览或其他原因）。
3. 用户对网站外观、页面清晰度、信息易懂性和信息实用性的评价。
4. 用户使用网站的频率（每日、每周、每月或更少）。
5. 用户是否计划未来继续使用该网站，若不使用，请说明原因。

问卷最后提供了提交、推迟或不再显示选项。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：政府使用开源软件和开放格式的可行性及其实际执行中的问题

不同观点：
• Vox_Leone认为，尽管巴西有相关立法要求使用开源软件，但像巴西央行开发的重要支付服务Pix的代码并未公开，表明仅有法律是不够的。
• Tajnymag支持该倡议，但对请愿能否达到目标持怀疑态度，认为由于公共部门的腐败，政府软件合同的透明度难以实现，公开代码会暴露过度昂贵和拖延的项目。
• belval认为LibreOffice的主要问题在于品牌和界面设计，而不是功能。如果其界面能现代化，像Office 365那样，用户的接受度可能会提高。
• mikece质疑是否有政府功能是Linux或LibreOffice无法完成的，暗示这些软件应能满足政府需求。
• xigoi关注如何参与请愿，作为一个捷克人，询问如何签署请愿。
• fside支持使用开源软件以节省纳税人的钱，但担心某些系统可能成为维护上的噩梦。
• dismalaf以加拿大政府的例子说明使用专有软件和格式的不便，主张至少应使用开放格式以节省成本，并建议雇佣本地开发者。
• fsflover提供了一个关于公共代码的链接，供进一步参考。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了开源软件在政府应用中的技术、经济和透明度问题。
• 有人担心政府部门的腐败和项目管理的低效会阻碍开源软件的实施。
• 界面设计和用户体验被认为是影响开源软件普及的重要因素。
• 不同国家的用户对如何参与和推动此类倡议表示关注。
• 讨论还涉及具体的技术问题，如某些政府表格只能用特定软件打开，给用户带来不便。

data.title: Jepsen: TigerBeetle 0.16.11
data.author: aphyr
data.article_summary:
TigerBeetle是一个专注于安全和速度的在线事务处理（OLTP）数据库，专为双重记账设计。它基于Viewstamped Replication（VR）共识协议，提供强序列化一致性。该数据库仅存储账户及账户间的转账信息，适用于金融交易、库存管理和票务等场景。TigerBeetle优化了高竞争和高吞吐量的工作负载，如中央银行交易和经纪结算。它通过单核处理写入操作，并利用批处理、IO并行化等技术提升性能。

TigerBeetle非常强调容错性，提供了针对内存、进程、时钟、存储和网络故障的明确模型。通过Viewstamped Replication和协议感知恢复技术，它能在单个副本保留记录的情况下继续运行，防止数据丢失。TigerBeetle采用确定性模拟测试来验证故障安全性，并支持无缝的二进制升级，无需人工干预。

此外，TigerBeetle定义了明确的时间模型，使用物理时间戳并确保其严格单调递增。当集群时钟不同步超过一定时间窗口时，系统将拒绝请求以保证一致性。

44199592.article_content:
1
Background
TigerBeetle is an
Online Transactional Processing (OLTP)
database built for double-entry accounting with a strong emphasis on safety and speed. It builds on the
Viewstamped Replication (VR)
consensus protocol to offer
Strong Serializable
consistency. Unlike general-purpose databases, TigerBeetle stores only accounts and transfers between them. This data model is well-suited for financial transactions, inventory, ticketing, or utility metering. To store other kinds of information, users typically pair TigerBeetle with other databases, linking them through user-defined identifiers.
TigerBeetle optimizes for
high-contention and high-throughput workloads
, such as central bank switches or brokerages. A central bank exchange might have only a half-dozen to a few hundred account recordsâone for each partner bankâand process
hundreds of millions
of
transactions per day
between 647 banks. A large brokerage, after the trading day closes, might need to settle the entire dayâs trades as quickly as possible.
1
These trades also tend to be concentrated on a small number of popular stocks. Under high contention, per-object concurrency control mechanisms can be the limiting factor in throughput. Instead, TigerBeetle funnels all writes through
a single core on the primary VR node
. This limits throughput to whatever a single node can execute: TigerBeetle is firmly scale-up, not scale-out. To make that single node as fast as possible, TigerBeetle makes extensive use of batching, IO parallelization, a fixed schema, and hardware-friendly optimizationsâsuch as fixed-size, cache-aligned data structures.
Refreshingly, TigerBeetle stresses fault tolerance in their marketing and documentation. They offer
explicit models
for memory, process, clock, storage, and network faults. ECC RAM is assumed to be correct. Processes may pause or crash. Clocks may jump forward and backward in time. Disks are assumed to not only fail completely, but to tear individual writes or corrupt data. Networks may delay, drop, duplicate, misdirect, and corrupt messages. To mitigate these faults, TigerBeetle combines Viewstamped Replication with techniques from
Protocol-Aware Recovery
, uses extensive checksums stored separately from data blocks, and for critical data, writes and reads multiple copies. TigerBeetle also makes extensive use of runtime correctness assertions to identify and limit the damage from faults and bugs alike.
Unlike most distributed systems, TigerBeetle claims to keep running without data loss
if even a single replica retains a copy
of a record:
A record would need to get corrupted on all replicas in a cluster to get lost, and even in that case the system would safely halt.
To test safety under faults, TigerBeetle employs
deterministic simulation testing
: tests which perform reproducible, pseudo-random operations against the system and ensure that some property holds.
2
The
Viewstamped Operation Replicator (VOPR)
test simulates an entire TigerBeetle cluster, including clock, disk, and network interfaces. It simulates clock skew, corrupts reads and writes, loses and reorders network messages, and so on. There are other simulation tests which stress specific subsystems, as well as
a variety of more traditional integration and unit tests
.
TigerBeetle also offers a noteworthy approach to upgrades. Each TigerBeetle binary includes the code not just for that particular version, but several previous versions. For example, the 0.16.21 binary can run 0.16.17, 0.16.18, and so on through 0.16.21. To upgrade, one simply
replaces the binary on disk
. TigerBeetle loads the new binary, but continues running with the current version. It then coordinates across the cluster to smoothly roll out each successive version, until all nodes are running the latest version available. This approach does not require operators to carefully sequence the upgrade process. Instead, upgrades are performed automatically, and coupled to the replicated state machine. This also allows TigerBeetle to ensure that an operation which commits on version
x
will never commit on any other versionâguarding against state divergence.
1.1
Time
TigerBeetle defines an
explicit model of time
. Viewstamped Replication forms a totally ordered sequence of state transitions, and its view and op numbers can be used as a totally ordered logical clock. Financial systems usually prefer wall clocks, so most TigerBeetle timestamps are in âphysical time,â which, like
Hybrid Logical Clocks
, approximate POSIX time with stronger ordering guarantees. Specifically, TigerBeetle leaders
collect POSIX timestamps
from all replicas
3
and try to find a time which falls within a reasonable margin of error across a quorum of nodes.
4
Those timestamps are incorporated into the VR-replicated state machine, and constrained to be strictly monotonic. When no quorum of clocks falls within a
twenty-second window
for longer than sixty seconds, the cluster refuses requests until clocks com
44199592.article_summary:
TigerBeetle是一个专注于安全和速度的在线事务处理（OLTP）数据库，专为双重记账设计。它基于Viewstamped Replication（VR）共识协议，提供强序列化一致性。该数据库仅存储账户及账户间的转账信息，适用于金融交易、库存管理和票务等场景。TigerBeetle优化了高竞争和高吞吐量的工作负载，如中央银行交易和经纪结算。它通过单核处理写入操作，并利用批处理、IO并行化等技术提升性能。

TigerBeetle非常强调容错性，提供了针对内存、进程、时钟、存储和网络故障的明确模型。通过Viewstamped Replication和协议感知恢复技术，它能在单个副本保留记录的情况下继续运行，防止数据丢失。TigerBeetle采用确定性模拟测试来验证故障安全性，并支持无缝的二进制升级，无需人工干预。

此外，TigerBeetle定义了明确的时间模型，使用物理时间戳并确保其严格单调递增。当集群时钟不同步超过一定时间窗口时，系统将拒绝请求以保证一致性。

data.article_summary: Dreamstar是一家由Joshua Dominic和Thomas Eastmond创立的私人铁路创业公司，计划重现1940年代洛杉矶和旧金山之间豪华过夜列车的魅力。该公司设想提供中等距离的高端卧铺列车服务，包括全卧室设施、车上美食和五星级酒店服务。Dreamstar计划使用Southern Pacific的Lark路线，并与Union Pacific签署了轨道使用协议。列车将尽量减少停靠站点，以确保乘客的连续休息，同时减少碳排放。车厢将包括四种不同级别的私人舱室，并提供餐饮、休息室和水疗等设施。虽然具体定价尚未确定，但公司目标是与航班加酒店、Amtrak类似服务的费用竞争。Dreamstar计划在2028年洛杉矶奥运会前开始运营，目前正与多家供应商和监管机构合作推进项目。

• [kylehotchkiss] 分享了自己乘坐海岸星光号的积极体验，并希望LA到SF有更多的列车选择，尤其希望改善互联网服务。

• [zokier] 指出LA到SF的距离相对较短，不适合过夜火车服务，并将其与欧洲类似距离的高速铁路服务进行比较。

• [fblp] 建议推出一种白天运行的火车，提供带桌子的座位以支持工作，不需要卧铺空间，特别适合3-4小时的行程。

• [paxys] 认为LA-SF过夜火车的成功取决于时间和价格的竞争力，需确保乘客能获得完整的睡眠，且价格需与航班或自驾竞争。

• [tristanb] 表达了对恢复从前SF到Sugarbowl滑雪火车的愿望。

• [ramesh31] 查找了海岸星光号的票价，指出其往返票价昂贵，不如选择私人司机或航班更经济。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于美国城际铁路基础设施是否支持可靠的过夜服务，以及过夜火车服务的经济性和市场需求。
- 有人对奢华火车服务持怀疑态度，认为其经济性不强，而有人则基于个人经历支持过夜火车的便利性和舒适性。
- 不同国家和地区的火车服务对比也为讨论提供了重要论据，尤其是欧洲和美国之间的差异。

44199005.article_content:
Can a passenger rail startup bring back the glamour of luxury overnight trains connecting Los Angeles and San Francisco that haven’t been seen since the 1940s?
Co-founders Joshua Dominic and Thomas Eastmond think so — and there’s a connection to freight rail at the heart of their proposal.
Dreamstar is a private venture reimagining medium-length passenger service in a setting that harks back to the heyday of first-class trains with all-bedroom accommodations, onboard gourmet dining and five-star hotel hospitality.
“Dreamstar started from a deeply personal frustration with the state of American travel,” said Dominic, in an interview. “After experiencing modern rail across Europe and Asia in my 20s, I kept asking, ‘Why don’t we have this in the U.S.?’ Years later, after hundreds of business and leisure trips that forced a choice between wasting precious daytime or sacrificing sleep, the idea crystallized: Build a better alternative. Dreamstar is our answer — a rail service that brings rest, reliability and elegance to medium-distance travel.”
The Southern Pacific’s Lark was the last domestic all-sleeper train to run exclusively in one state, operating two daily trains between San Francisco and LA. Espee added coaches after the Second World War; Amtrak’s all-sleeper California Zephyr ended service between Chicago and Emeryville, California, in 1997.
Dreamstar plans to run over much of the Lark’s route, having signed a memorandum of agreement for track access with Union Pacific, which merged with SP in 1996. That includes 400 miles between San Jose and Ventura, which the partners say has minimal overnight freight and passenger traffic.
Southbound Southern Pacific No. 76, the Lark, on Santa Susana Pass near Chatsworth, Calif., on Oct. 14, 1950. (Photo: William D. Middleton)
Union Pacific (NYSE:
UNP
) in a statement confirmed that it is in formal negotiations with Dreamstar but offered no details.
Freight tracks are an essential component of the original proposal, like another recent passenger train startup, Brightline, which started out running on the tracks of sister company Florida East Coast Railway.
Dominic said Dreamstar is working on access agreements with commuter agencies Caltrain and Metrolink, as well as the agency that manages Los Angeles Union Passenger Terminal.
“The flagship route is designed as an overnight, limited-stop service optimized for uninterrupted rest,” said Dominic. “We aim to keep stops to a minimum while ensuring operational viability and regional access.”
The startup also claims its trains will reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 75% compared to flying.
While pricing specifics are still being. worked on, Dominic said Dreamstar would be competitive with a flight-plus-hotel, last minute flight/business class flight, flying a family of four, and what Amtrak is currently charging for similar accommodations. Tickets will be sold online, similar to hotel and flight bookings.
Conceptual renderings emulate the proportions and outlines of contemporary passenger equipment. The cars follow the profile of the original Budd Hi-Level cars of Santa Fe’s El Capitan,
an all-coach train running between Los Angeles and Chicago, that were passed on to Amtrak and eventually replaced by the bilevel Superliners, also manufactured by Budd, which included sleeping accommodations.
There are four classes of accommodations — called private cabins — including standard, bedroom, stateroom and family room sleeping six, as well as lounges, dining spaces and a spa.
Rendering of Dreamstar stateroom. (Photo: Dreamstar)
The renderings also depict Dreamstar’s Auto Ferry, car transporters similar to those of Amtrak’s Auto Train.
Dreamstar’s original proposal in 2018 called for construction of an all-new train. Now, the company plans to rebuild four previously owned cars.
“We’ve completed the concept development phase in partnership with BMW Designworks,” Dominic said. “The next step is further refinement and engineering drawings. We’ve identified a handful of potential suppliers and are evaluating next steps.”
The Los Angeles design studio has worked with aircraft maker Embraer, John Deere and Singapore Airlines, among many other clients.
Construction of rolling stock is expected to take 18 to 24 months, with service to begin prior to the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.
A locomotive supplier has yet to be selected, “but we’ve identified several viable options that align with our performance and emissions goals. We’ve reviewed a few promising options and are continuing to explore the right partners for both operations and maintenance.”
The company said location planning is underway for maintenance facilities in parallel with operational modeling.
Dominic said Dreamstar is working with industry experts to smooth the way through regulatory approval processes.
At the same time, California homebuilder Bill Lyon has dropped $100,000 on Dreamstar.

• [ramesh31] 查找了海岸星光号的票价，指出其往返票价昂贵，不如选择私人司机或航班更经济。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于美国城际铁路基础设施是否支持可靠的过夜服务，以及过夜火车服务的经济性和市场需求。
- 有人对奢华火车服务持怀疑态度，认为其经济性不强，而有人则基于个人经历支持过夜火车的便利性和舒适性。
- 不同国家和地区的火车服务对比也为讨论提供了重要论据，尤其是欧洲和美国之间的差异。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了AMD Radeon 8050S "Strix Halo" 图形处理器在Linux系统上的性能表现。Radeon 8050S集成在Ryzen AI Max PRO 390中，相比旗舰型号Radeon 8060S（集成于Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395）略有缩减，拥有32个图形核心和2.8GHz频率。尽管性能稍逊于8060S，但仍远超Radeon 890M和英特尔的集成显卡。测试在Ubuntu 25.04上进行，使用Linux 6.14内核和Mesa 25.0。结果显示，Radeon 8050S在默认、低功耗和高性能模式下均表现稳定，能够支持高达8K@60Hz的显示输出。文中还对比了其他多款笔记本和SoC的集成显卡性能，全面展示了Radeon 8050S的图形能力。

AMD Radeon 8050S "Strix Halo" Linux Graphics Performance
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Graphics Cards
on 5 June 2025 at 06:31 AM EDT.
Page 1 of 8
.
14 Comments
.
Last month I began the much anticipated AMD
Strix Halo
Linux benchmarking at Phoronix by testing the top-end
Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395
that features 16 cores / 32 threads and the very impressive
Radeon 8060S
integrated graphics. Coming in one step below that flagship Strix Halo SoC is the Ryzen AI Max (PRO) 390 with Radeon 8050S graphics. Coming out today on Phoronix - coincidentally timed for
the 21st birthday of Phoronix.com
-  is the first
benchmarks of the Ryzen AI Max PRO 390
along with the Radeon 8050S graphics.
This article is focused on providing an initial look at the Radeon 8050S Strix Halo graphics performance under Linux while
a separate article is looking at the Ryzen AI Max PRO 390 CPU performance
found within the HP ZBook Ultra G1a, the same laptop series as used for the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395 testing the past few weeks.
The Radeon 8050S Graphics found with the Ryzen AI Max 390 and Ryzen AI Max 385 is slightly cut-down from the flagship 395 tier with the Radeon 8060S. The Radeon 8050S Graphics feature 32 graphics cores and a 2.8GHz frequency while the Radeon 8060S Graphics have 40 graphics cores with a 2.9GHz clock speed. While having a 100MHz lower graphics clock and just 80% the CUs, the Radeon 8050S is still a large step-up from the Radeon 890M graphics found with the Ryzen AI 300 "Strix Point" SoCs that feature just 16 graphics cores. Basically the Radeon 8050S has double the graphics cores as the Radeon 890M.
Like the Radeon 8060S, the Radeon 8050S is capable of driving up to 8K @ 60 displays, 4K @ 240Hz, 1080p @ 600Hz, and supports DisplayPort 2.1 and can handle up to four displays simultaneously. Adaptive-Sync and HDR support, of course, remain available too.
So with the Radeon 8050S Graphics on the Ryzen AI Max 385/390 you are a step below the Radeon 8060S but still much more capable than what is found with the likes of the Radeon 880M/890M integrated graphics or from the Intel Xe/Xe2 integrated graphics competition from Intel.
The AMD Radeon 8050S Graphics were working out-of-the-box on Ubuntu 25.04 and Fedora 42 just like with the Radeon 8060S Graphics. Of course, moving to Mesa 25.1 or even Mesa 25.2-devel can yield more performance and especially additional Vulkan features, but Mesa 25.0 is good enough for out-of-the-box on the likes of Ubuntu 25.04. With both the Radeon 8050S and 8060S graphics I haven't encountered any display issues, GPU hangs, anything along those lines. It's rather pleasant how well the open-source AMD graphics experience is now at launch or shortly thereafter.
For this AMD Radeon 8050S Graphics benchmarking article, there are tests of the Ryzen AI Max PRO 390 up against the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395 (Radeon 8060S), Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (Radeon 890M), and Core Ultra 7 256V (Lunar Lake Xe2) for the current top-end integrated graphics experiences from both Intel and AMD. Following that is a more diverse set of integrated graphics Linux benchmarks from a broader range of laptops/SoCs for seeing a more comprehensive look at the Radeon 8050S Graphics but due to going to the older/slower hardware that set of tests is more refined and less taxing than the benchmarks looking just at the current-gen top-end offerings.
The complete set of laptops and CPUs/iGPUs tested included:
- Core i7 8550U - Dell XPS 9370
- Core i7 8565U - Dell XPS 9380
- Core i7 1065G7 - Dell XPS 7390
- Core i7 1165G7 - Dell XPS 9310
- Core i7 1185G7 - Dell XPS 9310
- Core i7 1280P - MSI Prestige 14Evo
- Core Ultra 7 155H - Acer Swift Go 14
- Core Ultra 7 256V - ASUS Zenbook S14
- Core Ultra 7 258V - X1 Carbon G13
- Ryzen 7 4700U - Lenovo IdeaPad 5
- Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U - ThinkPad T14s G2a
- Ryzen 7 PRO 6850U - ThinkPad X13 G3
- Ryzen 7 7840U - Framework 13
- Ryzen 7 PRO 7840U - ThinkPad P14s G4
- Ryzen 7 7840U - Acer Swift Edge 16
- Ryzen 7 7840HS - Framework 16
- Ryzen AI 7 PRO 360 - ThinkPad T14s G6
- Ryzen AI 9 365 - ASUS Zenbook S16
- Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 - ASUS Zenbook S16
- Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 - Framework 13
- Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 395 - HP ZBook Ultra G1a
- Ryzen AI Max PRO 390 - HP ZBook Ultra G1a
- Ryzen AI Max PRO 390 - HP ZBook Ultra G1a - low-power
- Ryzen AI Max PRO 390 - HP ZBook Ultra G1a - performance
All of these Linux laptop integrated graphics benchmarks were done out-of-the-box on Ubuntu 25.04 with the Linux 6.14 kernel and Mesa 25.0.
With the Ryzen AI Max PRO 390 / Radeon 8050S Graphics testing today, it was done in the default (balanced) platform profile state as well as the low-power and performance profiles. Thus you can see the Radeon 8050S Graphics out-of-the-box as well as what happens if going for the "performance" platform profile or reverting to the "low-power" platform profile. More details on ACPI Platform Profiles can be found in the prior
Maximizing The Performance & Power Efficiency Of AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 With Platform Prof

data.title: Aether: A CMS That Gets Out of Your Way
data.author: LebCit
data.article_summary: Aether CMS是一款专注于简洁和性能的内容管理平台。作者最初在WordPress生态系统中工作，但因其过于复杂而转向轻量级工具开发，最终创建了Aether CMS。该平台基于四个核心模块（adm-zip、argon2、litenode、marked），无冗余功能，采用文件存储而非数据库，支持Markdown和YAML前页数据。Aether具有快速开发、内容创建和运行速度，生成静态网站以实现即时加载。其主题系统简单直观，由HTML、CSS和JavaScript构成，无需复杂构建步骤。平台灵活，适用于个人博客、公司文档、营销网站和多作者发布等多种场景，旨在解决现有CMS的弊端，如WordPress的臃肿和Ghost的过度主见。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Aether CMS 的功能、定位、易用性及其与其他CMS（如WordPress、Grav、Hugo、Zola、Decap等）的比较。

不同观点：
• **易用性与技术门槛**：
   - [ivanmontillam] 认为 Aether 虽然定位在内容创作者与开发者之间，但仍对非技术用户不友好。例如，非技术用户不熟悉终端操作，且在Windows系统上可能遇到 `npm` 未识别等问题。相比之下，WordPress 的低摩擦入门体验更适合非技术用户。
   - [CSSer] 赞赏 Aether 的简洁依赖设计，但指出缺乏内容创作者所需的功能（如自定义文章类型、元字段、模块等），这些功能对于现代CMS至关重要。

• **文件式CMS与数据库式CMS的比较**：
   - [dnrvs] 认为将内容存放在可读文件中而不是数据库中的想法在20多年前可能是激进的，但现在并不新颖。
   - [nobleach] 提到 TinaCMS 也是基于文件（git）而非数据库，同时指出像 Drupal 这样的CMS可以满足内容预览、草稿存储等需求。

• **项目定位与功能展示**：
   - [exiguus] 认为 Aether 的定位不够明确，初看时容易与静态网站生成器混淆。
   - [ale] 认为CMS的核心是UI层用于数据插入和模式定义，其他功能可能多余。
   - [c0brac0bra] 希望看到 Aether 与 Decap 的比较。
   - [LunaSea] 询问 Aether 与 Hugo、Zola 的区别。

• **Web前端与内容编辑体验**：
   - [nprateem] 希望有一个Web前端可以隐藏所有Markdown编辑和git操作，以便营销团队可以轻松创建内容。

• **技术选择与个人偏好**：
   - [cies] 赞赏自建项目，但不喜欢用服务器端JS替代PHP，认为这不是进步。

补充讨论：
• **演示与推广**：
   - [r0fl] 对项目感兴趣，但指出缺乏演示使其难以评估。

争议焦点：
• Aether 是否真正实现了对非技术内容创作者的友好性。
• 文件式CMS与传统数据库式CMS在现代应用中的优劣比较。
• 项目定位的明确性与功能展示的清晰度。

44198503.article_content:
Aether CMS is a fast, minimal platform built for simplicity. No bloat, just clean,
modular architecture for effortless content management.
My journey with content management started in the WordPress ecosystem, building themes and
plugins. But over time, I grew tired of the heavyweight platforms and returned to the roots
of the web: HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
That path led me through the
JAMstack
world, but I found
most tools overcomplicated and bloated. So I built
Blog-Doc
, a lightweight CMS/SSG that taught
me the value of simple content workflows. Then came
LiteNode
, my custom Node.js framework built
for performance and minimalism.
Aether CMS is where that journey led
. It's everything I've learned
about content systems, distilled into a platform that runs on just four core modules:
adm-zip
,
argon2
,
litenode
, and
marked
. No bloat. No overengineering. Just fast, clean, modular architecture.
Unlike many JAMstack tools that feel like using a cannon to kill a fly, Aether strikes the
perfect balance between developer empowerment and user-friendliness.
Built from Experience, Not Hype
Aether isn't a weekend project or an AI-generated solution. It's the result of years
of real-world development, starting with WordPress, evolving through Blog-Doc, crafting
LiteNode for it, and culminating in a complete rethink of what a CMS should be.
Every architectural decision reflects actual use and iteration. The integrated static site
generator isn't bolted on, it's fundamental to the design. The file-based storage
isn't trendy, it's practical. The four-dependency approach isn't restrictive,
it's liberating.
This is what happens when you build tools for yourself first, then share them with the
world.
The Philosophy: Files Over Databases
Here's a radical idea: what if your content lived in simple, readable files instead of
being locked away in a database? What if you could edit a blog post in any text editor,
version control your entire site with Git, and deploy anywhere without worrying about
database migrations?
Aether stores everything as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. Your blog post isn't a
row in a MySQL table, it's a file you can read, edit, and understand:
---
title: "Why I Built Another CMS"
slug: "why-i-built-another-cms"
category: "Development"
tags: ["cms", "javascript", "philosophy"]
status: "published"
---
# Why I Built Another CMS
Because sometimes you need to scratch your own itch...
Simple. Portable. Future-proof.
Built for Speed (All Kinds of Speed)
Development Speed
Want to create a custom page layout? Drop an HTML file in your theme's
custom/
folder. Need to modify how posts are displayed? Edit the template. No
plugin APIs to learn, no complex build processes. Just files and folders that make sense.
Content Creation Speed
The admin interface feels familiar if you've used any modern CMS, but it's built
with one goal: get out of your way. Write in Markdown, see a live preview, hit publish. The
media library handles your images without fuss. Categories and tags work exactly like
you'd expect.
Runtime Speed
Here's where Aether really shines: it generates static sites that load instantly. No
database queries, no server-side rendering delays, no PHP processing. Just pre-built HTML
files that any CDN can serve at lightning speed.
npm run build
# Your entire site is now a folder of HTML files
# Deploy to any platform that host static sites
Themes That Don't Fight You
Remember WordPress's template hierarchy? Aether borrowed that idea and made it simpler.
Want a custom layout for your documentation pages? Create
docs.html
in your
theme's
custom/
folder. Need a special design for a specific post? The
template system cascades gracefully from specific to general.
But here's the kicker: themes are just folders of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Templates
are plain
.html
files that use
LiteNode's STE
(Simple
Template Engine), a powerful and intuitive
AST-based
template engine
that runs directly inside your HTML. No complex build steps. No proprietary magic. If you
can build a website, you can build an Aether theme.
Real-World Flexibility
I designed Aether around actual use cases, not theoretical ones:
Personal Blog?
Posts, categories, tags, and RSS feeds work out of the box.
Company Documentation?
Nested custom pages with automatic navigation and
breadcrumbs.
Marketing Site?
Custom page templates for landing pages, about pages,
whatever you need.
Multi-author Publication?
User management with role-based permissions.
Portfolio Site?
Built-in media library with automatic metadata and alt text
management.
The same CMS handles all of these without plugins, extensions, or configuration hell.
Why Another CMS?
Fair question. The world has plenty of content management systems. But most of them optimize
for the wrong things:
❌
WordPress
is powerful but bloated (and still on PHP...)
❌
Ghost
is beautiful but tightly opinionated
❌
SSGs
are fast but only usable by devs
❌
Headless CMSs
are flexible but complex
✅
Aether
:

data.title: An Interactive Guide to Rate Limiting
data.author: sagyam
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据存储和速率限制算法的选择，尤其是在水平扩展服务和API请求管理的场景下。

不同观点：
• joshstrange：询问用户/组织的请求跟踪的最佳数据存储方案，提到了几种选择，如Redis/Valkey、Postgres、DynamoDB。
• hxtk：提出为何很少见到基于服务请求成本或动态学习系统容量的速率限制算法。提到路由器缓冲管理中的算法（如Stochastic Fair Blue），但指出难以应用于HTTP请求场景，因为需要定义每个请求的成功/失败指标。还提到Google的Zanzibar系统中简要提及了基于CPU时间分配的速率限制，但没有详细说明。
• conradludgate：推荐通用信元率算法（GCRA），认为其实现简单，无需后台任务和最小状态存储。GCRA不仅可作为速率限制器，还能作为节流实现，并能自然转换为漏桶算法。
• jsw：认为AIMD算法（加性增加，乘性减少）与令牌桶结合，可以很好地适应后端容量，优于断路器。
• fside：好奇是否有人在遇到实际扩展问题后切换算法，并询问是否有只在规模化时才显现的“坑”。

补充讨论：
• behnamoh：批评某些博客的用户体验，如看到要求使用Google登录的提示就关闭页面。
• chrisweekly：提到《HPBN》（High-Performance Browser Networking）一书，认为其包含相关概念。
• tonyhart7 和 phelm：推荐了另一篇关于速率限制算法的文章链接。
• tra3：提到尝试解释断路器和自适应并发以改善分布式单体性能的困难，认为可视化工具很有帮助。
• mcdow：对交互部分的构建工具表示兴趣。
• onionbagle：好奇是否有人实现了这些算法，并询问使用的技术。
• buggeryorkshire：提到CGNAT在之前工作中引发的问题，但未被提及。

争议焦点：
• mtlyncr：批评文章像是由AI生成且未经仔细审查，指出文章结构和样式问题，如反复使用“Working:”作为标题，以及在暗模式下示例不可用的问题。

这些讨论展示了在数据存储选择和速率限制算法上的多样观点和实际应用中的挑战，尤其是规模化时的潜在问题。

data.title: Odyc.js – A tiny JavaScript library for narrative games
data.author: achtaitaipai
data.article_summary: Odyc.js 是一个小型 JavaScript 库，旨在帮助用户创建视频游戏，即使没有编程经验也能轻松上手。它提供了简单易用的工具，让初学者可以通过编码学习游戏开发。用户可以利用该库制作自己的游戏，同时还能浏览和借鉴他人作品的展示库以获取灵感。Odyc.js 专注于让游戏开发变得更易于访问和有趣，是学习编程和游戏设计的理想选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个JavaScript游戏库的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• [socalgal2] 对标题中的"narrative games"（叙事游戏）提出质疑，认为库的主页并没有明确说明这是针对叙事游戏的，且对什么是叙事游戏表示困惑。她指出，通过谷歌搜索"narrative game"的结果与她看到的示例游戏不符，并质疑该库在制作叙事游戏方面是否有其他游戏引擎不具备的独特功能。

• [kevinsync] 分享了一个具体的游戏链接（Magic Mushroom），并对该游戏表示赞赏，但没有对库本身的功能或定义做进一步讨论。

• [c0nfused] 对该库的整体设计表示赞赏，提到自己曾写过多个JavaScript游戏引擎，而这个库在快速制作游戏和深度研究之间找到了一个很好的平衡点。他计划用这个库来快速制作小游戏以娱乐孩子。

• [NotAnOtter] 认为该库是一个很好的学习工具，特别适合10岁左右的孩子，比Scratch等工具更适合，因为Scratch被设计得过于低龄化。他还建议可以为此工具开设儿童课程，并认为可以在游戏资产的程序生成方面做进一步开发。

• [halfmatthalfcat] 简单表达了对该库的赞赏，但没有进一步展开。

• [fudged71] 分享了一段代码示例，展示了如何使用该库进行简单的游戏对话，但没有对库本身的功能做评价。

• [matkurianski] 对项目表示赞赏，但指出项目是开源的却没有明确的许可证。他询问是否可以添加许可证，以便开发者能够了解可以如何修改和发布他们的分支，并具体询问是否可以将项目翻译成其他语言。

• [hahahacorn] 认为该库非常酷，并分享了一个个人故事，讲述自己在发现这个库之前正好在制作一个叙事 romance 游戏，且从未开发过任何游戏。他认为这个库正好解决了他的需求，并认为这个巧合非常惊人。

• [sciolizer] 提到该库让他想起了PuzzleScript，并提供了一个链接，但没有对库本身的功能做进一步评价。

• [navs] 对库中的canvas视频录制功能表示好奇，表示希望实现类似的功能，但没有对库的其他方面做评价。

• [eldog_] 赞赏了编辑器中的类型使用，特别是它能够识别模板精灵的引用，并在调用函数时传递错误参数的情况下高亮错误。

• [ryoshu] 表示非常喜欢这个库，认为它正好符合一个副项目的要求，但没有进一步展开。

• [wdiamond] 认为这是一个很棒的产品，类似于Scratch，但没有进一步展开。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于什么是“叙事游戏”以及该库是否特别适合制作此类游戏。
• 一些用户对该库的教育用途表示赞赏，特别是对于儿童学习编程的潜力。
• 部分用户对库的具体功能（如代码高亮、视频录制）表示赞赏，并分享了使用场景和个人经验。
• 开源许可证问题也被提出，用户关心是否可以对项目进行修改和发布。

data.title: A masochist's guide to web development
data.author: sebtron
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者将一个Rubik’s Cube解算器从C代码通过Emscripten编译为WebAssembly，并结合JavaScript和HTML构建为网页应用的复杂过程。本文并非传统的网页开发教程，而是面向C/C++开发者，展示如何将程序或库移植到网页端，并提供详细的步骤和代码示例。内容涉及WebAssembly、JavaScript、DOM、多线程、Web Workers、持久存储等主题，并提醒读者该过程可能非常困难。

主要步骤包括：
1. 设置开发环境（Emscripten、Node.js、web服务器）。
2. 从"Hello World"示例开始，展示如何编译和运行WebAssembly程序。
3. 构建复杂库，涵盖多线程、回调函数等高级主题。
4. 提供代码示例和详细说明，帮助读者理解和实现。

本文适合希望将C/C++项目移植到网页的开发者，但不建议寻求常规网页开发指南的读者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript模块系统、代码移植问题、多线程处理困难、项目复杂性及技术选择

不同观点：
• lscharen认为，无论选择`.js`还是`.mjs`扩展名，都会遇到问题。基于其丰富的经验，从dojo到CommonJS、AMD、ESM等各种模块系统的使用经验让他深知这一点的复杂性。
• socalgal2指出，使用`var`声明变量可能引发问题，建议使用`let`或`const`。同时提到原生应用移植到web时，硬编码特定平台惯例（如快捷键）可能会导致跨平台兼容性问题，建议监听复制粘贴事件。
• apatheticonion对JavaScript/Node.js中的多线程处理表示不满，指出SharedArrayBuffer在实际应用中几乎不可用，并提到其团队在处理大规模内存应用时面临的困难，需要借助原生代码和手动管理共享内存。
• lerax认为JavaScript生态系统非常混乱，相比之下，其他技术方案可能更为合理。
• knallfrosch对文章的撰写表示赞赏，提到其团队也在使用emscripten/C++构建项目，并计划引入WebGPU/shaders和WebAudio，预见到更多挑战。
• divbzero对编译代码在浏览器中运行的速度表示惊讶，引用了Emscripten项目的描述，强调WebAssembly的高效性。
• maximevince简单表达了对文章的感谢。
• broken_broken_对文章内容表示认可，并提出关于SQLite和WebAssembly结合使用的疑问和建议。
• wmichelin和udev4096的评论较为简短，分别涉及代码实例和端口使用问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于JavaScript模块系统和变量声明的最佳实践。lscharen和socalgal2从实际经验出发，指出了不同选择可能引发的问题。
• apatheticonion的多线程处理问题揭示了在JavaScript中处理大规模和高性能应用时的技术挑战，特别是SharedArrayBuffer的局限性。
• 其他评论更多是技术实现的细节探讨，如SQLite的使用、WebAssembly的高效性及项目复杂性。

整体来看，讨论涵盖了JavaScript模块系统、变量声明、跨平台兼容性、多线程处理、WebAssembly应用等多个技术层面，展示了开发者在实际项目中面临的各种挑战和解决方案。

44200895.article_content:
A masochist’s guide to web development
Table of contents
Introduction
Setting things up
Hello world
Intermezzo I: What is WebAssembly?
Building a library
Intermezzo II: JavaScript and the DOM
Loading the library and making it a module
Multithreading
Intermezzo III: Web Workers and Spectre
Don’t block the main thread!
Callback functions
Persistent storage
Closing thoughts
Introduction
I have recently worked on making a web application out of
my latest Rubik’s cube optimal solver
.
This involved building a rather complex C code base (with
multithreading, SIMD, callback functions and whatnot) to
WebAssembly
via
Emscripten
, and writing a minimal amount of
JavaScript and HTML for the frontend.
This whole process was complex, tiring and at times frustrating -
but eventually
it was a success
! Not only
I accomplished my goal, but I have learnt a lot along the way. After
finishing the work, I decided to write down all that I have learnt and
share it with the world with this post.
You may be wondering why one should do such a thing instead of either
rewriting their code base in a more web-friendly language, or distributing
their app using a native GUI framework. The main reason to use WebAssembly
is that it can provide near-native performance (or so they claim) while
running inside a web browser; this gives you all the portability of a
web app without too much of a performance drawback, something that would
not be possible with an interpreted language such as JavaScript.
So, what is this blog post? A tutorial for web development? I am not sure
about this, but if it is, it is definitely not a normal one. As the title
suggests, you should not start from this guide unless you just
love
banging your head against the wall.  If you are looking for a
sane
guide to web development, I strongly advise you head on to the
Mozilla Developer Network tutorials page
and start from there.
But if you are a C or C++ developer looking to port a program or library
to the web, then you are in the right place. With this post I am going
to walk you through the process of building an increasingly complex
library that can run in a web browser.  Make sure you are
sitting comfortably and be ready to sweat, because I am not going to
shy away from the hard stuff and the complicated details.
To follow this tutorial you won’t need much experience with web
development, but some familiarity with HTML and an idea of what JavaScript
will be useful. It will also help to know that you can access your
browser’s JavaScript console and other developer tools by pressing F12,
at least on Firefox or Chrome - but I guess I have literally just taught
you that, if you did not already know it. For all the rest, I’ll make
sure to add many hyperlinks throughout the text, so you can follow them
if something is new to you.
A little disclaimer: although I am a somewhat experienced C developer,
I had very little web development experience before embarking in
this adventure.  If you are a web developer, you may find errors in
this post that are going to make you laugh at my ignorance. If you do,
I’d appreciate it if you could report them to me by sending an email to
sebastiano@tronto.net
!
With this out of the way, let’s get started!
Setting things up
The examples used in this tutorial are all contained in a git repository,
which you can find either on
my git page
or
on github
.
In order to follow them you are going to need:
A working installation of
Emscripten
(which also includes Node.js). Refer to the official website for
installation instructions.
A web server such
darkhttpd
or the Python
http.server
package; the examples will use darkhttpd.
I have only tested all of this on Linux, but everything should work
exactly the same on any UNIX system. If you are a Windows user, you can
either run everything inside
WSL
, or you can try and
adjust the examples to your system - if you choose this second option,
I’ll happily accept patches or pull requests :)
Hello world
Let’s start with the classic Hello World program:
#include <stdio.h>
int main() {
printf("Hello, web!\n");
}
You can compile the code above with
emcc -o index.html hello.c
And if you now start a web server in the current folder, for example with
darkhttpd .
(the dot at the end is important), and open a web browser to
localhost:8080
(or whatever port your web server
uses), you should see something like this:
As you can see, the compiler generated a bunch of extra stuff around
you print statement. You may or may not want this, but for now we can
take it as a convenient way to check that our program works as expected.
There are other ways to run this compiled code. With the command above,
the compiler should have generated for you 3 files:
index.html
- the web page in the screenshot above.
index.wasm
- the actual compiled code of your program; this file contains
WebAssembly bytecode.
index.js
- some JavaScript
glue code
to make it possible for
index.wasm
to actually run in a browser.
If you don’t specify
-o inde

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何通过“Confused Deputy”攻击利用GitHub的Dependabot自动合并恶意代码。Dependabot通常用于自动更新项目依赖，但若配置不当，可能被攻击者利用。攻击者可以通过以下步骤进行攻击：首先， fork目标仓库；然后，在fork中添加恶意代码并启用Dependabot，使其生成包含恶意代码的更新分支；接着，创建指向原仓库的Pull Request，触发自动合并工作流。由于`github.actor`不总是指代PR创建者，攻击者可利用此特性触发自动合并，绕过保护规则，最终将恶意代码合并入原仓库。文章还披露了两种新的攻击技术，以扩展已有方法。

44199597.article_content:
Blog Articles
Weaponizing Dependabot: Pwn Request at its finest
Sébastien Graveline
TL;DR
: Your trusty Dependabot (and other GitHub bots) might be an unwitting accomplice. Through "Confused Deputy" attacks, they can be tricked into merging malicious code. This doesn’t stop here. It can escalate to full command injection via crafted branch names and even bypass branch protection rules. Plus, we disclose two new TTPs to build upon previously known techniques.
Introduction
Ah,
Dependabot
!
GitHub's built-in butler, tirelessly checks if your dependencies are fresh and, if not, prepares a PR with the updates. What a lifesaver, right? But, as with any cog in an automated system, there’s always the potential for rust. In this story, it is the
deputy confusion
attack.
Meet Dependabot: Your Automated Dependency Butler
So, how does this magic work? You can boss Dependabot around using a
.github/dependabot.yml
file (check out the
Dependabot options reference
).
Once active, Dependabot periodically scans your repo, guided by its config file. It also perks up and re-scans whenever you tweak this file or poke it via the
https://github.com/<Owner>/<Repo>/network/updates
tab.
When Dependabot spots an outdated dependency, it kicks off a workflow (you'll see "Dependabot Updates" pop up in your Actions tab). Then, it creates a new branch, usually named something like
dependabot/<module_type>/<registry>/<package_name>/<new_version>
. Finally, it opens a Pull Request to your default branch with all the suggested changes.
The "Confused Deputy" Problem: Wait, Who Asked You To Do That?
Now, let's talk about the
Confused Deputy Problem
. It's a classic vulnerability class (
CWE-441
, if you're into that sort of thing) where a trusted party (our "deputy") is tricked by an attacker into performing an action. The deputy thinks it’s doing honest work, but it's carrying out the attacker's nefarious plan.
Some workflows are sensitive – they might have special permissions or access to secrets, so many developers added a user check at the beginning of them. Just to make sure it was triggered by a trusted user.
Naturally, folks got a bit tired of manually approving every single Dependabot PR. "It's just a version update," they'd say. Others might say: "and we usually just end up blindly merging it anyway!". So, they created workflows to auto-merge PRs if the creator was Dependabot.
Something like this GitHub Actions workflow:
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
auto-merge:
runs-on: ubuntu-latest
if: ${
{
github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
}}
steps:
- run:
gh pr merge
$ -d -m
Seems safe, doesn't it? After all, Dependabot is trusted, and an attacker can't just force it to open a PR on a repo they don't control… Here's the trick:
github.actor
does not always refer to the actual creator of the Pull Request. It's the user who caused the latest event that triggered the workflow.
So, if an attacker could somehow force Dependabot into making a change that triggers this auto-merge workflow, they can merge their own malicious code.
Now, an attacker can't directly command Dependabot on a repo they don't have rights to. So, what can they make Dependabot do? Let's look at the events Dependabot is able to trigger:
Event
Action
From fork
Command
pull_request_target
,
pull_request
When creating or updating a pull request.
true
@dependabot recreate
issue_comment
When showing information.
false
@dependabot show <dependency name> ignore conditions
push
When pushing to the branch, when merging etc.
false
@dependabot merge
create
When creating a new branch.
false
N/A
delete
When deleting a branch.
false
@dependabot close
workflow_run
It simply gets triggered as a side-effect of another (named) workflow running or completing.
true
Relevant if the parent workflow was triggered using one of the above commands.
The juicy one here is that Dependabot can be forced to update a Pull Request, even one originating from a fork!
Here's the evil plan:
Fork It
: Attacker forks a target repository. This repo has one of those "auto-merge if Dependabot" workflows.
Rig it
: Attacker adds their
malicious payload
to the
Default branch
of their fork.
Wake Up, Dependabot!
: Attacker enables Dependabot on their fork and adds an obviously outdated dependency to get its attention (often at the time you fork, this pre-requisite will already be met).
Dependabot Does Its Thing
: Dependabot creates its update branch on the fork. Since this branch is based on the fork's own Default branch, the now includes the attacker's payload (
through the refs/pulls/ read-only namespace
).
The Bait
: Attacker creates a Pull Request from this weaponized Dependabot branch on their fork, targeting the original (victim) repository.
Firing blanks
: This new PR triggers the auto-merge workflow in the victim repo. However, at this point,
github.actor
is the attacker, so the if condition fails, and the workflow doesn't merge anything.
Confused, are you?
: Attacker goes back to the original Pull Request in their fork

data.title: Small Programs and Languages
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了小型Forth实现以及小型程序的吸引力。小型程序更易于阅读和理解，例如一个有趣的功能若仅用20行代码实现，会比用2000行实现更引人关注。文章列举了几个例子，如Luke Jackson的25行JavaScript库`ijk`，以及Philippe Brochard的46字节Forth实现。作者还提到Roger K.W. Hui描述的单页C语言解释器，以及William Byrd演讲中提到的精美Lisp解释器。

文章进一步探讨了这些小型程序的意义，指出它们不仅是一种编程娱乐，还揭示了程序的最小复杂性。例如，名片大小的光线追踪器展示了光线追踪器的最低复杂度。作者还提到了Kolmogorov复杂性，即生成某个对象的最短程序长度，并指出小型实现帮助人们理解编程语言的基本概念。最后，提到Justine Tunney实现的436字节LISP，展示了垃圾回收语言的核心可以压缩到如此小的规模。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小型编程语言与Kolmogorov复杂性的关系，小型语言的表达能力与实用性，以及具体的小型语言实现和其设计哲学。

不同观点：
• **tromp**：Kolmogorov复杂性激发了对最小且最具表达力语言的探索，并定义了不同 flavor 的 Kolmogorov 复杂性。tromp 强调通过小型语言来理解程序的最小尺寸和复杂性。
• **karmakaze**：小型语言通常是创建特定编程抽象的原型语言，像 Lisp 这样的语言由于每个项目自成一个方言而不易普及。相比之下，像 Clojure 这样更具意见性且功能齐全的语言更实用。
• **antilisp**：实现小型语言是一种极好的学习体验，通过实现语言可以发现新的创新机会。例如，在 Lisp 中将宏和公理作为函数类型的特例处理，并通过解释器决定运行时的评估方式。
• **nicolaskruchten**：通过量化和可视化库来研究小型语言的小型性与表达能力的权衡，得出了一些有趣的结论。
• **bradain**：不喜欢小型 Lisp 实现，认为真正的 Lisp 应该是元循环的，即解释器能够解释自身。使用简化技巧虽然缩短了代码，但失去了元循环评估的能力。
• **norir**：Kolmogorov 复杂性虽然有趣但具有误导性，因为解释某些极小程序时需要依赖外部上下文和公理，而这些无法在程序本身中定义。

补充讨论：
• **forinti**：20世纪80年代的计算机杂志经常刊登小型项目，这些项目既能教学又足够小，可以手动输入学习。
• **asplake**：寻找类似于ML或更具Lisp风格但支持柯里化的微小语言，可能是为了学习和趣味。
• **dunham**：Meta II 是一个用于编写编译器的小型语言，包括自编译能力，具有历史和技术意义。
• **xelxebar**：提到一个仅有41行的极其简洁的C语言Lisp解释器，强调了可读代码的重要性。
• **muth02446**：Cwerg 是一种类似C的低级语言，具有Python风格的语法，前端代码限制在10k行以内，展示了小型语言的另一种实现方式。
• **agentultra**：小型编码和尺寸编码是有趣的活动，参考demo场景。正在开发最小的事件存储数据库，作为企业软件开发之外的调剂。
• **anthk**：提到一个网站（https://t3x.org）提供多种小型语言，如Lisp、Forth和Pascal等，并指出TCL（jimtcl）具有强大的CLI/TUI工具开发能力。
• **codr7**：最近在多个宿主语言中开发小型语言的基板/引导程序，展示了小型语言的实现和探索的持续性。

争议焦点：
• **小型语言的实用性**：karmakaze 认为小型语言如 Lisp 因为自定义方言的问题不易普及，而 antilisp 和 tromp 则强调小型语言的实现和研究价值。
• **Kolmogorov 复杂性的实际应用**：norir 认为 Kolmogorov 复杂性在实际应用中具有误导性，因为外部上下文和公理的依赖性，而 tromp 则认为这是理解程序最小尺寸和复杂性的关键。

总体而言，讨论围绕小型语言的设计、实现、实用性以及其在Kolmogorov复杂性研究中的应用展开，展示了不同开发者和研究者的视角和经验。

44200797.article_content:
My
Implementing a Forth
article got some
great feedback, particularly around the subject of tiny Forth implementations.
(And it was an excuse to list some of the tiniest Forths I’ve seen.)
I know I’m not alone in seeing the appeal of tiny Forths, tiny languages, tiny
programs, and just small stuff in general. What’s up with that, anyway?
The appeal of tiny programs
Tiny programs are approachable.
If I see that something is 200 lines of code, I’m
much
more likely to
read it than if it’s 2,000 or 20,000 lines.
What’s more, if it’s a program that does something interesting in 20 lines when
I was
expecting
2,000, then I’m going to be very, very interested to read
those 20 lines!
When I was researching DOM diffing libraries
prior to creating
RetroV
, one of
the repos I looked at was
ijk
by Luke Jackson.
I was pretty used to looking at fat JavaScript
libraries at that point, so when I cracked open
the source file for ijk, I was really surprised.
Here’s the source:
index.js
(githubusercontent.com).
Just 25 lines!
I was instantly intrigued.
More recently, one of the responses to my aforementioned Forth article was
Philippe Brochard with a 46 byte "Forth".
46 bytes!
It’s
so
small, I can just put the hexdump right here:
50b8 8e00 31d8 e8ff 0017 003c 0575 00ea
5000 3c00 7401 eb02 e8ee 0005 0588 eb47
b8e6 0200 d231 14cd e480 7580 c3f4
(See my update to
Implementing a Forth
for more
about this artifact.)
Sure, very few people jump at a chance to read raw machine code. But that’s
exactly my point.  Something
this
small doesn’t feel so scary, right? I mean,
46 bytes. If you put the effort into it, you
know
you can figure out how it
works eventually.
This next one almost serves as a counter-example because the code is so dense
and frightening, but I can’t help mentioning it anyway.
One of my favorite software stories is Roger K.W. Hui’s Appendix A "Incunabulum"
from
An Implementation of J
in which he describes Arthur Whitney writing
an array-based language interpreter,
"…​on
one page
and in one afternoon â an interpreter fragment
on the AT&T 3B1 computer. I studied this interpreter for about a week for its
organization and programming style…​"
Hui can list the entire interpreter in the appendix because it’s just that
single page,
122 lines

https://code.jsoftware.com/wiki/Essays/Incunabulum
I haven’t personally tackled that puzzle yet, but it’s in my unwritten list of
dense computer things that I would print out and take with me if I suddenly
found myself cast out of society and forced to go live alone up on a mountain
or something.
(By the way, J is in the family of array languages which include APL.
If you enjoy brevity, cryptic programming puzzles, and high performance
numerical computing, these languages have got you covered!)
Something else that would certainly need to be in the collection I take to that
lonely mountain would have to be

(lambda (expr env)
(pmatch expr
[`,x (guard (symbol? x))
(env x)]

(eval-expr body (lambda (y)
(if (eq? x y)
arg
(env y)))))]

((eval-expr rator env)
(eval-expr rand env))])))

transcription of the code

Now, we all know that
code golfing
(wikipedia.org) is
a programmer’s recreational game, and just for fun, right?
But is any of this actually useful?
Actually, I’ll go one step further and say that these examples are
more than just useful. They are
meaningful
.
When you see a
ray tracer that fits on a business card
(fabiensanglard.net), it makes you realize that a ray tracer is
something that can fit on a business card
!
That’s an actual
fact
about the minimum complexity of ray tracers.

(wikipedia.org) is:
"…​the length of a shortest computer program (in a predetermined programming language) that produces the object as output."

favorite thing in what was otherwise a pretty dry and depressing book.)
The meaning I get from this is that code golfers, for the benefit of the whole

complexity
of those programs. Way to go code golfers!

fact

44200797.article_summary:
文章讨论了小型Forth实现以及小型程序的吸引力。小型程序更易于阅读和理解，例如一个有趣的功能若仅用20行代码实现，会比用2000行实现更引人关注。文章列举了几个例子，如Luke Jackson的25行JavaScript库`ijk`，以及Philippe Brochard的46字节Forth实现。作者还提到Roger K.W. Hui描述的单页C语言解释器，以及William Byrd演讲中提到的精美Lisp解释器。

文章进一步探讨了这些小型程序的意义，指出它们不仅是一种编程娱乐，还揭示了程序的最小复杂性。例如，名片大小的光线追踪器展示了光线追踪器的最低复杂度。作者还提到了Kolmogorov复杂性，即生成某个对象的最短程序长度，并指出小型实现帮助人们理解编程语言的基本概念。最后，提到Justine Tunney实现的436字节LISP，展示了垃圾回收语言的核心可以压缩到如此小的规模。
44200797.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小型编程语言与Kolmogorov复杂性的关系，小型语言的表达能力与实用性，以及具体的小型语言实现和其设计哲学。

不同观点：
• **tromp**：Kolmogorov复杂性激发了对最小且最具表达力语言的探索，并定义了不同 flavor 的 Kolmogorov 复杂性。tromp 强调通过小型语言来理解程序的最小尺寸和复杂性。
• **karmakaze**：小型语言通常是创建特定编程抽象的原型语言，像 Lisp 这样的语言由于每个项目自成一个方言而不易普及。相比之下，像 Clojure 这样更具意见性且功能齐全的语言更实用。
• **antilisp**：实现小型语言是一种极好的学习体验，通过实现语言可以发现新的创新机会。例如，在 Lisp 中将宏和公理作为函数类型的特例处理，并通过解释器决定运行时的评估方式。
• **nicolaskruchten**：通过量化和可视化库来研究小型语言的小型性与表达能力的权衡，得出了一些有趣的结论。
• **bradain**：不喜欢小型 Lisp 实现，认为真正的 Lisp 应该是元循环的，即解释器能够解释自身。使用简化技巧虽然缩短了代码，但失去了元循环评估的能力。
• **norir**：Kolmogorov 复杂性虽然有趣但具有误导性，因为解释某些极小程序时需要依赖外部上下文和公理，而这些无法在程序本身中定义。

补充讨论：
• **forinti**：20世纪80年代的计算机杂志经常刊登小型项目，这些项目既能教学又足够小，可以手动输入学习。
• **asplake**：寻找类似于ML或更具Lisp风格但支持柯里化的微小语言，可能是为了学习和趣味。
• **dunham**：Meta II 是一个用于编写编译器的小型语言，包括自编译能力，具有历史和技术意义。
• **xelxebar**：提到一个仅有41行的极其简洁的C语言Lisp解释器，强调了可读代码的重要性。
• **muth02446**：Cwerg 是一种类似C的低级语言，具有Python风格的语法，前端代码限制在10k行以内，展示了小型语言的另一种实现方式。
• **agentultra**：小型编码和尺寸编码是有趣的活动，参考demo场景。正在开发最小的事件存储数据库，作为企业软件开发之外的调剂。
• **anthk**：提到一个网站（https://t3x.org）提供多种小型语言，如Lisp、Forth和Pascal等，并指出TCL（jimtcl）具有强大的CLI/TUI工具开发能力。
• **codr7**：最近在多个宿主语言中开发小型语言的基板/引导程序，展示了小型语言的实现和探索的持续性。

争议焦点：
• **小型语言的实用性**：karmakaze 认为小型语言如 Lisp 因为自定义方言的问题不易普及，而 antilisp 和 tromp 则强调小型语言的实现和研究价值。
• **Kolmogorov 复杂性的实际应用**：norir 认为 Kolmogorov 复杂性在实际应用中具有误导性，因为外部上下文和公理的依赖性，而 tromp 则认为这是理解程序最小尺寸和复杂性的关键。

总体而言，讨论围绕小型语言的设计、实现、实用性以及其在Kolmogorov复杂性研究中的应用展开，展示了不同开发者和研究者的视角和经验。

data.title: Top researchers leave Intel to build startup with 'the biggest, baddest CPU'
data.author: dangle1
data.article_summary: AheadComputing是由四位曾在英特尔工作数十年的顶级芯片架构师创立的初创公司，其CEO Debbie Marr表示，他们离开英特尔是为了在一个新的架构RISC-V上开发更高效的微处理器。RISC-V是一种开放架构，相较于英特尔的x86架构，它更简洁且无需支付许可费用，适合定制化芯片设计。AheadComputing计划打造高性能CPU，目标市场包括PC、笔记本电脑和数据中心，潜在客户有谷歌、亚马逊等。尽管距离产品上市还需数年，公司已获得2200万美元风投资金，并在行业内引起广泛关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CPU架构设计及其未来发展方向，包括多核处理器、指令集、遗留问题、专利问题以及与现有技术的比较。

不同观点：
• [zackmorris] 主张设计并销售具备本地内存的多核CPU（256-1024核），认为现代编程语言（如Erlang/Go）和工具（如GNU Octave/MATLAB）可以有效管理大量进程，避免传统指令集架构的局限性。他还提到Amdahl's law对并行计算的限制，并认为Rust语言的兴起是为了解决这些问题。

• [johnklos] 强调了CPU中的遗留问题，指出为了兼容旧技术，现代CPU耗费大量晶体管处理同步、指令解码等问题。他提出了一种假设，即如果没有这些遗留问题和安全漏洞（如Spectre和Meltdown），我们可以实现更高的性能，甚至超过当代x86 CPU。

• [kleiba] 对专利问题表示担忧，指出在设计新CPU架构时避免专利侵权是一个重大挑战。

• [ahartmetz] 对RISC-V和专用芯片的未来表示疑问，认为尽管RISC-V没有版权费用，但在创新方面并没有太多新意。他还对是否应开发更多核或更高效的核提出疑问。

• [guywithahat] 作为一个对CPU架构了解较少的人，提出是否可能设计一种新的指令集，以更好地适应现代需求。他认识到这需要巨大的软件努力，并提到RISC-V尽管更新但仍基于ARM。

补充讨论：
• [phendrenad2] 提到之前讨论过的内容，提供了一个9个月前的讨论链接。
• [Foobar8568] 怀念20世纪80-90年代的架构疯狂时代。
• [aesbetic] 认为Intel拒绝提供细节使得这个话题看起来更像是Intel的问题，而不是真正令人兴奋的创新。
• [ngneer] 提到与被取消的Royal和Beast Lake项目可能的关系。
• [esafak] 希望开发GPU而不是新的CPU。
• [energy123] 对AheadComputing这个名称表示赞赏，认为其具有复古和过时的趋势。
• [pstuart] 建议Intel资助更多的初创公司，以快速和自由地进行创新，并在成熟时整合到Intel中。
• [jmclnx] 对RISC-VI开放架构表示支持，并希望其不会像Intel的某些技术那样带来负面影响。

争议焦点：
• 是否可以通过新的CPU架构和指令集设计来突破现有技术的限制，特别是在多核处理和遗留问题方面。
• RISC-V和其他新兴架构是否能真正带来颠覆性的创新，还是仅仅是现有技术的变种。
• 专利问题在设计新架构时是否会成为重大障碍。

44201072.article_content:
Top researchers leave Intel to build startup with ‘the biggest, baddest CPU’
Published:
Jun. 06, 2025, 6:15 a.m.
AheadComputing CEO and co-founder Debbie Marr spent more than three decades at Intel, helping lead development of several generations of microprocessor. But she said her latest ideas required her to start fresh: "What we want to do has to be done outside of Intel. We want to move fast, we want to take a run at RISC-V."
Mike Rogoway/The Oregonian
By
Mike Rogoway | The Oregonian/OregonLive
Together, the four founders of Beaverton startup AheadComputing spent nearly a century at Intel.
They were among Intel’s top chip architects, working years in advance to develop new generations of microprocessors to power the computers of the future.
Now they’re on their own, flying without a net, building a new class of microprocessor on an entirely different architecture from Intel’s. Founded a year ago, AheadComputing is trying to prove there’s a better way to design computer chips.
“AheadComputing is doing the biggest, baddest CPU in the world,” said Debbie Marr, the company’s CEO.
A CPU is a central processing unit, the brain inside a computer. Intel has dominated the CPU market for decades, selling processors based on an architecture the chipmaker owns, called x86.
Today, the computing ecosystem is fragmenting as new standards emerge. That’s one of the reasons Intel is struggling, as computing mainstays like Apple and Google use rival architectures to design their own chips for PCs, smartphones and data centers.
AheadComputing is betting on an open architecture called RISC-V — RISC stands for “reduced instruction set computer.” The idea is to craft a streamlined microprocessor that works more efficiently by doing fewer things, and doing them better than conventional processors.
For AheadComputing’s founders and 80 employees, many of them also Intel alumni, it’s a major break from the kind of work they’ve been doing all their careers. They’ve left a company with more than 100,000 workers to start a business with fewer than 100.
“Every person in this room,” Marr said, looking across a conference table at her colleagues, “we could have stayed at Intel. We could have continued to do very exciting things at Intel.”
They decided they had a better chance at leading a revolution in semiconductor technology at a startup than at a big, established company like Intel. And AheadComputing could be at the forefront of renewal in Oregon’s semiconductor ecosystem.
“We see this opportunity, this light,” Marr said. “We took our chances.”
Big players lose clout
Intel has been operating in Oregon since the 1970s and has long been Oregon’s largest corporate employer. It has more than 20,000 employees in Washington County, including some of the world’s top semiconductor researchers.
Very rarely, though, have any of those thousands of workers left to start their own chip business.
That’s partly because it’s prohibitively expensive for a new company to build a semiconductor factory, and partly because Intel and other tech giants controlled the essential pieces around the CPU. It was hard for newcomers to break in.
Today’s chip startups, however, don’t need their own factories. So-called fabless semiconductor designers like AheadComputing can outsource manufacturing to contractors like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. The graphics and AI chip designer Nvidia has become a $3 trillion company — the world’s most valuable business — doing exactly that.
And AheadComputing cofounder Jonathan Pearce says the reign of the chip titans is fading as the systems that run computers break up into a series of “chiplets” from various companies, optimized for specific tasks.
“You get the opportunity for a company like AheadComputing to provide that piece of the overall system,” Pearce said. “As opposed to the past 20 years where it was just one tech giant.”
RISC-V, pronounced “Risk-five,” is especially inviting to startups because it’s an open technology, overseen by a consortium of tech firms. Unlike processors based on x86 or ARM designs, there’s no licensing fee to use RISC-V.
AheadComputing maintains that open standards are the future for microprocessors, giving technology companies more opportunity to customize chip designs to suit their specific needs.
It will be years before AheadComputing’s designs are on the market, but it envisions its chips will someday power PCs, laptops and data centers. Possible clients could include Google, Amazon, Samsung or other large computing companies.
Members of AheadComputing's executive team. From left to right: Mark Dechene (co-founder), Alon Mahl (vice president), Jonathan Pearce (co-founder), Srikanth Srinivasan (co-founder), Debbie Marr (co-founder, CEO)
Mike Rogoway/The Oregonian

data.title: The Coleco Adam Computer
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: The Coleco Adam电脑是玩具和游戏机制造商Coleco于1983年推出的一款家用电脑，旨在与Commodore 64竞争，但最终未能实现预期，于1985年停产。Coleco曾是知名的玩具制造商，1982年成功推出ColecoVision游戏机，采用Z-80 CPU及德州仪器的图形和声音芯片，性能接近任天堂NES。Coleco Adam最初定价525美元，包含80K RAM、全行程键盘、磁带存储、打印机及软件，计划通过与现有ColecoVision游戏机结合来吸引消费者。然而，Coleco低估了生产难度，价格升至725美元，且延迟发布，缺陷率高，存储设备和打印机存在设计问题。与此同时，Commodore解决了生产问题，售出300万台C64，而Coleco因供货不足和产品缺陷错失机会，最终失败。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Coleco Adam计算机的优缺点及历史评价

不同观点：
• VonGuard认为Coleco Adam是一台“绝对的悲剧”，批评其设计缺陷，如磁带驱动器问题、加载时间长、以及如果启动时磁带未取出可能导致数据丢失。他还提到该计算机附带的Buck Rogers游戏虽然受欢迎，但整体体验糟糕。
• forinti回忆帮助购买电脑的经历，提到Adam的磁带问题和8位计算机在当时的过时性。他建议购买Amiga或MSX，最终购买了Atari ST，认为Adam不值得选择。
• jgneff对Adam的评价较为正面，提到其母亲用Adam与自己通过电子邮件交流，并认为其功能类似于打字机，效果不错。不过，其母亲后来因不适应窗口系统而停止使用新电脑。
• badc0ffee对Adam的高速磁带驱动技术感到着迷，认为尽管这项技术是过时的，但其设计精良，属于旧技术的终极改进。
• PaulHoule回忆高中时使用Adam的经历，提到其坚固的金属框架和独特的磁带驱动音效，同时指出早期计算机由于硬件依赖性强，软件移植困难。

补充讨论：
• DrNosferatu认为Coleco错失了通过制造或授权Coleco Vision游戏适配器在MSX平台上赚钱的机会。
• flomo指出Adam在营销上曾承诺将ColecoVision升级为电脑，但因延迟发布和不吸引人的价格而失败。
• stilldavid和barney54对Adam有美好回忆，主要因其游戏功能，而非其实际计算能力。
• devnull3提到在《辛普森一家》中出现的电脑是Coleco Adam，增加了一些趣味性。
• BizarroLand分享了个人获得Adam的经历，尽管最终因家庭原因被丢弃，但回忆起其运行质量如卡通般的游戏体验。
• Mountain_Skies提到同学对Adam的渴望，以及自己后来得到一台Adam，虽然过时，但对其内部结构感兴趣。

争议焦点：
