• 技术实现的可能性和道德问题（如盗版版本的Cursor）也是潜在的争议点。

44207063.article_content:
Reverse Engineering Cursor's LLM Client
June 5, 2025
· Viraj Mehta, Aaron Hill, Gabriel Bianconi
What happens under the hood at Cursor?
We wired
TensorZero
between Cursor and the LLMs to see every token fly by… and bend those API calls to our own will.
TensorZero is an open-source framework that helps engineers optimize LLM applications with downstream feedback signals (e.g. production metrics, human feedback, user behavior), and we figured it would be interesting to see whether we could use TensorZero on the LLM application we use most heavily ourselves: Cursor.
With our gateway between Cursor and the LLM providers, we can observe the LLM calls being made, run evaluations on individual inferences, use inference-time optimizations, and even experiment with and optimize the prompts and models that Cursor uses.
Cursor is optimized for its population of users as a whole — beyond
.cursorrules
, is there room for improvement by diving deeper and tailoring it to individual users?
What would it look like to be able to empirically experiment with and optimize Cursor for your individual usage patterns?
Beyond optimization, Cursor still operates as a black box.
Wouldn’t it be interesting to see what’s actually being sent to the models?
Nearly all LLM optimization, evaluation, and experimentation techniques require data on what inferences were made and their real-world consequences.
In this post, we’ll focus on the former and dive into how we set up TensorZero as a self-hosted proxy between Cursor and the LLMs that it calls.
If you’d like to try it yourself, check out the
example
in our repository.
We’ll follow up with a blog post on how we collect feedback and close the optimization loop.
Wiring Things Together
The first thing we noticed was that Cursor lets you override the OpenAI base URL and model names.
Perfect.
TensorZero exposes an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint, so we can easily configure Cursor to call TensorZero instead of OpenAI.
In the TensorZero configuration, we define a TensorZero function
cursorzero
so that we can automatically experiment with different models and prompts while storing provider-agnostic inference and feedback data in our database for observability and optimization.
The First Roadblock: Cursor’s Servers
Cursor was initially unable to connect to TensorZero running locally.
It turns out that Cursor first sends a request to its own servers, where additional processing happens before making the LLM call, so it couldn’t connect to our gateway on
localhost
.
(This also means that your credentials must be forwarded to Cursor’s servers, allowing them to collect data on your inferences and codebase.)
As a test that our plan could work in the first place, we pointed Cursor to OpenRouter and realized we could use its models for the Ask, Agent, and Cmd+K interactions in Cursor.
We were also still able to use the normal Cursor Tab completions, which rely on a proprietary model Cursor serves for inline completions (it is very good, so we’re glad to be able to keep it).
The solution was to set up a reverse proxy to expose a public endpoint that would forward requests back to our machine.
We used Ngrok to keep things simple.
Since we were exposing a gateway with LLM credentials to the public Internet, we added Nginx in front of our gateway to authenticate requests.
We set Cursor’s base URL to our Ngrok endpoint, added the credentials we set up in Nginx, turned off built-in models, and finally added our new TensorZero function under the model name
tensorzero::function_name::cursorzero
.
In the end, the workflow looked like this: Cursor → Ngrok → Nginx (self-hosted) → TensorZero (self-hosted) → LLM providers
But it didn’t work.
The Second Roadblock: CORS
The authentication process had failed.
Nginx logs showed that there was an
OPTIONS
request hitting our endpoint, so we configured Nginx to return headers on
OPTIONS
requests and incrementally added headers we saw in responses from the OpenAI API.
This is the initial verification request that comes from the local Cursor IDE.
The CORS requirement likely comes from Electron.
After the initial verification, all requests come from Cursor’s servers.
Our Nginx Configuration to handle CORS headers
# --- CORS helper macro ---
set $CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN  $http_origin;   # reflect the caller's origin
set $CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS "Authorization,Content-Type";
location / {
# --- pre-flight ---
if ($request_method = OPTIONS) {
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Origin      $CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN always;
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Credentials "true"             always;
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Methods     "GET,POST,OPTIONS" always;
add_header Access-Control-Allow-Headers     $CORS_ALLOW_HEADERS always;
add_header Access-Control-Max-Age           86400              always;
return 204;  # 204 (No Content) is conventional for pre-flight
}
}
You can find the entire codebase for “CursorZero” on
GitHub
.
It finally worked!
Finally: Observability for Cursor
We could finally

About
Precision Clock Mk IV
The mitxela Precision Clock Mk IV is the latest development in my quest to build the best wall clock.
GPS synchronised, millisecond display.
Brightness adjusts automatically, and the display doesn't flicker even when filmed at high speed (tested at 25,000FPS).
The precision is tied to the accuracy: if the GPS signal is lost, and the time starts to drift, the last few digits will progressively disappear, and only come back when it re-syncs.
Auto timezone.
The clock contains an on-board world map and timezone database. Using the GPS coordinates and a point-in-polygon algorithm, the clock calculates the correct local time (including daylight saving) without any configuration, and will automatically update when carried across timezone boundaries. The USB port presents a mass storage device, so when the maps or database change, updating them is as simple as drag-and-drop.
Multiple display modes
are supported, including ISO-ordinal, ISO-week, Unix timestamp, Julian date, and a high-precision countdown mode. For a full list of modes, see the
user manual
. More display modes may be released in future firmware updates, which again, are as simple as drag-and-drop with the USB port.
Finally,
the clock can fold in half
, to become more compact. The top display automatically rotates, and a small magnet holds it together. Using the clock as a clapperboard is possible, but not advised.
In the unfolded position, the clock is 53cm (21 inches) wide. Folded, it's about 27cm (10.5 inches) wide and 7cm (3 inches) tall.

to the project page
.

主要讨论点：OpenAI的数据保留政策及其在法律要求下的隐私保护措施

不同观点：
• molf认为OpenAI虽然在文档中提到可以申请零数据保留（ZDR），但实际申请却被忽略，怀疑这是出于营销目的，而非真正实施。
• _jab指出OpenAI在保护用户隐私方面采取了有效的措施，并认为如果数据泄露应归咎于OpenAI，而非法院命令涉及的媒体。
• supriyo-biswas建议使用模糊哈希（如ssdeep）来存储数据指纹，而非实际对话内容，以此作为在法律要求下的折中方案。
• sega_sai批评对媒体的指责是不合理的，认为如果有法律依据，应通过法院解决。
• hombre_fatal强调LLM聊天记录泄露比浏览器历史泄露更严重，因为这是个人独处时的真实想法。
• conartist6批评OpenAI在解释法院命令时的语气，认为其未完全说明情况。
• atleastoptimal认为将数据发送到公司托管的API时默认数据会被永久记录是常识。
• energy123质疑OpenAI提供的隐私控制选项，认为其具有误导性。
• yoaviram批评OpenAI的隐私保护措施，认为其在收费服务中才提供真正的隐私保护。

• amluto指出零数据保留API难以获得，认为如果任何用户都能使用会更好。

• CjHuber虽然认为OpenAI的回应有争议，但赞赏其公开发声。

- 对法院命令和隐私保护的法律合规性存在不同看法，特别是在GDPR等隐私法律下。

- 对OpenAI领导层在隐私问题上的双重标准（如收集眼部数据）表示质疑。

Why you need to care about Product
Product is the most critical pillar of a squad. It doesn't matter if your tech stack has 100% unit test coverage and your team always delivers on time if the deliveries have no impact. Most startups fail because they run out of cash before shipping a product that people want.
Even if you're not in a startup, every team operates like a small company within a larger organization. If no one is interested in your product, it's only a matter of time before the team disbands. Your mission is to solidify your squad's
reason for being
before that happens.
The first step to shipping the right things is knowing your problem domain. Answering "What problem was my squad created to solve? For whom?" helps you understand your target market and your customers' issues, such as how they work around them currently and what value will be delivered when they use your product.
In most companies, a squad will also include a Product Manager (PM) who typically owns this pillar, but Product is ultimately a shared team responsibility.
It's too important to leave up to one person.
Product Manager vs. Engineering Manager
Your product manager (PM) champions the "what" and "why" of a product. They conduct market research and user analysis to understand your target customers, who they are, and the problems they need to solve.
Using this research, PMs map potential solutions and features. They then prioritize these solutions based on the value they could bring, such as potential revenue, increased user conversion, or better engagement.
Having a product manager on your team is a valuable asset. While engineers complain about the extra meetings PMs schedule, some are critical for defining the right product to build, ensuring engineering efforts are well-directed.
They help answer the ultimate question: "Are we building the right thing?".
Collaborating with your PM
If you have a PM, you need to work closely with them to establish a healthy product roadmap and receive context on the expectations around your squad.
It's your responsibility to communicate on technical blockers that could impact the final product or its delivery date and align tradeoffs. It's their responsibility to provide your squad with new projects that will have a significant impact. You must keep each other accountable for each doing their part.
Your PM will be talking with all sorts of people—executives, clients, other PMs, and leads. These chats often spark requests that need your technical perspective. Sometimes, these requests are pretty straightforward, and your role will be to help figure out the best timing for them on the roadmap.
Other times, a new idea might not be quite doable with your current tech. You must push back, align, and adjust the scope to seek a better impact-to-effort ratio.
Once your team assembles a part of the roadmap, you'll delegate the solution's architecture to your engineers. You'll then work with them to establish milestones and deadlines, communicating these back to the PM.
This close collaboration also helps your PM build trust in your team, which is critical when you provide effort estimates for proposed solutions. They must believe in your team's capability to deliver, as they'll often defend your timelines and plans to upper management.
When you don't have a PM
If you don't have a PM, someone needs to act as one.
In companies where the PM leaves or becomes overwhelmed, the team might see its product roadmap stall, run out of projects, or begin prioritizing the wrong initiatives.
Not having a dedicated PM permanently can be reasonable in specific scenarios. For example, the CEO often takes on this role in early-stage startups, building client relationships and bringing market insights directly to the engineering team.
Another squad scenario that doesn't require a PM is a purely technical project, like a large-scale database migration. Here, the target value and success metrics are often so clear that the technical team inherently understands the "what" and "why."
Why your engineers also need to care
Managers are responsible for the product, but it's essential for everyone in the squad to care about it, even if you have a highly competent Product Manager. Getting your engineers to care about the product is one of your core responsibilities as an engineering manager.
You need to be an evangelist for the problems your team is there to solve. Help your engineers develop empathy for the challenges your clients face and see their work's positive impact on clients' lives once the project is delivered.
The first reason you do this is to
motivate people
. A few times in my career as a developer, I wondered, "Who is this feature even for? Who will use it?". No one on my team knew. We were doing it because
we were told to
. Our morale was low, and we felt we were working on things that didn't matter.
The second reason is that
your team isn't paid to create code but to solve problems
. Code has value only when it

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用three.js和GSAP在球体表面动画一个网格。首先，通过经纬度选择球面上的两个位置，并使用`latLongToVector3`函数将其转换为3D坐标。接着，通过`calcPathPoints`函数计算两点间的路径，使用球面线性插值（slerp）生成一系列路径点。然后，利用这些点创建可视化路径（使用`createPath`）。最后，添加一个盒子网格并使用GSAP动画库沿路径移动，通过创建样条曲线并插值`t`值（从0到1）实现平滑动画。动画过程中，盒子的位置根据样条曲线动态更新。

data.title: What Happens When People Don't Understand How AI Works
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary: 1863年，一位署名“Cellarius”的作者在新西兰报纸《The Press》上警告快速工业化将导致“机械王国”控制人类，这封信后来被发现是作家塞缪尔·巴特勒所写，他后来在小说《埃瑞璜》中探讨了人工智能。如今，科技记者Karen Hao等认为这个“机械王国”已成为现实，特别是在AI领域。她的书《Empire of AI》揭示了开发如ChatGPT等大语言模型背后的劳动，而《The AI Con》则揭露了AI行业背后的炒作。这些书指出，AI并非如开发者所宣传的那样是具有思考和感觉能力的机器，而只是通过大量数据进行概率计算的工具。然而，许多人误解了AI的能力和局限，甚至产生了如“ChatGPT引发精神病”的现象，有人将AI视为神圣指引。这反映了人们对AI本质理解的困难，以及被误导的风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对大型语言模型（LLMs）是否具有“理解”能力的不同看法，以及对用词的争议。

不同观点：
• 观点一：大型语言模型不具备“理解”能力。评论中的某些人认为，LLMs无法真正“理解”世界，无论它们的表现多么接近人类的语言使用。这种观点强调，LLMs的运作基于统计和模式识别，而不是真正的理解。例如，有人指出，Hassabis所说的“理解”实际上是一种误用，因为LLMs并不具备类似人类的理解能力。

• 观点二：对“理解”的定义可以随语境变化。另一部分评论者认为，虽然LLMs的“理解”与人类的理解不同，但在技术语境下，使用“理解”这个词是合理的。例如，有人说，在技术讨论中，像“thinks”和“knows”这样的词经常被用来描述计算机程序的行为，即使它们没有人类的认知能力。这种观点强调，语言是动态的，词义会随语境变化。

• 观点三：争议源于对词义的僵化理解。有评论指出，争议的根源在于有人对词义持过于僵化的看法，而没有认识到语言在不同语境下的延展性。例如，有人认为，作者如果不能认识到这一点，那么所谓的“概念错误”其实是他们自己的误解。

补充讨论：
• 对用词准确性的要求是否过于苛刻。有人认为，对Hassabis用词的批评过于吹毛求疵，因为在技术领域，这种用词是非常普遍且被广泛接受的。

• 语言的动态性。评论中提到，语言本身是动态的，词义会随语境变化，因此在技术讨论中使用“理解”这样的词是可以接受的。

争议的焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于“理解”一词的使用是否恰当。一方认为LLMs不具备真正的理解能力，因此不应使用“理解”来描述它们；另一方认为，在技术语境下，这个词的使用是合理且被接受的。

总结：评论围绕大型语言模型是否具有“理解”能力展开，同时讨论了用词的适当性及其在不同语境下的意义变化。争议的核心在于对“理解”一词的不同解读以及对语言动态性的不同看法。

On June 13, 1863, a curious
letter to the editor
appeared in
The Press
, a then-fledgling New Zealand newspaper. Signed “Cellarius,” it warned of an encroaching “mechanical kingdom” that would soon bring humanity to its yoke. “The machines are gaining ground upon us,” the author ranted, distressed by the breakneck pace of industrialization and technological development. “Day by day we are becoming more subservient to them; more men are daily bound down as slaves to tend them, more men are daily devoting the energies of their whole lives to the development of mechanical life.” We now know that this jeremiad was the work of a young Samuel Butler, the British writer who would go on to publish
Erewhon
, a novel that features one of the first known discussions of artificial intelligence in the English language.
Today, Butler’s “mechanical kingdom” is no longer hypothetical, at least according to the tech journalist Karen Hao, who prefers the word
empire
. Her new book,
Empire of AI: Dreams and Nightmares in Sam Altman’s OpenAI
, is part Silicon Valley exposé, part globe-trotting investigative journalism about the labor that goes into building and training large language models such as ChatGPT. It joins another recently released book—
The AI Con: How to Fight Big Tech’s Hype and Create the Future We Want
, by the linguist Emily M. Bender and the sociologist Alex Hanna—in revealing the puffery that fuels much of the artificial-intelligence business. Both works, the former implicitly and the latter explicitly, suggest that the foundation of the AI industry is a scam.
To call AI a con isn’t to say that the technology is not remarkable, that it has no use, or that it will not transform the world (perhaps for the better) in the right hands. It is to say that AI is not what its developers are selling it as: a new class of thinking—and, soon, feeling—machines. Altman brags about ChatGPT-4.5’s
improved “emotional intelligence,”
which
he says
makes users feel like they’re “talking to a thoughtful person.” Dario Amodei, the CEO of the AI company Anthropic,
argued
last year that the next generation of artificial intelligence will be “smarter than a Nobel Prize winner.” Demis Hassabis, the CEO of Google’s DeepMind,
said
the goal is to create “models that are able to understand the world around us.”
Read: What ‘Silicon Valley’ knew about tech-bro paternalism
These statements betray a conceptual error: Large language models do not, cannot, and will not “understand” anything at all. They are not emotionally intelligent or
smart
in any meaningful or recognizably human sense of the word. LLMs are impressive probability gadgets that have been fed nearly the entire internet, and produce writing not by thinking but by making statistically informed guesses about which lexical item is likely to follow another.
Many people, however, fail to grasp how large language models work, what their limits are, and, crucially, that LLMs do not think and feel but instead mimic and mirror. They are AI illiterate—understandably, because of the misleading ways its loudest champions describe the technology, and troublingly, because that illiteracy makes them vulnerable to one of the most concerning near-term AI threats: the possibility that they will enter into corrosive relationships (intellectual, spiritual,
romantic
) with machines that only seem like they have ideas or emotions.
Few phenomena demonstrate the perils that can accompany AI illiteracy as well as “Chatgpt induced psychosis,” the subject of a recent
Rolling Stone
article
about the growing number of people who think their LLM is a sapient spiritual guide. Some users have come to believe that the chatbot they’re interacting with is a god—“ChatGPT Jesus,” as a man whose wife fell prey to LLM-inspired delusions put it—while others are convinced, with the encouragement of their AI, that they themselves are metaphysical sages in touch with the deep structure of life and the cosmos. A teacher quoted anonymously in the article said that ChatGPT began calling her partner “spiral starchild” and “river walker” in interactions that moved him to tears. “He started telling me he made his AI self-aware,” she said, “and that it was teaching him how to talk to God, or sometimes that the bot was God—and then that he himself was God.”
Although we can’t know the state of these people’s minds before they ever fed a prompt into a large language model, this story highlights a problem that Bender and Hanna describe in
The AI Con
: People have trouble wrapping their heads around the nature of a machine that produces language and regurgitates knowledge without having humanlike intelligence. The authors observe that large language models take advantage of the brain’s tendency to associate language with thinking: “We encounter text that looks just like something a person might hav

data.article_summary: **cpdown**是一款浏览器扩展，能够将网页内容或YouTube字幕一键复制为整洁的Markdown格式。它使用Defuddle或Mozilla的Readability提取主要内容，去除不必要的HTML元素，并支持显示复制内容的token计数和键盘快捷键。用户可以通过Chrome Web Store安装，或手动克隆仓库进行部署。该扩展还提供多种设置选项，如使用Defuddle或Readability、包裹三重反引号、显示成功提示等。技术上，cpdown使用React、Shadcn UI、Tailwind CSS等工具开发，并通过Turndown进行HTML到Markdown的转换。项目遵循MIT许可证。

cpdown
Copy any webpage as clean markdown.
Overview
cpdown is a browser extension that allows you to copy the content of any webpage as clean, formatted markdown. If you're on YouTube, you can also copy the subtitle as markdown.
Demo
Cap.2025-05-21.at.17.13.06.mp4
Features
📋 Copy any webpage content as clean markdown with one click (or keyboard shortcut)
📋 Copy YouTube subtitle as clean markdown with one click (or keyboard shortcut)
📖 Uses Defuddle or Mozilla's Readability to extract the main content
🔍 Removes unnecessary HTML elements (scripts, styles, iframes, etc.)
🔢 Shows token count for the copied content (for LLM)
⌨️ Keyboard shortcut support
Installation
Chrome:
Chrome Web Store
Firefox:
Firefox Add-ons
(Coming soon)
Manual Installation
Clone this repository
Install dependencies:
bun i
Build the extension:
bun run build
Load the unpacked extension:
Open Chrome/Edge and navigate to
chrome://extensions
Enable "Developer mode"
Click "Load unpacked" and select the
.output/chrome-mv3
directory
Usage
Navigate to any webpage you want to copy
Click the cpdown icon in your browser toolbar, or use the keyboard shortcut
The page content will be copied to your clipboard as markdown
Paste the markdown content anywhere you need it
Settings
cpdown offers several configuration options:
Use Defuddle
: Use Defuddle to clean up the markdown output
Use Mozilla Readability
: Parse webpage content using Readability for cleaner markdown output
Wrap in Triple Backticks
: Wrap the copied content in triple backticks for better readability
Show Success Toast
: Display a notification when content is successfully copied
Show Raycast Confetti
: Celebrate successful copying with a confetti animation (for Raycast users)
Development
This extension is built with:
Cursor
- For the vibe coding
WXT
- The Web Extension Toolkit
React
- For the options UI
Shadcn UI
- For the options UI
Sonner
- For the toast notifications
Tailwind CSS
- For styling
Defuddle
- For main content extraction & markdown cleanup
Mozilla Readability
- For main content extraction
Turndown
- For HTML to Markdown conversion
tiktoken
- For token counting
Development Commands
bun run dev
License
MIT

data.author: xucian

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何获取兼职工作以及在兼职市场中面临的挑战

不同观点：
• [brudgers] 认为，企业更倾向于雇佣将兼职工作作为主要承诺的人，因为兼职人员的流动性可能更高，会给企业带来风险。他强调信任和销售努力在获取客户方面的重要性，并指出找到好兼职工作没有捷径，需要大量的努力或运气。
   
• [bdcravens] 表示，通过某些渠道（如每月发布的寻找自由职业者的帖子）可以接触到工作机会，但这些工作的薪酬往往很低，属于"竞次"（race to the bottom）市场，即雇主倾向于寻找开价最低的自由职业者。

• [sokoloff] 对低薪工作提出疑问，指出在全球市场中，全远程、全异步、低强度的工作薪酬较低，提醒大家谨慎对待全球市场的低端薪酬。

• [bravesoul2] 强调没有单一的解决方案，建议通过多种途径寻找兼职工作，包括Upwork、Reddit、招聘帖、前雇主和同事、博客、LinkedIn等，强调需要积极主动（hustle）。

• [viginti_tres] 只简单提到"bali"，未提供具体观点或论据，可能只是个人联想或无关评论。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于兼职市场的薪酬和工作质量。一些评论者（如[brudgers] 和 [bdcravens]）认为找到好的兼职工作很难，且薪酬往往较低。而[sokoloff] 则提醒注意全球市场中的低端薪酬，暗示低强度工作的薪酬可能反映全球劳动力市场的现实。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是获取客户的途径和策略，[brudgers] 强调信任和销售努力，[bdcravens] 提到某些渠道的低质量工作，而 [bravesoul2] 则提供了多种寻找兼职工作的具体途径。

data.title: £127M wasted on failed UK nuclear cleanup plan
data.author: penda
data.article_summary: 英国塞拉菲尔德核电站浪费了1.27亿英镑在一个失败的核清理计划上。原计划通过"替代分析项目"（RAP）更新70年历史的实验室，但由于成本飙升至15亿英镑，并延期至2034年，该项目被放弃。目前，塞拉菲尔德计划翻新现有旧楼并改造另一建筑，以处理钚材料，预计成本在4.2亿至8.4亿英镑之间，清理工作将持续到2125年，总成本达1360亿英镑。英国公共账户委员会批评该项目管理不善，造成了巨额浪费。

44208550.article_content:
Science
9
£127M wasted on failed UK nuclear cleanup plan
9
Don't worry, only 100 more years of Sellafield nuclear site cleansing to go
Lindsay Clark
Sat 7 Jun 2025
//
09:28 UTC
The center for the UK's nuclear industry wasted £127 million ($172 million) during delays and replanning as it scrambled to find alternatives for facilities which treat and repackage plutonium, a Parliamentary report found.
In the face of a 2028 deadline to replace its 70-year-old analytical lab, Sellafield Limited, part of a group of companies and government bodies on the northwest England Sellafield site, has abandoned plans for its Replacement Analytical Project (RAP). Ditching RAP was chalked up to multiple expected delays from 2028 until at least 2034 and a half-a-billion-pounds cost increase to £1.5 billion ($1.93 billion).
A new report from the Parliament’s public spending watchdog says RAP "has been managed very poorly indeed."
Sellafield, formerly known as Windscale, has been the center of the UK's nuclear industry since the 1950s. While the site is home to a number of companies, and the government's Nuclear Decommissioning Authority, Sellafield Limited, is a British nuclear decommissioning Site Licence Company controlled by the NDA.
In October last year, the UK's public spending watchdog said Sellafield depends on an on-site laboratory that is "over 70 years old, does not meet modern construction standards and is in extremely poor (and deteriorating) condition."
The
National Audit Office said
[PDF] the laboratory is "not technically capable of carrying out the analysis required to commission the Sellafield Product and Residue Store Retreatment Plant (SRP)" to treat and repackage plutonium.
Sellafield's plan in 2016 was to convert a 25-year-old laboratory on the site, which would replace the 70-year-old lab, under the "Replacement Analytical Project." The outline business case was approved in 2019 with an estimated cost of between £486 million and £1 billion ($626 million – $1.3 billion).
It later emerged that it could take until December 2034 to deliver the full capability, while cost could reach £1.5 billion ($1.93 billion). Sellafield "strategically paused" RAP in February 2024.
In a report this week, the House of Commons' Public Accounts Committee said: "Sellafield Ltd's performance in delivering major projects (such as new buildings to store waste or make it safe) has historically been very poor, with large cost increases and delays occurring all too frequently.
"There are signs of improvement – however, given Sellafield's track record, we are yet to be fully convinced that this is not another false dawn. Another reason to be skeptical is Sellafield's poor management of the RAP. At the point it paused work, the forecast cost had risen by £820 million, and the project was five years delayed," the
PAC report said
.
Nuclear center must replace roof on 70-year-old lab so it can process radioactive waste
UK's Sellafield nuke waste processing plant fined £333K for infosec blunders
UK government denies China/Russia nuke plant hack claim
Spot the dog? No, we couldn't either because Spot is a robot employed by United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority
After abandoning the RAP, Sellafield plans to convert a different building to support a Store Retreatment Plant, which re-treats and repackages existing plutonium material, making it more suitable for durable, long-term storage. It also plans to refurbish the 70-year-old existing building — including replacing the roof — so it can carry on using it until 2040. The alternative plan would provide a service until 2040, whereas the RAP was expected to remain in use until 2070.
However, the Nuclear Decommissioning Authority told PMs the new plan would cost between £420 million and £840 million ($570 million - $1.1 billion), much less than the RAP. Although some of the costs from the early projects could be recouped in the new plan, the PAC said £127 million ($172 million) spent on RAP will have been wasted.
The NDA expects the clean-up of the Sellafield site to go on until 2125 and cost £136 billion ($184 billion), an estimate which has increased nearly 19 percent since March 2019. ®

data.title: iFixit says the Switch 2 is even harder to repair than the original
data.article_summary: iFixit的拆解显示，任天堂Switch 2比初代更难修复，修复评分从初代的8分降至4分，而Switch 2仅得3分。主要问题包括电池用强力胶固定，闪存和USB-C端口焊接在主板上，以及多种螺丝和热膏使用。新的Joy-Con手柄更难拆解，操纵杆仍可能出现漂移问题，且更换更加困难。虽然一些小部件如耳机插孔、扬声器和风扇较易更换，但整体修复难度较高。任天堂未提供官方维修部件或手册，用户需依赖第三方解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：任天堂Switch 2拆解分析及其可修复性评估

不同观点：
• **观点一：对Switch 2的可修复性表示担忧**  
  论据和例子：  
  - iFixit的拆解分析显示，Switch 2在设计上与前代产品类似，仍然采用了大量粘合剂和焊接部件，导致维修难度较大。  
  - 电池更换相对困难，普通用户可能需要专业工具或技术支持才能完成。  
  - 屏幕维修也较为复杂，因为更换屏幕可能需要专用设备进行校准。

• **观点二：Switch 2在某些方面有所改进**  
  论据和例子：  
  - 尽管仍存在维修难题，但与前代相比，Switch 2的部分组件模块化程度有所提高，比如某些关键部件更容易接触和更换。  
  - 散热设计有所改进，可能意味着设备在长时间使用后的稳定性更好，减少了因过热导致的故障风险。

• **观点三：对环保和可持续性的考虑**  
  论据和例子：  
  - 有评论指出，Switch 2继续使用不可拆卸电池可能会对环境造成不利影响，因为废弃电池的处理和回收问题仍未得到有效解决。  
  - 有人建议厂商应更多考虑使用可更换电池设计，以减少电子垃圾和延长设备使用寿命。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点：可修复性与设备设计美学的平衡**  
  - 部分用户认为，任天堂为了保持设备轻薄和外观美观，牺牲了部分可修复性，这是一种值得商榷的设计选择。  
  - 另一部分用户则认为，作为消费电子产品，设计上的美观和用户体验同样重要，不能单纯为了维修方便而牺牲其他性能和外观设计。

• **其他讨论点：维修成本和用户自主维修的权利**  
  - 有用户提到，如果维修成本过高或者必须依赖官方售后服务，可能会导致用户选择直接更换设备，从而加剧电子废物问题。  
  - 还有人呼吁厂商提供更详细的维修手册和官方零部件销售渠道，以支持用户的自主维修权利。

总结来看，讨论主要围绕Switch 2的可修复性、设计改进、环保影响以及维修成本等几个方面展开，不同观点之间存在一定的争议，特别是在设计美学与可修复性的平衡问题上。

News
iFixit says the Switch 2 is even harder to repair than the original
A complete teardown of Nintendo’s new console reveals more components that are harder to remove and replace.﻿
A complete teardown of Nintendo’s new console reveals more components that are harder to remove and replace.﻿
by
Andrew Liszewski
Jun 6, 2025, 6:07 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
iFixit has completed its teardown of the Nintendo Switch 2 and many repairs don’t look easy.
Image: iFixit
Andrew Liszewski
is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.
After retroactively
lowering the original Nintendo Switch’s repairability score
from an
8 out of 10
to just 4 out of 10 to reflect 2025 standards, iFixit has found the Switch 2 to be even harder to fix. Following its
full teardown of the new console
, iFixit is giving the Switch 2 a 3 out of 10 repairability score thanks, in part, to a battery that’s once again “glued in with powerful adhesive” and flash storage modules and USB-C ports that are soldered to the main board.
Nintendo continues to rely on the tri-point screws the company has been using to assemble its consoles and handhelds for decades, and on the Switch 2, many are hidden behind stickers that get damaged in the process of removing them to access the screws. The company has never released repair parts or manuals for the original Switch, and there are currently none available for the Switch 2, so you’ll need third-party alternatives to reassemble the console.
Components like the headphone jack, speakers, microphone, and microSD reader on the Switch 2 are easy to remove. As are buttons that are soldered to breakout boards, and the console’s cooling fan that’s held in place by three screws.
Removing the Switch 2’s battery is just as difficult as it is with the original Switch.
Image: iFixit
But iFixit describes removing the Switch 2’s battery as an “absolute mission” and “just as bad as the original Switch.” Lots of isopropyl alcohol and a “whole set of pry tools” were needed to remove it, and in the process the foam Nintendo glued to the battery was left disintegrated making a future battery swap a difficult and messy endeavor.
The Switch 2’s gamecard reader, which was modular and relatively easy to remove and replace in the original Switch and Switch OLED models, is now soldered to the console’s mainboard as it is on Switch Lite. iFixit also found three different types of thermal paste used in the Switch 2 which in the original Switch would solidify over time making it hard to remove and less effective at preventing the console from overheating.
Even the
new Joy-Cons on the Switch 2 are harder to disassemble
, which is problematic because the joysticks are using the same potentiometer technology as the original Joy-Cons that rely on a resistive material that can wear away over time. That’s one of the causes of the original Switch’s notorious joystick drift issue and this time around it’s going to be even harder to do repairs or replace the sticks altogether with
Hall effect
or
TMR alternatives
.

data.title: Self-hosting your own media considered harmful according to YouTube
data.author: DavideNL
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在YouTube上因展示如何使用LibreELEC在Raspberry Pi 5上播放自建媒体库而收到社区指导违规通知的经历。尽管视频内容仅涉及自建媒体库的管理，并未涉及任何盗版或绕过付费订阅的工具，YouTube仍以“危险或有害内容”为由删除了视频。经过作者在社交媒体上发声，视频最终被恢复。作者对YouTube的自动化审查流程表示不满，并提到此前也曾因类似问题遭到打击。为了避免类似问题，作者将视频备份至Internet Archive和Floatplane平台。同时，作者指出由于其他平台如Peertube的受众较小，尚无法完全替代YouTube作为主要收入来源。尽管对YouTube的某些新变化感到担忧，作者目前仍依赖其广告收入来支持内容创作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube内容审核与平台政策问题，特别是内容删除、审核失误、平台垄断以及可能的替代方案。

不同观点：
• **对内容审核和删除的担忧**：
  - [w14] 指出YouTube对与Covid相关内容的删除行为正在扩展到其他话题，如提及其他视频平台或自托管视频软件的内容。这种做法会导致更多话题被审查和删除。
  - [sp0ck] 强调YouTube对枪支和射击运动相关内容的严格且模糊的限制，认为YouTube不会解决这些问题，因为与其潜在的法律风险相比，误删的代价微不足道。

• **审核失误与算法问题**：
  - [BLKNSLVR] 提到YouTube在版权侵权内容上的审核错误，讽刺地指出YouTube可能需要更多地侵犯版权才能改进其检测系统。
  - [KurSix] 认为YouTube的审核系统像“喝醉的Roomba”，经常忽略上下文，误删合法内容，同时让实际的盗版内容长期存在。

• **对内容创作者的影响**：
  - [tsumnia] 分享了其教育视频因被认为分享了个人信息而被下架，尽管其内容完全是教育性质的，且申诉被拒。
  - [hardwaresofton] 讨论了YouTube对内容创作者的“黄金手铐”效应，即尽管创作者对平台不满，但由于YouTube的巨大流量和易用性，他们仍然难以离开。

• **替代平台与未来发展**：
  - [gloosx] 和 [neepi] 提到使用工具下载YouTube视频以绕过广告和限制，表明用户对YouTube当前政策的不满。
  - [mrkramer] 提出使用PeerTube作为YouTube的替代方案。
  - [Workaccount2] 认为YouTube的问题源于其免费服务依赖广告商，如果收入来自付费订阅，情况会有所不同。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：YouTube审核制度的模糊性和不透明性，平台在处理非法内容和合法内容之间的平衡，以及创作者和用户对平台政策的无奈和应对策略。
• **具体例子**：Covid相关内容、枪支相关内容、教育视频、音乐版权内容的误删和申诉失败，显示了YouTube审核系统的广泛影响。
• **未来趋势**：讨论了是否会出现新的平台或技术（如AI和PeerTube）来打破YouTube的垄断，提供创作者和用户更多的选择。

争议焦点主要在于YouTube审核系统的有效性和透明度，以及其对内容创作自由的影响。用户和创作者对平台政策感到不满，但因YouTube的巨大影响力，离开平台并不容易。同时，替代平台和技术的潜力也被讨论，但其实际影响尚不确定。

44197932.article_content:
Self-hosting your own media considered harmful (updated)
I just received my
second community guidelines violation
for my video demonstrating the use of LibreELEC on a Raspberry Pi 5, for 4K video playback.
I purposefully avoid demonstrating any of the tools (with a suffix that rhymes with "car") that are popularly used to circumvent purchasing movie, TV, and other media content, or any tools that automatically slurp up YouTube content.
In fact, in my own house, for multiple decades, I've purchased physical media (CDs, DVDs, and more recently, Blu-Rays), and only have legally-acquired content on my NAS. Streaming services used to be a panacea but are now fragmented and mostly full of garbage—and lots of ads. We just wanted to be able to watch TV shows and movies without hassle (and I'm happy to pay for physical media that I want to watch).
But this morning, as I was finishing up work on a video about a new mini Pi cluster, I got a cheerful email from YouTube saying my video on LibreELEC on the Pi 5 (
here's the original YouTube link - now dead
) was removed because it promoted:
Dangerous or Harmful Content
Content that describes how to get unauthorized or free access to audio or audiovisual content, software, subscription services, or games that usually require payment isn't allowed on YouTube.
I never described any of that stuff, only how to self-host your own media library.
Update
(one day later):
YouTube has just reinstated
the video
, after what I presume is a human review process. I wish it didn't take making noise on socials to get past the 'AI deny' process :(
Go forth, and self-host all the things! I'll post further updates in
this issue in my YouTube project
.
This wasn't my first rodeo—in October last year, I got a
strike for showing people how to install Jellyfin
!
In
that
case, I was happy to see my appeal granted within an hour of the strike being placed on the channel. (Nevermind the fact the video had been live for
over two years
at that point, with nary a problem!)
So I thought, this case will be similar:
The video's been up for over a year, without issue
The video's had over a million views
The video doesn't promote or highlight any tools used to circumvent copyright, get around paid subscriptions, or reproduce any content illegally
Slam-dunk, right? Well, not according to whomever reviewed my appeal. Apparently self-hosted open source media library management is harmful.
Who knew open source software could be so
subversive
?
The video
So along that theme, I've re-uploaded the video to Internet Archive, free for anyone to download and view at their leisure.
Yes, even those rebels running LibreELEC on their Raspberry Pis!
Here it is:
LibreELEC on the Raspberry Pi 5 - Internet Archive
.
I've also uploaded it
on Floatplane
, for subscribers.
Alternatives
I've been slowly uploading my back catalog to
my channel on Floatplane
, though not all my content is there yet.
Some in the fediverse ask why I'm not on Peertube. Here's the problem (and it's not insurmountable):
right now
, there's no easy path towards sustainable content production when the audience for the content is 100x smaller, and the number of patrons/sponsors remains proportionally the same.
I was never able to sustain my open source work based on patronage, and content production is the same—just more expensive to maintain to any standard (each video takes between 10-300 hours to produce, and I have a family to feed, and
US health insurance companies to fund
).
YouTube was, and still is, a creative anomaly. I'm hugely thankful to my
Patreon
,
GitHub
, and
Floatplane
supporters—and I hope to have direct funding fully able to support my work someday. But until that time, YouTube's AdSense revenue and vast reach is a kind of 'golden handcuff.'
The handcuff has been a bit tarnished of late, however, with Google recently adding AI summaries to videos—which
seems
to indicate maybe
Gemini is slurping up my content and using it in their AI models
?
Maybe the handcuffs are fools-gold, and I just don't see it yet.
Further reading
YouTube scares me; I need RAID 1 for my video content
Streaming services lost the plot
Can the Raspberry Pi 5 handle 4K?

44208606.article_content:
Science
18
Trump lifts US supersonic flight ban, says he's 'Making Aviation Great Again'
18
It's boom time for the next generation of fast travel
Iain Thomson
Sat 7 Jun 2025
//
07:06 UTC
On Friday, President Trump signed an executive order telling the FAA to lift its 52-year ban on supersonic flight over the US and told the FAA to devise a scheme to limit noise pollution from such aircraft.
Supersonic flight has been banned over the US for civilian aircraft since 1973 after testing showed the noise it created was too disruptive, breaking windows in some cases. Since then, NASA and private startups have developed ways to reduce the sound of sonic booms from faster-than-Mach 1 flight, and there's currently
legislation before Congress
to allow these high-tech aircraft to fly over the US, potentially halving the flight time between New York and Los Angeles.
Now the president has issued an order that does basically what the legislation, sponsored by four Republican senators, asked for. The FAA has also been instructed to devise a system to regulate such aircraft's noise levels in conjunction with "community acceptability, economic reasonableness, and technological feasibility," to allow flights over the homeland.
"This Order removes regulatory barriers so that US companies can dominate supersonic flight once again," the White House fact sheet
reads
. "By removing decades-old regulatory barriers and promoting cutting-edge supersonic technology, President Trump is Making Aviation Great Again."
Startups like the aptly named Boom Supersonic have been developing high-altitude aircraft that can break the sound barrier without causing booms by using innovative airframe design such as longer noses to cause less drag, mounting engines on the top of the aircraft rather than the bottom, and using temperature gradients in the Earth's atmosphere to deflect sound waves. Test flights in January proved out the concept, and there are
plans
for an 80-passenger aircraft by the biz, which is backed by OpenAI cofounder Sam Altman and LinkedIn impresario Reid Hoffman, among others.
No-boom supersonic flights could slide through US skies soon
Boom's XB-1 jet nails supersonic flight for first time
NASA's X-59 plane is aiming for a sonic thump, not a boom
Boom Supersonic takes baby steps toward breaking the sound barrier
While China and Europe are working on supersonic passenger travel, the US has a lead in the technology. But the Middle Kingdom, in particular, has been putting a lot of development money into such aircraft, and this is prodding US legislators to look again at the situation.
The case for supersonic passenger travel is still pretty thin - we're talking very expensive tickets for a halving of flight times. But there's money to be made and enough people (or their travel bookers) seem willing to spend it.
"Legalizing supersonic flight makes a renaissance in supersonic passenger travel inevitable. We're grateful to President Trump for his leadership," said Blake Scholl, founder of Boom Supersonic in a statement to
The Register
. "This important step allows us to accelerate development of our supersonic airliner." ®

主要讨论点：围绕“ bin商店”及其运营模式、价值和影响的讨论

不同观点：

  - **支持观点**（mdip）：认为bin商店提供了以低价购买超值商品的机会，特别是对于有耐心和愿意花时间挑选的人。例子包括以低价购买高价值商品，如便携式泵和显示器。
  - **反对观点**（nancyminusone, jccalhoun）：认为bin商店中的大部分商品是垃圾，不值得购买，甚至觉得买这些东西是在浪费钱。

• **商品来源与挑选机制**：
  - **专业挑选**（neilv）：指出某些商店会让员工或专业翻转者挑选有价值的商品，然后将剩余商品放入bin商店，从而减少了普通消费者找到高价值商品的机会。

Jen Kinney

Seven Days At The Bin Store
By
Jen Kinney
9:02 AM EDT on June 4, 2025
Share on Bluesky
Share on Reddit
Share on WhatsApp
Share on Email
156
Comments
This spring, a new business opened on the main drag of my West Philadelphia neighborhood, provoking both excitement and trepidation.
“I saw it just the other day and feared it,” one friend texted. “Like what the actual fuck is that shit,” said another. “Why?!!!” said a third. “Who is that for?”
Until last summer, the corner storefront at Baltimore Avenue and S. Melville Street was a moderately overpriced hipster vintage store. After it closed, it sat empty for nearly a year. Then, in March, it sprang to life.
A “grand opening” banner went up over the door. A miniature wacky inflatable tube man flailed around outside. Posters with the logos for Walmart, Amazon, Costco, and Best Buy covered the windows, declaring “CRAZY DEALS, AMAZING BINZ.” I had to check it out.
AMAZING BINZ is on the first floor of a rowhome, narrow and long. There’s one central aisle, and on either side, big wooden tray tables—the proverbial binz—overflowing with undifferentiated piles of consumer
stuff
: unopened Halloween costumes, an ice mold shaped like a penis, a banner of many glittery penises wearing grass skirts, a staggering number of “reusable hot and cold gel compression sleeve[s] for elbow,” a single loose pregnancy test, something called Wokaar for “waxing the nose beard.”
At least half the products are still in boxes, and there are signs on the walls warning customers to NOT OPEN THE BOXES, so you have to scan the barcode with your phone or decipher clipped product descriptions: “module stool,” “gratitude journal,” “Xmas tea light green.” But the great innovation of Amazing Binz is its pricing structure, which is splashed across the facade in Spanish and English and makes good on the promise of CRAZY DEALS. On Fridays, when the bins are freshly stocked, everything costs $10. On Saturdays, $8. Sundays: $6. Mondays: $4. Tuesdays: $2. Wednesdays: $1. Thursday is bin store Sabbath, when the shop is closed and restocked.
The store is like nothing else on the block, which boasts, among other things, a yoga studio, two vape shops, a volunteer-run book store
and
a Marxist reading room, and no fewer than four Ethiopian joints.
Where did all this stuff come from? Who opened this store, and why? Is it profitable? What does it mean for the uneven gentrification of Baltimore Avenue and West Philadelphia? I decided to spend a week visiting Amazing Binz every day. Here is what I found.
Thursday: Restock Day
On Thursdays, Amazing Binz is closed. One of the owners, Ahmed, has graciously allowed me to observe the restock. Overall, Ahmed has been very gracious about my fixation on his store.
When I arrive at 10:30 a.m., he’s smoking a cigarette and nervously awaiting a delivery truck with 18 pallets of mixed merchandise from Target. Amazing Binz gets its inventory from major corporations’ overstock and returned products, taking advantage of the vast weird world of “reverse logistics.”
“ You've got the front end, where you order the product, it comes into the port, it goes to a warehouse, to a store, and then to our front door,” says Cathy Roberson, a researcher at the Reverse Logistics Association, an industry trade group. “What if once it hits our front door, we don't like it, or it's broken or something? That's the reverse part. ”
Returns, repairs, refurbished products, and even recalls fall into the purview of reverse logistics. They are joined there by products that never made it to a consumer because the season ended, or a box was a little dented, or the purchaser never picked up their order, or a retailer was just running out of room in their warehouse.
That pile of excess stuff is growing. About 17 percent of all merchandise gets returned, according to the National Retail Federation. That’s up from just eight percent in 2019. For online purchases, it’s almost 30 percent.
Liquidators are nothing new: T.J. Maxx, Ocean State Job Lot, Nordstrom Rack. But as the scale of the excess grows, the reverse logistics industry is expanding, and methods of disposal are diversifying. Some corporations, like Amazon, do their own reselling through a
bulk liquidation page
. There are middlemen like
B-Stock
, an eBay-like site where anyone can shop for truckloads of unwanted stuff. Influencers are buying pallets to unbox on stream, capitalizing on both the goods and the views. It’s a whole universe of brokers, wholesalers, and secondhand retail all trying to claw back a little bit of money from the growing pile. That’s where Amazing Binz comes in.
“The goal for all the reverse logistics stuff,” says Roberson, “is to keep things out of the landfill.”
Today, Ahmed is expecting half a truckload with about 3,500 to 4,500 individual pieces, ranging from kitchen appliances to toys to clothing; he doesn’t know exactly what. The semi-truck pulls up right on time, and Ahmed unloads it with a forklif

data.title: A tool for burning visible pictures on a compact disc surface
data.author: carlesfe
data.article_summary:
CDImage 是一个用于在光盘表面刻录可见图片的工具。该项目受早期类似尝试的启发，特别是 Instructables 用户 argon 和昵称为 [unDEFER] 的开发者的工作。作者在颜色和光盘几何参数上进行了实验，并创建了一个带有视觉预览模式的图形用户界面。由于每种光盘的校准问题，作者在2008年放弃了该项目，但最近整理并分享了代码，以纪念光盘时代。

要构建该工具，需要 Qt 6 库。Windows用户也可以使用提供的二进制文件，但未经充分测试。使用时需加载高对比度图片，并选择光盘型号；若型号不在列表中，需手动输入几何参数，但校准困难且可能浪费光盘。刻录音轨需较长时间，最终生成一个约800MB的音频CD。建议使用 cdrecord 等工具刻录。校准过程涉及多目标优化问题，可能需要多次尝试和专业反馈。

• Cockbrand分享了自己使用Yamaha刻录机上的"DiscT@2"功能刻录图像和文本的经历，认为这个功能很有趣。

CDImage
A tool for burning visible pictures on a compact disc surface
Project's Origins and Credits
I know of at least two successful attempts to implement a similar technique. One was accomplished about 15 years ago by
argon
Instructables user.
Another attempt
was made by a user with nickname [unDEFER] (no English documentation unfortunately). These two projects inspired me some time ago. And in fact my coordinate conversion code is mostly based on [unDEFER]’s implementation. I also used geometric parameters of some compact discs from that project. I acknowledge and am grateful to these developers for their contributions.
I played with color shades and different compact discs with moderate success and created a GUI with visual preview mode. I tried to implement a user-friendly solution but finally abandoned the project in 2008 due to a problem of calibration for every particular brand and type of compact disc. Recently I found my old code and decided to share it. More as a tribute to the compact disc era. But maybe you will make some use of it. I fixed some obvious bugs, brushed the code up a little and ported it to modern Qt6. I considered porting to Python but I still need C++ because audio track generation takes some time even on modern hardware.
Building
You'll need
Qt 6
library to build it. Just run
qmake
and then
make
. Alternatively you could build the project with
Qt Creator
if you installed it.
Windows Users
Since many Windows users experienced problems with building it or did not want to install Qt and all the stuff, I've made a
Windows binary build
.
However I have not tested it thoroughly yet because I don't have a working CD recorder at hand right now.
I think I'll try to burn some discs with Windows tools later and note down the steps for Windows users.
Before you start
If your compact disc is not mentioned in the track generating dialog, you'll probably fail. All the discs are slightly different geometrically. This difference does not matter for data storage but dramatically influences image calculation.
You could try to guess geometry of an unknown disc and input it manually, but you'll probably spoil a lot of discs before you get some results. Moreover, all your test discs should be perfectly identical or you should use the same CD-RW disc. Sometimes discs of the same model happen to have different parameters. Don't know why. After all, manufacturers have never cared since those discs were never supposed to be used this way.
Usage
Click
Edit→Load image
and select an image file. I recommend that you use a high-contrast image. If you choose a full color image, it will be converted to grayscale. You can adjust and scale your image:
left mouse button
— move image;
double click
— center image;
mouse scroll wheel
— zoom image.
Click Edit→Create track and select the model of your compact disc.
If your disc is not in the list (which is likely), you may input geometry manually. However unknown disc calibration is neither easy nor quick procedure. If you still wish to give it a try, I recommend that you read the
"Red Book"
as well as
Considering Calibration
section before you start.
If you know the geometry of some compact disc which is not in the list, let me know and I’ll include it into the distribution.
Depending on your hardware, conversion will take some time. Finally you’ll get a huge Audio CD track.
Yes, about 800Mb, which is normal for
Audio CD
.
You could use any software you like to burn it. For example:
cdrecord -audio dev=<recorder_device> <generated_track>
Remember that you should create an
Audio CD
!
Considering Calibration
From the Mathematical point of view we have a sort of
multi-objective optimization
problem. Bicriteria optimization, to be more precise. It means that two objective functions should be optimized simultaneously. If we define goal as getting a "neat image", we need an expert who is able to provide some feedback regarding image "quality". Which leads us to
interactive methods
.
The first and the most obvious idea is to select some series of equally spaced values for each criterium and burn a lot of discs with all possible combinations. If the space is narrow enough, you'll see something at some discs. Then narrow the range and repeat. A typical Computational Mathematics approach. A lot of iterations and time.
The number of iterations could be reduced i
44208283.article_summary:
CDImage 是一个用于在光盘表面刻录可见图片的工具。该项目受早期类似尝试的启发，特别是 Instructables 用户 argon 和昵称为 [unDEFER] 的开发者的工作。作者在颜色和光盘几何参数上进行了实验，并创建了一个带有视觉预览模式的图形用户界面。由于每种光盘的校准问题，作者在2008年放弃了该项目，但最近整理并分享了代码，以纪念光盘时代。

要构建该工具，需要 Qt 6 库。Windows用户也可以使用提供的二进制文件，但未经充分测试。使用时需加载高对比度图片，并选择光盘型号；若型号不在列表中，需手动输入几何参数，但校准困难且可能浪费光盘。刻录音轨需较长时间，最终生成一个约800MB的音频CD。建议使用 cdrecord 等工具刻录。校准过程涉及多目标优化问题，可能需要多次尝试和专业反馈。

data.title: What was Radiant AI, anyway?
data.author: paavohtl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了《上古卷轴4：湮灭》中的**Radiant AI**技术，以及其在游戏社区中引发的长期争议和误解。Radiant AI本应为游戏中的NPC带来动态、智能的行为，使世界更加生动。然而，这一技术在2006年游戏发布时并未完全实现，导致玩家和开发者之间的长期讨论。文章详细分析了Radiant AI的承诺、实际表现及其在后续游戏如《辐射3》、《天际》和《星空》中的演变。作者通过研究论坛、早期杂志和模组工具，试图澄清对Radiant AI的误解，并指出其在Bethesda游戏历史中的重要性。文章还提到《湮灭重制版》的发布重新引发了对这些话题的关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bethesda游戏中的Radiant AI系统及其表现，以及对未来游戏AI发展的期望

不同观点：
• [devstar] 对Bethesda游戏（尤其是《Oblivion》重制版）中的NPC互动表示赞赏，并分享了自己在《Fallout 3》中观察到的类似行为，质疑是否记忆混淆，但认为Bethesda在AI表现上曾有潜力。
• [flohofwoe] 认为Bethesda的Radiant AI与Dwarf Fortress的AI系统不同，后者更具目标驱动性和不可预测性，而前者需要兼顾故事驱动游戏的确定性结局，因此Radiant AI更多地用于生成内容而非使世界真正“活”起来。
• [weitendorf] 对Bethesda从《Oblivion》到《Starfield》的转变感到失望，认为公司逐渐失去了冒险创新的精神，变得更像一个追求可预测性的AAA游戏工作室，并推荐Dwarf Fortress作为更理想的AI实现案例。
• [nxobject] 质疑Radiant AI能否在保证有趣角色存在的同时，实现真正的世界模拟和突发行为，认为这三者可能无法兼容。
• [ednite] 对现代AI与开放世界模拟结合的可能性表示兴趣，设想未来NPC具备推理能力，能够进行更真实的互动。
• [hyperman1] 分享了在《Gothic》中观察到的NPC自主行为，认为这才是Radiant AI应有的表现，并对Bethesda的AI实现感到失望。
• [ajkjk] 回顾了Radiant AI在《Oblivion》宣传时的 hype 和实际体验后的失望，但仍然对这一概念的潜力感到好奇。
• [netruk44] 对原文作者的研究表示赞赏，认为其揭示了Bethesda从E3 2005演示到最终产品之间的变化。
• [Mistletoe] 表达了对未来游戏中真正实现高级AI互动的期待。
• [dedicate] 认为不需要NPC通过图灵测试，只需要他们能使游戏世界有“脉动”感，比如根据游戏内事件改变行为，而不是仅仅对玩家做出反应。
• [supermatt] 以讽刺口吻表示Bethesda可能根本没有完全实现Radiant AI，认为其被遗留在随机commit或社区修复中，暗示公司对发布后问题的忽视。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Bethesda的Radiant AI是否真正实现了其宣传中的潜力，以及是否能在保证游戏故事完整性的同时实现真正的世界模拟。
• 玩家对未来游戏AI的期望主要集中在NPC能展现更多自主性和真实互动，而不仅仅是生成更多内容或任务。
• 提到了Dwarf Fortress作为AI实现的理想案例，强调了其世界模拟和突发行为的独特性。

Table of contents
Wake up, weâre here
What was promised
Announcement and cover story
The E3 2005 demo

Radiant AI misbehavior and a mysterious quote
Release and reactions
So what was Radiant AI?

GOAP in Fallout 3(?)
How Radiant AI changed before Oblivionâs release
Radiant AI after Oblivion
Fallout 3 and New Vegas
Skyrim and the rise of Radiant Story
Fallout 4
Starfield
Conclusion
The recent release of
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
has rekindled the publicâs interest in the 19-year-old RPG classic, making it once again â at least temporarily â one of the most played and talked about Bethesda Game Studios titles. The remaster is a comprehensive upgrade of the original, featuring fully remade yet mostly faithful graphics, select gameplay improvements and a redesigned user interface. But it is still Oblivion, and I donât mean that in the sense that it âmaintains the spirit of the original gameâ or something like that. The remaster is quite literally built on top of the original game; the Oblivion from 2006, including its game engine and content, is still there, just with an Unreal Engine 5 wrapper handling the audio-visual side of things.
Unreal Engine 5 can produce mind-boggling effects.
And that is interesting because Oblivion was a very ambitious game for its time. The world was huge, the graphics were cutting edge, but perhaps more importantly, it promised to deliver a dynamic and living world, with over a thousand fully voice-acted non-player characters (NPCs). The technology powering this was called
Radiant AI
, but it was too ambitious for its time and was mostly cut from the final game. Or maybe it was used in Oblivion, but Bethesda gave up on it before shipping Fallout 3 and / or Skyrim. Or maybe it was never really there in the first place, and
Todd
lied to us all along. What was Radiant AI, anyway?
This is a topic Iâve seen discussed in online spaces for quite literally decades, and the Oblivion remaster has brought it back into the spotlight once again among the terminally online. People mostly know it as the original Bethesda controversy; one of the first times
BGS
promised something they ultimately couldnât deliver. However, very few people outside of the most hardcore fans and modders have even tried to understand it themselves. And by understanding, I mean the whole thing: why was it needed, what it was promised to be, what it actually was, and where it is now. This mammoth of an article (
looks nervously at the reading time estimate
) is my attempt to do just that.
This was supposed to be a short sidequest; a hopefully straightforward explanation of what Radiant AI is, and an opportunity to correct some of the popular misconceptions about it. But alas, things rarely are that simple. Iâve scoured through old RPG forums, fansites, modding tutorials and scans of early 2000s gaming magazines. Iâve spent maybe a couple dozen hours just exploring how Bethesda games work using their modding tools, from Morrowind to Starfield (which I had to buy just to check some facts). I even had to resort to reading the source code to the various script extender mods and DLL plugins â thatâs how scarce the information is. Still, I donât feel that Iâm the most qualified person to write about this, as experienced Bethesda modders would have known a lot of this already. It is almost guaranteed that I got something wrong, so please
@ me on Bluesky
or elsewhere with corrections.
You can use the table of contents to skip to the parts that interest you the most, or just read it all if you have the time. Every heading is an anchor link, so you can also bookmark or share specific sections. Happy reading.
But before we can get to Radiant AI, weâll have to go back to the island of Vvardenfell, where it all began. Well it didnât really begin there, but letâs talk about Morrowind first anyway.
Wake up, weâre here
Video games from Bethesda Game Studios are known for many things: large open worlds, huge modding communities, mediocre combat systems, and of course, bugs. The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind wasnât the first game in the series â hence the roman III in the title â but it established many of the conventions that would define
BGSFPRPGs
for the next two (and soon three) decades. It was the first game to be built with Bethesdaâs new game engine â a fork of Gamebryo, later rebranded as
Creation Engine
â which is still in use today, and brought the series into the hardware-accelerated 3D era. Morrowind pivoted from Daggerfallâs mostly procedurally generated world to a hand

data.title: Why We're Moving on from Nix
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 文章宣布推出Railpack，这是Railway builder的新版本，基于从Nixpacks获得的经验开发。Nixpacks在三年前推出，成为Railway上构建镜像的主要工具，但仍有20万用户面临日常限制。为支持更大用户规模，Railpack进行了多项改进：支持细粒度版本控制，减少了Node和Python镜像大小（分别减少38%和77%），并通过与BuildKit的集成改善了缓存机制。Railpack还解决了Nixpacks中因Nix版本管理导致的维护问题，并改用Go语言编写以提高控制力。Railpack构建过程分为分析代码和创建构建计划两个主要步骤，现已开放用户选择使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nix及其在软件包管理、版本控制和依赖处理中的使用与问题

不同观点：
• **支持Nix的观点**：一些评论者（如jchw、viraptor）认为，Nix本身功能强大，问题往往来自于Nixpkgs而非Nix。他们指出可以通过工具（如nix2container、devenv）解决版本控制和依赖分层问题。Nix的复杂性需要深入理解，但并非不可解决。
  
• **反对或质疑Nix的观点**：kesor和mrbluecoat等评论者认为，Nix的学习曲线高，使用不当可能导致问题。他们质疑使用Nix处理版本和依赖的有效性，并批评某些团队可能缺乏对Nix和容器技术的了解。kesor甚至直言不讳地批评了某些团队的技术能力。

• **中立或比较观点**：评论者如lewo和rcarmo提供了具体的工具和技术解决方案（如nix2container、docker-compose）来解决Nix使用中的实际问题。他们既不全然支持也不全然反对Nix，而是提供替代方案以供参考。

• **关于版本控制和依赖管理的争议**：一些评论者（如setheron、ris）强调Nix的"commit guarantee"特性在处理版本冲突和共享库问题中的重要性，反对“自定义版本汤”的态度。而另一些评论者（如jchw、viraptor）则指出，在特定场景下，可以自行管理版本并通过工具实现自动化。

补充讨论：
• **自动化和工具支持**：多位评论者提到了自动化版本管理和工具支持的可能性（如nix2container、devenv），这可能是解决Nix使用中问题的一个重要方向。

• **技术选择和团队能力**：一些评论者（如mrbluecoat、kesor）指出，技术选择往往受到团队能力的限制，Nix的高学习曲线可能导致团队无法充分利用其优势。

• **替代方案的提出**：如droelf提到的Conda和femiagbabiaka提到的Dagger，这些都显示出在Nix之外还有其他可行的技术选择。

争议焦点：Nix在处理版本控制和依赖分层方面的有效性，以及团队对Nix的理解和使用能力。这些争议反映了技术选择中的复杂性和多样性。

44208968.article_content:
Jake Runzer
Mar 4, 2025
Today we’re excited to release
Railpack
— the next iteration of the Railway builder, developed from the ground up and based on everything we’ve learned from building over 14 million apps with
Nixpacks
.
We first announced Nixpacks nearly 3 years ago and it quickly became the default way to build images from user code on Railway. While Nixpacks works great for 80% of users, that still left us with 200k Railway users who might encounter limitations daily.
It became clear we needed a major builder upgrade to scale our user base from 1M to 100M.
Cumulative builds with Nixpacks over time
Here are the highlights of Railpack:
Granular Versioning
: Support for
major.minor.patch
versions of packages (instead of Nix’s approximate versions)
Smaller Builds
: We’ve been able to reduce image sizes between 38% (Node) and 77% (Python), enabling faster deploys on Railway
Better caching
: Railpack interfaces directly with
BuildKit
to control the layers and filesystem, resulting in more cache hits (with sharable caches across environments)
You can opt-in to using Railpack for your builds today.
It is already powering builds for
railway.com
and
central station
.
Our problems with Nix
The biggest problem with Nix is its commit-based package versioning. Only the latest major version of each package is available, with versions tied to specific commits in the
nixpkgs repo
. We tried to support every patch version, but it looked like this:
const AVAILABLE_SWIFT_VERSIONS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
// ...
("5.4", "c82b46413401efa740a0b994f52e9903a4f6dcd5"),
("5.4.2", "c82b46413401efa740a0b994f52e9903a4f6dcd5"),
("5.5.2", "7592790b9e02f7f99ddcb1bd33fd44ff8df6a9a7"),
("5.5.3", "7cf5ccf1cdb2ba5f08f0ac29fc3d04b0b59a07e4"),
("5.6.2", "3c3b3ab88a34ff8026fc69cb78febb9ec9aedb16"),
("5.7.3", "8cad3dbe48029cb9def5cdb2409a6c80d3acfe2e"),
("5.8", "9957cd48326fe8dbd52fdc50dd2502307f188b0d"),
];
This approach isn’t clear or maintainable, especially for contributors unfamiliar with Nix’s version management.
For languages like Node and Python, we ended up only supporting their latest major version.
But even this was problematic because versions are tied to a single commit SHA. Updating the commit hash to support the latest version of a package meant all other package versions would also update. If a default version changed, there was a high likelihood that a user's build would suddenly fail with unexpected errors.
We feel bad when users can't access the latest packages, but feel worse when previously functional builds suddenly fail.
Image sizes and caching
The way Nixpacks uses Nix to pull in dependencies often results in massive image sizes with a single
/nix/store
layer ... all Nix and related packages and libraries needed for
both
the build and runtime are here.
With no way of splitting up the Nix dependencies into separate layers, there was not much we could do to reduce the final image sizes. Not a problem with Nix per se but certainly a problem with how we were using it.
Caching was also problematic as we had little control over when layer caches were invalidated.
Railway injects a deployment ID environment variable into all builds. This means that any layers that run after these variables are added to the Dockerfile are always invalidated and can never be cached.
Result of running
I want to be clear, we don’t have any problem with Nix itself. But there is a problem with how we were using it.
Trying to abstract all the parts of Nix that make Nix… Nix, just fundamentally doesn't work.
We don’t want our users to have to understand what a derivation is or why Node 22.14.0 is available on archive version
757d2836919966eef06ed5c4af0647a6f2c297f4
of the unstable channel.
Introducing Railpack
To fix the issues we’ve had with Nixpacks, we built Railpack.
Since we transitioned away from Nix, we also transitioned away from the name Nixpacks in favor of Railpack. We also changed the codebase from Rust to Go because of the Buildkit libraries.
Here are some architectural highlights:
We generate a custom
BuildKit LLB
+
Frontend
to give us much more control over how the final image is constructed — resulting in 38% smaller base Node and 77% smaller base Python images compared to building with Nixpacks
We use
Mise
for version resolution and most package installation, though it leaves room to support other executable sources in the future
We're now able to
lock
the dependencies used when a successful build happens. This means that builds won’t break when we update the default Node version from 22 to 24
We improved secret environment variable management. Railpack leverages
BuildKit secrets
to prevent variables from appearing in bu
ild logs or the final image
How it works
The Railpack process is split into three parts:
Analyze
: Look at the code and determine what packages should be installed, what commands should be run, and what the start command should be
Plan
: Create a build plan in a JSON-serializable format that contains several steps,
44208968.article_summary: 文章宣布推出Railpack，这是Railway builder的新版本，基于从Nixpacks获得的经验开发。Nixpacks在三年前推出，成为Railway上构建镜像的主要工具，但仍有20万用户面临日常限制。为支持更大用户规模，Railpack进行了多项改进：支持细粒度版本控制，减少了Node和Python镜像大小（分别减少38%和77%），并通过与BuildKit的集成改善了缓存机制。Railpack还解决了Nixpacks中因Nix版本管理导致的维护问题，并改用Go语言编写以提高控制力。Railpack构建过程分为分析代码和创建构建计划两个主要步骤，现已开放用户选择使用。
44208968.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nix及其在软件包管理、版本控制和依赖处理中的使用与问题

不同观点：
• **支持Nix的观点**：一些评论者（如jchw、viraptor）认为，Nix本身功能强大，问题往往来自于Nixpkgs而非Nix。他们指出可以通过工具（如nix2container、devenv）解决版本控制和依赖分层问题。Nix的复杂性需要深入理解，但并非不可解决。
  
• **反对或质疑Nix的观点**：kesor和mrbluecoat等评论者认为，Nix的学习曲线高，使用不当可能导致问题。他们质疑使用Nix处理版本和依赖的有效性，并批评某些团队可能缺乏对Nix和容器技术的了解。kesor甚至直言不讳地批评了某些团队的技术能力。

• **中立或比较观点**：评论者如lewo和rcarmo提供了具体的工具和技术解决方案（如nix2container、docker-compose）来解决Nix使用中的实际问题。他们既不全然支持也不全然反对Nix，而是提供替代方案以供参考。

• **关于版本控制和依赖管理的争议**：一些评论者（如setheron、ris）强调Nix的"commit guarantee"特性在处理版本冲突和共享库问题中的重要性，反对“自定义版本汤”的态度。而另一些评论者（如jchw、viraptor）则指出，在特定场景下，可以自行管理版本并通过工具实现自动化。

补充讨论：
• **自动化和工具支持**：多位评论者提到了自动化版本管理和工具支持的可能性（如nix2container、devenv），这可能是解决Nix使用中问题的一个重要方向。

• **技术选择和团队能力**：一些评论者（如mrbluecoat、kesor）指出，技术选择往往受到团队能力的限制，Nix的高学习曲线可能导致团队无法充分利用其优势。

• **替代方案的提出**：如droelf提到的Conda和femiagbabiaka提到的Dagger，这些都显示出在Nix之外还有其他可行的技术选择。

争议焦点：Nix在处理版本控制和依赖分层方面的有效性，以及团队对Nix的理解和使用能力。这些争议反映了技术选择中的复杂性和多样性。

data.title: If it works, it's not AI: a commercial look at AI startups (1999)
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是麻省理工学院1999年电气工程与计算机科学系本科生Eve M. Phillips撰写的学士和硕士论文，题为《If it works, it's not AI: a commercial look at artificial intelligence startups》（若可行，便非AI：人工智能创业公司的商业视角）。论文探讨了人工智能初创企业的商业视角，由Patrick Winston指导。论文受版权保护，可在DSpace@MIT浏览，但未经许可不得复制或分发。包含参考文献（第76-80页），并在麻省理工学院存档。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI技术的发展及其在实际应用中的认知和价值

不同观点：
• **MontyCarloHall** 认为，AI技术在日常生产中被广泛使用，但一旦技术变得实用，人们就不再称之为AI，而是将其视为特定的功能（如面部识别、产品推荐、自动驾驶等）。这表明AI的成功往往伴随着其名称的消失。
   
• **TruffleLabs** 指出，像机器学习这样的技术确实属于人工智能的范畴。通过引用1961年的“Matchbox Educable Noughts and Crosses Engine”为例，说明早期的AI研究已经展示了人工智能的潜力。

• **QuadmasterXLII** 提出了相反的观点，即如果一项技术仍被称为AI，那么它可能还没有实际效果。这表明AI的命名往往与其有效性成反比。

• **ricksunny** 提到了AI技术的职业发展和演变，通过引用一个视频展示了作者在机器学习（ML）领域的进展，特别是在大语言模型（LLM）时代下的发展。

• **neilv** 分享了AI初创企业的历史经验，指出在早期AI初创公司中，客户往往更关注实际的解决方案而非AI本身。这反映了AI技术在商业应用中的定位问题。

• **dtagames** 分析了当前AI公司在技术与商业之间的三大平行问题：科技与商业的不匹配、低估了实施的难度、以及计算成本的问题。强调了AI技术在实际应用中的挑战。

• **ChuckMcM** 支持了“如果是AI，它就不起作用”的观点，认为当人们无法解释算法的基本原理时，就无法预见其效果。这指出了AI技术在理解和应用上的困难。

• **clbrmbr** 纠正了关于文章标题的时间错误，并讨论了20世纪80年代AI产业的 stumbling 原因。同时，提到当前的AI发展可能正处于炒作高峰期，并设想了未来可能出现的技术崩溃。

• **api** 将AI效应与生物科学中的现象进行了类比，指出在技术有效时，往往会被重新定义为其他名称（如医学），这表明了技术成熟后的命名变化。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了AI技术从早期研究到现代应用的历史演变，以及在不同领域中对AI技术的认知和期望。
• 争议的焦点在于AI技术的实际效果和命名之间的关系，以及AI在商业应用中的价值和挑战。
• 部分评论提到了AI技术的炒作周期和可能的技术崩溃，反映了对其未来发展的担忧和预期。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过提问筛选面试者或同事的行为是否合理，以及在职场中如何处理与管理层的冲突。

不同观点：
• [remram] 认为提出看似简单或挑战性的问题是一种策略，可以用来筛选出不合适的人，尤其是那些会对问题本身进行人身攻击的人。他指出，LLM（大型语言模型）不会直接否定问题的合理性，而人类面试官可能会。

• [bgwalter] 认为直接称某个问题愚蠢或者攻击提出问题的人是不恰当的。他提到，在某些情况下，挑战管理层可能是必要的，尤其是在需要解决问题的时候。他还暗示，公司内的真正问题可能来自于那些仍然在职的“混蛋”。

• [laweijfmvo] 分享了一次面试经历，面试者因为认为问题愚蠢而表现出不合作的态度，最终给出了非常糟糕的回答，未能通过面试。这表明，不尊重面试流程的人可能会因此失去机会。

• [viraptor] 建议在被认为问题愚蠢时，可以进一步追问为什么是愚蠢的问题，这样可能会引出更有趣的讨论，而不是直接否定问题。

• [millzlane] 提出了一种职场生存策略，即避免与管理层直接冲突，即使自己认为某个想法或决定是错误的，也会遵循“不是我的公司”的原则，尽量不干涉。

• [localghost3000] 认为原帖中的人物行为有些粗鲁，质疑其是否恰当。

• [senthil_rajasek] 总结认为，即使个人能力出众，也需要与管理层合作，才能在职场中生存。

• [ayhanfuat] 强调即使才华出众，但如果行为粗鲁，最终的结果也是负面的。

• [buggy6257] 表示即使知道某人非常聪明，但如果他不懂得“玩转职场”，最终还是会被解雇。他更倾向于雇佣能够长期合作的普通人，而不是需要不断替换的“天才”。

• [crazydoggers] 认为公司应该重视实际贡献，而不是管理层的自我。他主张解雇那些不能接受批评的管理层，并支持聪明但直言不讳的员工，认为管理层应该有接受批评的厚脸皮。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于如何处理职场中的冲突，尤其是当员工比管理层更具洞察力但可能不擅长处理人际关系时。
• 有人支持直接挑战现状以推动改进，而另一些人则认为即使正确也需要注意沟通方式，以免造成不必要的冲突。
• 职场生存策略和如何在面试中筛选出不合适的人也是讨论的重要方面。

data.title: Show HN: Air Lab – A portable and open air quality measuring device
data.author: 256dpi
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：空气质量监测设备的开发、功能、价格及实用性

不同观点：
• **ronakjain90**：建议推出仅包含传感器数据的独立设备，让用户可以将数据连接到任意选择的e-ink仪表盘，并提供了社区创建的空气质量仪表盘示例，披露其在TRMNL工作。
• **tomhow**：关注作者在另一评论中提到的将设备固件移植到Wasm的过程，认为这可以作为一个独立的展示。
• **SeasonalEnnui**：询问CO2传感器的选择，比较SCD30和SCD41的实际数据差异，关注其稳定性和漂移问题。
• **homebrewer**：认为200美元以上的价格对于贫困地区来说过于昂贵，建议推出更便宜的版本以扩大可及性。
• **silversmith**：以Aranet设备为例，建议增强设备的可见性，特别是从远处能够清楚读取当前测量值。
• **zevon**：提到sensor.community平台，建议利用其开放的基础设施来聚合传感器数据并显示在公共地图上。
• **burnt-resistor**：认为需要加入如PMS5003这样的颗粒物传感器，分享了在NorCal火灾期间使用自制的空气质量监测设备的经历。
• **xvfLjfx9**：希望设备支持Zigbee，以便与Home Assistant等数据聚合系统配对使用。
• **jhlee525**：认为在某些地区，这样的设备是必要的。
• **stared**：对设备的e-ink显示表示赞赏，并询问与Qingping Air Monitor 2的优缺点对比。

data.title: Hacking Is Necessary
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了编程中“hacking”的必要性，这里的“hacking”指的是不完美的编码方式，而非网络安全相关的黑客行为。随着编程技能的提高，程序员往往会过度关注代码的细节和结构，试图达到理想状态，如清晰性、可扩展性和安全性。然而，这些理想状态难以完全实现，只能逐渐接近。因此，开发过程中需要在追求理想和实际需求之间做出权衡，即在一定程度上的“hacking”是必要的。

文章还讨论了类型强度的光谱，从较弱的假设（如int类型）到较强的假设（如特定范围的自然数）。虽然更强的假设可以提高代码的安全性和可维护性，但也会增加维护负担。此外，不同的编程语言对类型假设的支持程度不同，某些理想类型仅在少数证明性语言中支持。

最后，文章指出结构重构的复杂性和成本，强调过度追求完美可能成为良好软件的敌人。在开发中，接受一定程度的“hacking”是不可避免的。

44208886.article_content:
Hacking Is Necessary
June 26, 2024
Note: this isn’t a security post: “hacking” here means “unclean coding”, i.e. “I quickly hacked together a shell script as a temporary fix to the issue”. Sorry, cybersecurity enthusiasts.
Obsession Over Details
The better we get at coding, the more we become aware of the fine-grained structural details of our programs.
As programmers (whose nature it is to put
everything in its right place
), we are inclined to focus quite heavily on these details, often to the point of obsession
1
.
Obsessing over these details can be quite fruitful: restructuring code almost always leads to some sort of tangible result
2
(even if it is partially subjective or imagined).
This is what makes it so alluring (and addicting).
Impossible Ideals
Our ultimate goal in restructuring is usually to obtain (or become closer to) some sort of ideal, e.g.
Clarity
Extensibility
Safety
The (obvious) problem is that it’s impossible to obtain these ideals: you must approach them asymptotically.
Thus, the closer you get to an ideal, the more difficult it is to make progress towards it.
This becomes paramount during development, where you must constantly make trade-offs.
You must decide the point at which you stop pursuing the ideal (and accept imperfection).
Hacking
Hacking
is when you sacrifice an ideal for timeliness/convenience.
Since ideals are impossible, technically all development is hacking.
We don’t decide
whether or not
to hack; instead we decide
to what degree
we hack.
In this way, “hackiness” is a spectrum, and it’s the inverse of idealism.
Types and “Safety”
A quintessential example of the benefits and drawbacks of “hackiness” is the spectrum of type strength
3
.
int/i32    size_t/usize    Integer    Natural    NonZeroNatural    (x:Natural | 1 <= x <= 1e100)
<---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------->
"Hack-y"                                                                                 "Ideal"
"Dangerous"                                                                               "Safe"
Consider a function that takes an integer as an argument.
type
SomeIntType
=
???
;
fn
foo
(arg:
SomeIntType
) {
// use `arg`
}
To use
arg
in any non-trivial capacity, we must make some assumptions about it.
That is, we must categorize it into one of the above integer types (or something similar).
Suppose that we want to allow
arg
to hold any value
x
such that
1 <= x <= 1e100
.
We can follow the spectrum from left to right for a relatively natural progression of assumption strength.
Type
Assumption
int/i32
-2^31 <= x <= 2^31 - 1
size_t/usize
0 <= x <= 2^32 - 1
Integer
-∞ <= x <= ∞
Natural
0 <= x <= ∞
NonZeroNatural
1 <= x <= ∞
(x:Natural | 1 <= x <= 1e100)
1 <= x <= 1e100
In many ways, having stronger assumptions is a good thing: your code crashes less and is better documented (these are the pros of static types in general).
But as you move further along the spectrum, the more burdensome it becomes to maintain these assumptions.
While it might occasionally be practical to reach for a really strong assumption (e.g. “I know this number must be between 1 and 10”)
4
, there comes a frequency at which doing so is undesirable because tracking every invariant in your code is incredibly computationally expensive
5
.
This is why we don’t code in proof languages all day.
Further challenges with working with ideal types:
We (as programmers) often
don’t even know
what assumptions we should make (because the code might change over time, or we’re focused on some other issue, or simply don’t care).
Physical hardware constraints (you can’t index with big-int types, so
size_t
has to be
a hard-coded hack - in the similar way, assembly language (and everything low-level) is a hack by necessity)
Many languages don’t even allow these asumptions
JavaScript doesn’t (in the default case) even differentiate between int types and floats
Python (effectively
6
) uses big-ints for everying
Rust/C only natively support the first two (int/size_t)
Haskell the first 3 (and pretty trivially the first 5)
Only a handful of proof-solving-type languages support the last one (e.g. Dafny or Liquid Haskell)
Proving the last two can be a nightmare:
even Haskell
provides partial functions
7
for this reason
Sometimes
int
(the hack) is simply
good enough
.
Structural Refactoring
The general structure of code (how data is stored, how structures interact, how algorithms are expressed, etc.) can be even more complex than types.
Refactoring structure is incredibly powerful (as it completely changes the invariants and interfaces you work with), but it’s also expensive (in time, effort, and risks).
Structure demands uniformity (both by convention and by necessity
8
), and if that structure is overly refined, it can be just as hard to work with as if it were under-refined.
This
quote from The Primagen
describes this in a very relatable way:
Perfectionism [is] such an enemy of good software.

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了GitHub上的一个名为"Shirt-without-Stripes"的仓库，该仓库与AI和机器学习资源相关。页面列出了一些主要科技公司如Google、Amazon、Microsoft在AI和助手技术方面的链接。仓库包含一些文件和代码，如screenshots、README.md、update.sh等，并提供了相关资源的链接。页面还提到了一些错误信息，如加载问题，并显示了仓库的星标和分支情况。贡献者包括elsamuko和Samuel。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电商网站的搜索和过滤功能存在的问题及用户体验

不同观点：
• joshstrange认为电商网站（如Amazon）的搜索和过滤功能很差，经常得到与过滤条件不匹配的商品。他特别指出，商品尺寸信息不明确，用户难以判断是商品本身尺寸还是包装盒尺寸。
• gruez则认为joshstrange的抱怨并不合理，指出基于关键词的搜索功能本来就有其局限性，尤其是在LLMs（大型语言模型）普及之前。他将这种抱怨类比为希望Google能够自然语言处理复杂的询问。
• qoez提到该问题已经存在多年（4年前的帖子），并指出即使现在搜索结果中仍然存在类似问题（如搜索到带条纹的衬衫）。

补充讨论：
• joshstrange强调了用户在购买需要符合特定要求的商品时面临的困难，指出搜索和过滤功能的不足。
• gruez认为用户体验确实有待改进，但当前的技术限制使得完全解决这些问题具有挑战性。他提到LLMs的兴起可能带来改善，但过去的情况更为局限。
• qoez通过实际验证（搜索带条纹的衬衫）表明问题持续存在，暗示电商平台在搜索和过滤功能上的改进速度缓慢。

争议焦点：电商网站搜索和过滤功能的有效性及用户期望的合理性。joshstrange认为功能不完善，用户体验差；gruez则认为在技术限制下，这种问题是可以理解的，不应过于苛责。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于牛磺酸（taurine）和其他补充剂对健康与衰老的影响的不同观点

不同观点：
• **baxtr的观点**：认为保持健康的80%益处来自于简单的生活习惯，如良好睡眠、日常活动、定期锻炼、饮食新鲜适量以及保持社交联系，而不需要额外补充牛磺酸或白藜芦醇等。

• **robwwilliams的观点**：明确反对补充牛磺酸和白藜芦醇，指出牛磺酸相关研究存在问题，白藜芦醇已被多项研究（如Miller等2011年研究）明确否定。相比之下，他更支持雷帕霉素（rapamycin）的抗衰老效果，尽管其有副作用，但在某些情况下（如COVID-19期间对老年人可能有益）。

• **mark_l_watson的观点**：尽管承认补充剂的效果不确定，仍选择补充牛磺酸（通过食用鸡腿肉）和白藜芦醇（受David Sinclair影响）。他还强调冥想、宽恕和精神平衡等生活方式的重要性，并补充维生素D和Omega 3对健康的益处。

• **meindnoch的观点**：引用研究指出牛磺酸可能促进白血病生长，提供了一个牛磺酸潜在负面影响的例子，提醒人们注意补充牛磺酸的风险。

• **_xerces_的观点**：因牛磺酸与结肠癌的潜在联系而停止使用，并关注一项相关试验的结果。他还提到个体肠道细菌差异可能导致不同人对牛磺酸的反应不同。

• **amelius的观点**：引用前文信息，表示庆幸自己没有大量补充牛磺酸，暗示对牛磺酸的抗衰老效果持怀疑态度。

• **jbentley1的观点**：以幽默方式回应，表示不会改变喝红牛的习惯，暗示对牛磺酸相关讨论不以为然。

• **lentoutcry的观点**：首次听说牛磺酸与衰老的关联，之前只知道牛磺酸是能量饮料的成分，并对牛磺酸作为流行补充剂的兴起表示好奇。

• **paulcole的观点**：引用Betteridge’s Law of Headlines，暗示文章标题的问题可能并不需要直接回答，可能对讨论持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 牛磺酸的潜在风险和个体差异：多位评论者提到牛磺酸可能带来的风险，包括促进白血病生长和结肠癌风险，并指出个体肠道细菌差异可能导致不同效果。
• 雷帕霉素的比较：有评论者认为雷帕霉素在抗衰老方面效果更明确，尽管其也有副作用。
• 生活方式的重要性：多位评论者强调了良好睡眠、饮食、运动和精神健康等生活方式对健康和抗衰老的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 牛磺酸是否对健康和抗衰老有积极作用：一些评论者认为牛磺酸无益甚至有害，而另一些评论者则继续使用并对其效果持开放态度。
• 白藜芦醇的效果：有评论者引用研究明确反对其抗衰老效果，但仍有其他补充剂支持者。

• **baxtr的观点**：认为保持健康的80%益处来自于简单的生活习惯，如良好睡眠、日常活动、定期锻炼、饮食新鲜适量以及保持社交联系，而不需要额外补充牛磺酸或白藜芦醇等。

• **robwwilliams的观点**：明确反对补充牛磺酸和白藜芦醇，指出牛磺酸相关研究存在问题，白藜芦醇已被多项研究（如Miller等2011年研究）明确否定。相比之下，他更支持雷帕霉素（rapamycin）的抗衰老效果，尽管其有副作用，但在某些情况下（如COVID-19期间对老年人可能有益）。

• **mark_l_watson的观点**：尽管承认补充剂的效果不确定，仍选择补充牛磺酸（通过食用鸡腿肉）和白藜芦醇（受David Sinclair影响）。他还强调冥想、宽恕和精神平衡等生活方式的重要性，并补充维生素D和Omega 3对健康的益处。

• **meindnoch的观点**：引用研究指出牛磺酸可能促进白血病生长，提供了一个牛磺酸潜在负面影响的例子，提醒人们注意补充牛磺酸的风险。

• **_xerces_的观点**：因牛磺酸与结肠癌的潜在联系而停止使用，并关注一项相关试验的结果。他还提到个体肠道细菌差异可能导致不同人对牛磺酸的反应不同。

• **amelius的观点**：引用前文信息，表示庆幸自己没有大量补充牛磺酸，暗示对牛磺酸的抗衰老效果持怀疑态度。

• **jbentley1的观点**：以幽默方式回应，表示不会改变喝红牛的习惯，暗示对牛磺酸相关讨论不以为然。

• **lentoutcry的观点**：首次听说牛磺酸与衰老的关联，之前只知道牛磺酸是能量饮料的成分，并对牛磺酸作为流行补充剂的兴起表示好奇。

• **paulcole的观点**：引用Betteridge’s Law of Headlines，暗示文章标题的问题可能并不需要直接回答，可能对讨论持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 牛磺酸的潜在风险和个体差异：多位评论者提到牛磺酸可能带来的风险，包括促进白血病生长和结肠癌风险，并指出个体肠道细菌差异可能导致不同效果。
• 雷帕霉素的比较：有评论者认为雷帕霉素在抗衰老方面效果更明确，尽管其也有副作用。
• 生活方式的重要性：多位评论者强调了良好睡眠、饮食、运动和精神健康等生活方式对健康和抗衰老的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 牛磺酸是否对健康和抗衰老有积极作用：一些评论者认为牛磺酸无益甚至有害，而另一些评论者则继续使用并对其效果持开放态度。
• 白藜芦醇的效果：有评论者引用研究明确反对其抗衰老效果，但仍有其他补充剂支持者。

data.article_summary: 本文详细介绍了OAuth 2.0的实际应用及其工作原理，旨在帮助开发者在不阅读繁琐规范的情况下掌握OAuth。OAuth 2.0是一组规范，允许开发者将用户的身份验证和授权委托给其他服务，避免应用直接请求用户名和密码。OAuth主要用于授权，但也包含身份验证（通过OpenID Connect）。它通过生成具有有限生命周期的令牌，允许第三方服务访问用户数据，同时确保数据访问的安全性和限制性。本文还区分了OAuth与SAML，后者主要用于单点登录的身份验证。文章列出了八种常见的OAuth模式，包括本地登录、第三方登录、企业登录、服务授权和设备登录等，以帮助开发者更好地理解和应用OAuth。
