OAuth
What is OAuth and How Does it Work?
By Brian Pontarelli, Ahmed Hashesh and Dan Moore
I know what you are thinking, is this really another guide to OAuth 2.0?
Well, yes and no. This guide is different from most of the others out there because it covers all of the ways that we actually use OAuth. It also covers all of the details you need to be an OAuth expert without reading all the specifications or writing your own OAuth server. This document is based on hundreds of conversations and client implementations as well as our experience building FusionAuth, an OAuth server which has been downloaded over a million times.
If that sounds good to you, keep reading!
What is OAuth 2.0?
OAuth 2.0 is a set of specifications that allow developers to easily delegate the authentication and authorization of their users to someone else. While the specifications donât specifically cover authentication, in practice this is a core piece of OAuth, so we will cover it in depth (because thatâs how we roll).
OAuth in general was designed as a reaction to the
direct authentication pattern
, which features applications requesting usernames and passwords when accessing user-specific data at other services. When utilizing OAuth, the user still provides this information, but they log into one platform and use tokens generated by that platform to grant access to data and perform actions in one or more other applications. These applications may be owned by third parties or by the same folks who control the authentication platform. This flexibility is one reason for confusion when it comes to OAuth.
Before authentication and authorization with OAuth was available, websites would ask users to enter a username and password into a form, for example the credentials for a Gmail account, to gain access to Gmail data. Users realized they didnât want to grant full access to any old service. They preferred limited access instead. A user might want a third party service to access their email account, but only have rights to read contacts, not send email or add contacts.
When using OAuth, a token, which has a limited lifetime, provides that constrained access. Connecting multiple applications is easier for users. It is also more secure since
user credentials
are not shared. Auth is also easier for developers to manage because they only need to integrate OAuth 2.0 in their application instead of having their own database to store usersâ sensitive information.
OAuth and SAML are sometimes confused. SAML is primarily an authentication system used for single sign-on, while OAuth is an authorization system that has authentication layered on top of it (OpenID Connect, or OIDC). Authentication is about confirming the userâs identity. Authorization is about deciding what services, functionality or data they can access. A detailed comparison between
OAuth and SAML is found here
.
What does the phrase used above, âdelegate the authentication and authorization of their users to someone elseâ, mean, really?
It means that your application sends the user over to an OAuth server, the user logs in, and then the user is sent back to your application. But. There are a couple of different twists and goals of this process. Letâs cover those next.
How Does OAuth 2.0 Work?
None of the specifications cover how OAuth is actually integrated into applications. Whoops! But as a developer, thatâs what you care about. They also donât cover the different workflows or processes that leverage OAuth. They leave almost everything up to the implementer (the person who writes the OAuth Server) and integrator (the person who integrates their application with that OAuth server).
Rather than just reword the information in the specifications (yet again), letâs create a vocabulary for real-world integrations and implementations of OAuth. Weâll call them
OAuth modes
.
There are eight OAuth modes in common use today. These real world OAuth modes are:
Local login and registration
Third-party login and registration
(federated identity)
First-party login and registration
(reverse federated identity)
Enterprise login and registration
(federated identity with a twist)
Third-party service authorization
First-party service authorization
Machine-to-machine authentication and authorization
Device login and registration
Iâve included notation on a few of the items above specifying which are federated identity workflows. The reason that Iâve changed the names here from just âfederated identityâ is that each case is slightly different. Plus, the term federated identity is often overloade

data.title: Test Postgres in Python Like SQLite
data.author: wey-gu
data.article_summary: Py-PGlite 是一个 Python 库，旨在简化使用 PostgreSQL 进行测试的过程，使测试像使用 SQLite 一样轻便。它无需 Docker、配置文件或手动设置，提供零配置的快速启动。支持 SQLAlchemy、Django 和 FastAPI 等框架，自动处理数据库连接和清理。通过 Py-PGlite，开发者可以快速启动一个真实的 PostgreSQL 数据库用于测试，且每个测试都有独立的数据库环境。此外，它支持 PostgreSQL 的全部功能，如 JSON 操作和复杂查询。安装简便，可通过 pip 安装核心包或集成特定框架的包。其架构设计无框架依赖，支持可选集成和智能默认配置。

• samwillis指出PGlite正在开发的WASI构建，可以去除Node.js依赖，但目前在错误处理方面存在问题。
• ptx质疑使用WebAssembly运行PostgreSQL的必要性，认为原生版本通过适当配置可以避免WebAssembly、Node.js和npm带来的额外开销。

• perrygeo推荐了Zonky作为JVM上的类似解决方案，直接运行嵌入式原生二进制文件。
• selimnairb分享了自己使用pytest-docker-compose的经验，认为这样可以避免NPM依赖问题。

• 不同的技术栈和工具（如Testcontainers、pytest-docker-compose、Zonky）被提出作为替代方案。

44196945.article_summary: Py-PGlite 是一个 Python 库，旨在简化使用 PostgreSQL 进行测试的过程，使测试像使用 SQLite 一样轻便。它无需 Docker、配置文件或手动设置，提供零配置的快速启动。支持 SQLAlchemy、Django 和 FastAPI 等框架，自动处理数据库连接和清理。通过 Py-PGlite，开发者可以快速启动一个真实的 PostgreSQL 数据库用于测试，且每个测试都有独立的数据库环境。此外，它支持 PostgreSQL 的全部功能，如 JSON 操作和复杂查询。安装简便，可通过 pip 安装核心包或集成特定框架的包。其架构设计无框架依赖，支持可选集成和智能默认配置。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：家用蒸馏活动的乐趣、合法性以及技术需求

不同观点：
• [01100011] 认为蒸馏过程本身是一种令人愉悦的爱好，尤其是对那些喜欢酿造的人来说。他提到在蒸馏开始时等待温度上升可能对某些人来说比较无聊，但他个人享受操控蒸馏设备的过程。他还用浪漫化的语言描述了热乙醇的折射效果，推荐有酿造兴趣的人尝试蒸馏。

• [ghushn3] 强调了家用蒸馏在许多地方是严格非法的，警告那些考虑从事这一爱好的人需要小心。他指出了全球多个地区（包括美国许多地方）对蒸馏活动的法律限制，暗示参与这一活动可能面临法律风险。

• [dylan604] 对蒸馏设备需要开源软件（OSS）表示困惑和不解。他认为蒸馏过程本质上非常简单，只需将发酵的麦汁放入蒸馏器中加热，然后收集蒸馏产物即可。相比之下，他认为类似于家用电器要求WiFi连接的需求是多余的，甚至显得荒谬。

补充讨论：
- [01100011] 的观点主要集中在蒸馏作为一种有趣的爱好，享受其中的过程和美学体验。
- [ghushn3] 的观点侧重于法律风险，提醒人们在尝试蒸馏之前要了解相关法律。
- [dylan604] 则对蒸馏设备技术需求提出了质疑，尤其不理解为何蒸馏过程会涉及开源软件，认为这是不必要的复杂化。

争议焦点：
- 蒸馏作为一种爱好是否值得推荐：[01100011] 积极推荐，而 [ghushn3] 则提醒潜在的合法性问题。
- 技术复杂性：[dylan604] 对蒸馏设备需要开源软件表示不满，认为蒸馏过程不应如此复杂。

data.title: The Universal Tech Tree
data.author: mitchbob
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了技术创新之间的相互关联性，特别是火器与相机技术的联系。文章提到，火器的设计启发了早期摄影设备的发展，例如法国科学家Étienne-Jules Marey的“摄影枪”，其设计借鉴了火器的旋转机制。而Marey的设计又可能影响了托马斯·爱迪生及其发明的活动电影放映机（kinetograph）。文章进一步追溯了火器技术的历史，指出旋转机制早在16世纪的欧洲和中国就已存在，并逐步演变为现代火器和摄影设备。作者致力于将主要技术创新及其关联可视化，创建了一个“科技树”项目，以展示技术发展的历史脉络和逻辑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术树（tech tree）的结构、用途、呈现方式及相关理论

不同观点：
• [acenturyandabit] 提供了实际技术树的链接，但没有深入讨论其内容或结构。
• [NamTaf] 认为将技术发展称为“树”并不准确，因为技术发展并非简单的1对多线性关系，而是更像社交媒体图谱，不同想法交织产生新发明。他提到《Connections》节目强调了这种非线性。
• [tunesmith] 提出技术树是否受到外部限制的问题，比如环境事件是否会导致某些技术无法被发明。他还讨论了技术树分支之间的独立性和潜在的未被发现领域。
• [jlcx] 提供了一个不同的项目链接，该项目采用“全包含树”方法，并使用DBpedia/Wikidata进行编辑。他指出该方法虽然可能包含更多错误，但揭示了有趣的整体结构。
• [diggan] 提到自己正在制作一个包含约50项技术的游戏技术树，并希望这个通用技术树的数据能够以更开放的许可发布，以便更多人使用。
• [thrtythreeforty] 引用了一本科幻小说《Lady of Mazes》，探讨了一个“完成”的技术树以及社会如何选择拒绝某些技术分支，反映了技术与社会价值观的互动。
• [efm] 赞赏了技术树的清晰组织，但指出其无法持续更新以及进行其他形式的分析，并建议以知识图谱形式呈现数据。
• [DavidPiper] 观察到技术树在1880到1980年间密度很高，而1980年后似乎发展放缓，提出了数据收集偏差或技术定义改变等可能原因。
• [CommenterPerson] 强调技术树从石器工具开始，重新定义了技术，指出技术不仅仅是现代设备，而是概念知识的应用。
• [ttoinou] 建议将技术树游戏化，类似于iOS上的拼图游戏Doodle God。
• [haddr] 提到“相邻可能”理论，解释技术发展的路径依赖于某些使能技术或经济条件是否具备。
• [garrettgarcia] 对早期技术的悠久历史表示兴趣，指出很多技术在智人出现之前已经被发明。
• [paulorlando] 赞赏技术树的执行，指出它与多种理论和方法重叠，并提供探索功能，是一个很好的资源。
• [meindnoch] 简短指出技术树实际上是一个有向无环图（DAG），而非树。
• [tbrownaw] 询问是否存在个人技能和工作的树结构。

补充讨论：
• 技术树的结构争议：多个评论者讨论了技术树是否应被称为“树”，指出技术发展更可能是复杂图谱而非简单的树结构。
• 技术发展的限制和可能性：讨论了技术发展是否受到外部事件或内部社会选择的限制，以及某些技术分支可能完全未被发现。
• 技术树的应用和扩展：包括技术树的游戏化可能性、开放数据的需求、以及在个人技能和职业方面的潜在应用。

争议焦点：
• 技术树的准确命名和结构：是否应称为“树”或更准确地描述为有向无环图（DAG）。
• 技术发展的线性与非线性：技术是否按照线性路径发展，还是受到多种因素交织影响。

44161607.article_content:
The Universal Tech Tree
Étienne Fortier-Dubois
When we try and pick out any technology in isolation, we find it hitched, in some way, to every innovation that preceded it. (Except for the Oldowan hand axe. We had to start somewhere.)
What do firearms and cameras have in common? One answer is shared vocabulary: load, aim, shoot. The etymological origins of this relatedness are murky. People likely borrowed language about firearms — which are over 500 years older than photography — to talk about cameras, which are operated in a similar manner.  But in the case of the movie camera, the connection is concrete.
The first movie camera is generally considered to be the kinetograph, invented in 1891 by Thomas Edison and William Kennedy Dickson, an inventor at the Edison lab. Two years earlier, Edison had travelled to Paris to the Exposition Universelle of 1889, a world’s fair, to showcase his company’s phonograph. There, he met with Étienne-Jules Marey, a French scientist who had begun his career studying blood circulation, and who had developed an interest in chronophotography partly out of his work on physiology. Chronophotography consists of taking multiple photographs in quick succession to capture movement.
A famous early achievement of the technique is
The Horse in Motion
, a series of photographs taken by Eadweard Muybridge in 1878 that proved something Marey had asserted years earlier: For a brief moment in gallop, a horse has all four hooves off the ground. Encouraged by Muybridge, Marey developed an improved device to take chronophotographs. The resulting design, the “photographic gun,” featured a long barrel derived from existing firearms. We don’t know what transpired between Marey and Edison, but it seems likely that Marey’s design inspired the kinetograph. Coincidentally (or not), the Online Etymology Dictionary’s entry for “
shoot
” claims “the meaning ‘to photograph’ (especially a movie) is from 1890” — around the time of the kinetograph’s invention.
Marey himself had been inspired by the invention of another Frenchman, the astronomer Pierre Janssen. In 1874, hoping to capture images of the transit of Venus, Janssen created a device he called the “photographic revolver.” It looked like a large telescope. Inside, it hosted a complex camera that used a revolving apparatus to take several images in quick succession. The resulting eight seconds of the black dot of Venus moving across the sun disk are often recognized as the first motion picture in history.
1
Prior to Jansenn’s invention, revolving components had not been used in photography or astronomy. They came from the Colt Paterson revolver, a handgun popular in the U.S. since its mid-19th century creation by Samuel Colt. Thus, we can reconstruct a genealogical succession of ideas: Colt inspired Janssen, who inspired Marey, who likely inspired Edison (who then inspired the Lumière brothers and further developments in filmmaking).
We can go further back still. Colt improved the revolver and made its mass production commercially viable, but he did not invent it. Nor was it a particularly recent development: Guns with a revolving barrel have existed since the 16th century. A
German revolver
dates from 1597, but there are even older specimens. The
xun lei chong
, a Chinese revolving musket, also dates from this period.
It makes sense: The 1500s were a time of great innovation in firing mechanisms for muskets and arquebuses, with developments like the wheellock (which used a spinning metal wheel against pyrite to create sparks), snaplock (which struck flint against steel using a spring-loaded arm), and flintlock (which improved on the snaplock with a combined hammer-flint holder). Volley guns made of multiple cannons existed in England since at least the 1330s. These were descendants, in turn, of simpler cannons that stem from the invention of gunpowder in China in the 800s. It stands to reason that eventually
someone
in Europe would think of making a spinning mechanism to allow a weapon to fire multiple shots in quick succession.
And yet, if you’re anything like me, most of what you just read was probably surprising. We don’t typically associate revolvers with the 1500s, or, for that matter, with movie cameras.
The reason I learned about this — and dozens of anecdotes around other inventions — is that I have been working on a quixotic project to place all major technological innovations in history on a timeline, together with the connections between them. The goal is to situate stories like that of the revolver and camera in their historical context, notice patterns, and understand the logic of the history of technology. The result is an interactive visualization that I call
the historical tech tree
.
Étienne-Jules Marey, Bird Flight, Pelican, 1886.
How to build a tech tree

• [meindnoch] 简短指出技术树实际上是一个有向无环图（DAG），而非树。

data.title: Show HN: Lambduck, a Functional Programming Brainfuck
data.author: jorkingit
data.article_summary:
Lambduck是一种函数式编程语言，具有以下特点：

1. **特殊形式**：
   - `lambda`（`\`）用于定义函数。
   - `apply`（`` ` ``）用于函数应用，采用左most-innermost的 eager evaluation。

2. **变量**：
   - `here`（`-`）获取当前函数的参数。
   - `there`（`+`）获取外层函数的参数。
   - `yonder`（`*`）获取更外层函数的参数。

3. **内置函数**：
   - `getchar`（`,`）从stdin读取一个字节并编码为Church数值。
   - `putchar`（`.`）将参数解码并写入stdout。

4. **程序解析**：
   - 忽略无效字符，成功解析第一个表达式后，剩余输入视为stdin。

5. **示例**：
   - `true`、`false`、`identity`、组合子`s`和`z`，以及简单的输入输出示例。

该语言通过独特的符号和函数组合实现基本的计算和I/O操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一种类似于Brainfuck的极简编程语言的讨论，涉及其评估方式、名称、与其它语言的对比以及实际应用等问题。

不同观点：
• **关于程序评估与顺序依赖性**：
  - **tromp** 提问该程序的评估是否依赖于评估顺序，并提到程序的I/O操作无需额外的原语。

• **关于语言的简洁性与纯度**：
  - **mmoskal** 认为该语言过于可读，建议去除字符字面量以保持“纯粹性”，并指出该语言比Brainfuck更紧凑，因为lambda calculus的表示更加常规。

• **关于名称的调侃**：
  - **2d8a875f-39a2-4** 调侃地建议将该语言命名为"Fuckbrain"。
  - **reverendsteveii** 则以幽默的方式建议命名为"LambDuck"，认为这能使其从最不可爱的语言名称变为最可爱的名称。

• **关于与Brainfuck及类似语言的对比**：
  - **somat** 指出Brainfuck是一种栈语言，更接近Forth，而该语言更像是Scheme的模拟，可能更接近Unlambda（无lambda形式的lambda calculus实现）。

• **关于实际应用与解释器代码**：
  - **sph** 称赞该工作非常聪明，但觉得自己可能不够聪明去实际使用它，并请求分享解释器代码。同时提供了de Bruijn指数的定义链接供学习。
  - **90s_dev** 表示难以理解该语言，询问如何实现"Hello World"，并描述了自己尝试输入某些代码和输入内容的经历。

• **关于Turing完备性与de Bruijn指数的限制**：
  - **reuben364** 讨论了de Bruijn指数的有限性，并好奇在保持Turing完备的前提下，这些指数可以被限制到什么程度。

补充讨论：
• **关于其他建议**：
  - **naikrovek** 自嘲自己太笨，无法识别该语言的深奥之处。
  - **jzemeocala** 开玩笑地建议下一次实现“Malborge”这一复杂的语言。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在**程序评估顺序**和**语言名称**的调侃上，一些人关注技术细节，另一些人则以幽默方式参与讨论。

data.title: Musk-Trump dispute includes threats to SpaceX contracts
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 2023年6月，唐纳德·特朗普与埃隆·马斯克之间的争执升级，主要围绕马斯克批评特朗普支持的预算协调法案，并在社交媒体上展开激烈交锋。特朗普威胁取消与马斯克公司（如SpaceX）的政府合同，马斯克则回应称将开始退役SpaceX的“龙”飞船。虽然双方言辞激烈，但并未落实为实际行动。马斯克随后收回了退役威胁。争执引发了对SpaceX可能失去NASA和国防部重要合同的担忧，因为这些机构高度依赖SpaceX的 launch services。与此同时，特朗普撤回了提名杰瑞德·艾萨克曼担任NASA局长的决定，称其为民主党人，不合适。总体而言，争执被视为言辞上的对峙，实际影响有限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特朗普与马斯克之间的争端及其潜在影响，特别是关于政府合同、商业竞争和政治策略的讨论。

不同观点：
• **反对基于个人喜好的政府合同**：onlyrealcuzzo认为，总统不应基于个人好恶取消政府合同，这样做类似于腐败，并可能导致任人唯亲，而不是基于实际表现授予合同。这种做法类似于导致苏联解体的路径。

• **现实考量与国际关系**：BirAdam指出，取消SpaceX合同可能导致美国依赖俄罗斯等国家，并且目前波音和蓝色起源的成本较高，也没有类似SpaceX的卫星网络。

• **政治立场与公众形象**：kaycebasques提到马斯克在共和党中很受欢迎，暗示政治立场可能影响公众和媒体对争端的看法。

• **SpaceX的国有化可能性**：seydor认为，当前局势可能导致SpaceX的国有化。

• **权力滥用与商业影响**：mystified5016将争端视为独裁者与其强大亲信的内斗，指出特朗普有能力通过多种手段打击马斯克，包括撤销安全许可和启动移民欺诈调查。

• **合同应基于服务质量和价格**：state_less认为，SpaceX合同应基于其服务质量和价格，而非个人争端，并批评特朗普的某些法案。

• **阴谋论与认知失调**：jmyeet认为，许多人将争端视为一种策略或形象修复，并指出这是认知失调的反映。同时提到马斯克和特朗普都是自负且情绪化的人，可能没有所谓的“优绩主义”。

• **性别偏见与政治**：ndr42引用研究指出，部分美国人认为女性因情绪化而不适合从政，暗示性别偏见在政治中的影响。

• **分散注意力与政策实施**：shrubble怀疑争端是为了转移公众对其他政策或法案（如 reconciliation 法案和Palantir获取更多美国公民信息）的注意力。

• **国际竞争与经济损失**：yb6677认为美国政府不会取消SpaceX合同，因为SpaceX是市场领导者，且马斯克有能力在海外设立基地，美国不愿看到他与别国紧密合作。

• **戏剧化与政治秀**：bgwalter指出，特朗普的许多行为都是为了迎合其MAGA基础，争端可能只是一场政治秀，实际影响有限。

• **全球观感与政治传统**：tsoukase感叹美国强大的形象因这场争端而受损，质疑正式协议、联邦律师、政治传统和秘密服务的缺失。

• **更深层次的策略**：Neil44认为，这场争端可能只是为了吸引公众注意力，背后有更大的政治策略。

补充讨论：
• **技术社区的角度**：dottjt提到技术社区（HN）倾向于将非技术事件转化为技术相关的讨论，以适应社区兴趣。

争议焦点：特朗普与马斯克争端的真实动机及其对政府合同、商业和国际关系的影响，是否存在更深层次的政治策略或阴谋。

44209515.article_content:
Elon Musk gestures while discussing the sixth Starship test launch with President-elect Donald Trump at Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas. To the right of Trump is Gen. Chance Saltzman, Chief of space operations for the U.S. Space Force. Credit: Brandon Bell/Getty Images
WASHINGTON — An escalating feud between President Trump and Elon Musk June 5 included threats to cancel SpaceX contracts and decommission spacecraft, although those words have yet to become actions.
In a heated exchange largely carried out on social media, Musk’s criticism of a budget reconciliation bill backed by Trump turned into full-fledged attacks on each other, less than a week after Musk ended his formal role in the administration as a “special government employee” overseeing the White House’s Department of Government Efficiency.
That exchange included a threat by Trump to cancel government contracts with Musk’s companies, such as SpaceX. “The easiest way to save money in our Budget, Billions and Billions of Dollars, is to terminate Elon’s Governmental Subsidies and Contracts,” Trump
posted
on his social media platform, Truth Social.
While the comment did not specifically mention SpaceX, Musk appeared to interpret it as a threat to SpaceX. “In light of the President’s statement about cancellation of my government contracts, @SpaceX will begin decommissioning its Dragon spacecraft immediately,” he
posted
on his social media platform, X, about 90 minutes later. He didn’t elaborate on what would be involved in “decommissioning” Dragon.
The back-and-forth between Musk and Trump raised fears that the White House might cut SpaceX off from its extensive work with NASA and the Defense Department, to the detriment of both the government and the company. It comes just months after many in the space industry worried that the then-close relationship between Musk and Trump might give SpaceX an unfair advantage.
Any loss of federal contracts would have a significant effect on SpaceX. Musk, in a rare glimpse into SpaceX finances,
said
June 3 that SpaceX is projecting $15.5 billion in revenue in 2025, of which $1.1 billion would come from NASA contracts. He did not disclose the amount coming from defense work, which would include launches as well as Starlink services and development of a reconnaissance satellite constellation for the National Reconnaissance Office.
The effects on the government from canceling those contracts, though, could be far greater. Both NASA and the Defense Department rely heavily on SpaceX for launch services as competing vehicles from other companies have been slow to enter service. SpaceX has the only operational vehicle, other than Russia’s Soyuz, to get crews to and from the International Space Station, and is a key cargo supplier. SpaceX also has a NASA contract to develop the U.S. Deorbit Vehicle, the spacecraft that will ensure a safe reentry of the station at the end of its life.
One industry source, speaking on background, dismissed the exchanges as “bluster” that neither Musk nor Trump would actually implement, noting the reliance the federal government has on SpaceX and SpaceX’s desire to retain government revenue.
Indeed, Musk, about five hours after making the threat to decommission Dragon, walked it back. “Good advice,” he wrote in a
post
, responding to a pseudonymous user who asked Musk to “cool off and take a step back for a couple days” from the debate. “Ok, we won’t decommission Dragon.”
NASA stood on the sidelines during the Trump-Musk exchanges. “NASA will continue to execute upon the President’s vision for the future of space. We will continue to work with our industry partners to ensure the President’s objectives in space are met,” said NASA press secretary Bethany Stevens.
Search for new NASA administrator nominee
The dispute between Musk and Trump overshadowed comments made by Trump earlier in the day about
his decision announced May 31 to withdraw the nomination of Jared Isaacman to be NASA administrator
.
Musk “wanted, and rightfully, recommended somebody that I guess he knew very well — I’m sure he respected him — to run NASA, and I didn’t think it was appropriate,” Trump said in a media availability with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Trump said that Isaacman was a Democrat, although Isaacman has donated to both Republican and Democratic candidates and organizations over the year.
“We won. We get certain privileges and one of the privileges is we don’t have to appoint a Democrat,” Trump said.
“NASA is very important. We have great people. Gen. Caine is going to be picking somebody. We’ll be checking him out,” he said, a reference to Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. It’s unclear why Trump asked Caine, an Air Force general with no space background, to select the head of the nation’s civil space agency.

• **反对基于个人喜好的政府合同**：onlyrealcuzzo认为，总统不应基于个人好恶取消政府合同，这样做类似于腐败，并可能导致任人唯亲，而不是基于实际表现授予合同。这种做法类似于导致苏联解体的路径。

• **现实考量与国际关系**：BirAdam指出，取消SpaceX合同可能导致美国依赖俄罗斯等国家，并且目前波音和蓝色起源的成本较高，也没有类似SpaceX的卫星网络。

• **政治立场与公众形象**：kaycebasques提到马斯克在共和党中很受欢迎，暗示政治立场可能影响公众和媒体对争端的看法。

• **SpaceX的国有化可能性**：seydor认为，当前局势可能导致SpaceX的国有化。

• **权力滥用与商业影响**：mystified5016将争端视为独裁者与其强大亲信的内斗，指出特朗普有能力通过多种手段打击马斯克，包括撤销安全许可和启动移民欺诈调查。

• **合同应基于服务质量和价格**：state_less认为，SpaceX合同应基于其服务质量和价格，而非个人争端，并批评特朗普的某些法案。

• **阴谋论与认知失调**：jmyeet认为，许多人将争端视为一种策略或形象修复，并指出这是认知失调的反映。同时提到马斯克和特朗普都是自负且情绪化的人，可能没有所谓的“优绩主义”。

• **性别偏见与政治**：ndr42引用研究指出，部分美国人认为女性因情绪化而不适合从政，暗示性别偏见在政治中的影响。

• **分散注意力与政策实施**：shrubble怀疑争端是为了转移公众对其他政策或法案（如 reconciliation 法案和Palantir获取更多美国公民信息）的注意力。

• **国际竞争与经济损失**：yb6677认为美国政府不会取消SpaceX合同，因为SpaceX是市场领导者，且马斯克有能力在海外设立基地，美国不愿看到他与别国紧密合作。

• **戏剧化与政治秀**：bgwalter指出，特朗普的许多行为都是为了迎合其MAGA基础，争端可能只是一场政治秀，实际影响有限。

• **全球观感与政治传统**：tsoukase感叹美国强大的形象因这场争端而受损，质疑正式协议、联邦律师、政治传统和秘密服务的缺失。

• **更深层次的策略**：Neil44认为，这场争端可能只是为了吸引公众注意力，背后有更大的政治策略。

补充讨论：
• **技术社区的角度**：dottjt提到技术社区（HN）倾向于将非技术事件转化为技术相关的讨论，以适应社区兴趣。

争议焦点：特朗普与马斯克争端的真实动机及其对政府合同、商业和国际关系的影响，是否存在更深层次的政治策略或阴谋。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：咖啡因在睡前对大脑活动的影响以及不同年龄层对咖啡因的耐受性

不同观点：
• [jasonthorsness] 认为，睡前摄入咖啡因是不明智的做法，并且质疑研究的新颖性。他提到大多数人可能已经知道睡前摄入咖啡因是不好的，并对这类研究的意义表示怀疑。
• [christophilus] 提出，随着时间推移，人体可能对咖啡因产生耐受性，并猜测中老年人群可能比年轻人群更不容易受到咖啡因的影响。这暗示了年龄可能是一个影响因素。
• [azaras] 提供了与[christophilus]部分相关的观察，指出长期饮用咖啡的老年人似乎在精神健康方面表现更好，相比饮酒者有优势。这暗示了咖啡因可能对精神健康有长期的积极影响。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于研究的新颖性和实际应用价值。一些人认为此类研究可能并没有提供新的见解，而另一些人则关注个体差异和长期影响，如年龄和耐受性的问题。
• 还提到了咖啡因与酒精对精神健康的不同影响，虽然这并非主要讨论点，但为咖啡因的潜在益处提供了对比视角。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款用于减少手机使用时间的工具及其API的讨论，涉及功能、技术实现、用户需求和隐私问题。

不同观点：
• [alexdanilowicz] 认为减少手机使用时间值得提倡，并分享了自己通过与亲属分享数据来“游戏化”严格控制屏幕时间的做法。
• [navs] 对通过数据点来衡量心理健康表示兴趣，并提到自己正在手动整合健康数据和情感日记，认为该工具可以作为一个新的数据点。
• [codethief] 对Clearspace app需要连接Google账户和网络权限表示不满，担心数据隐私问题，指出很多Play Store上的应用会出售用户数据。
• [ErikBjare] 提到自己开发的ActivityWatch项目，也具有类似功能，并指出在iOS上实现屏幕时间功能非常困难，赞赏该工具在iOS上的进展。

补充讨论：
• [handfuloflight] 询问数据如何通过API获取，是否需要用户安装额外的东西。
• [drag0s] 建议增加React Native SDK和通过API锁定/解锁屏幕时间的功能。
• [ctippett] 关注跨设备的使用情况，询问API如何处理iPhone和iPad上的时间统计。
• [TrueGeek] 希望工具能够支持用户想要更多使用的应用，而不仅仅是减少使用时间，并提到自己学习语言的应用被误锁。
• [roycebranning] 开玩笑地表示希望有一个当使用时间超过7小时时可以自动付钱给朋友的功能。
• [aziaziazi] 对工具的UI表示赞赏，并询问是否使用了公共CSS框架/主题。
• [beggi] 询问是否计划通过REST API来限制应用使用。
• [mikaoj85] 提到iOS上的网页使用不便，质疑是否是故意设计的。
• [awaseem] 询问API是否开放源代码，并表示可能会将此功能添加到自己的开放源代码限制应用Foqos中。
• [kovek] 对工具表示兴趣，并询问是否有MacOS上的类似解决方案。

争议焦点：
• 隐私问题：[codethief] 对Clearspace app需要连接Google账户和网络权限表示不满，担心数据被出售。
• 工具的功能限制：[TrueGeek] 提到工具默认锁定用户想要更多使用的应用，与用户需求不符。

data.title: Programming language Dino and its implementation
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: DINO是一种高性能编程语言，结合了脚本语言、函数式语言和面向对象语言的特性。它由Vladimir Makarov开发，早期用于俄罗斯游戏公司作为简化脚本语言。DINO具有多精度整数、异构数组、关联表、函数闭包、异常处理、并发和模式匹配等功能，并支持Unicode 8。其数组和关联表使用哈希表实现，支持无桶冲突解决和Murmur哈希函数。DINO的并发通过纤维（fiber）实现，类似于绿色线程，比OS线程更快且具有自动死锁检测。类是特殊类型的函数，支持多重继承和动态调度。性能上，DINO与Python、PyPy、Ruby、JS和Scala等语言在不同架构上进行了对比。未来计划通过OS线程实现并行性，摆脱全局解释器锁（GIL）的限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对编程语言OCaml的性能、特性以及历史背景的不同看法

不同观点：
• **对基准测试结果的困惑** ([johnisgood])：该评论者对OCaml的基准测试数据表示不解，认为OCaml的速度应该很快，但数据似乎显示其比Python或Ruby更慢。他们怀疑是代码实现问题，希望查看具体代码以确定性能差异的原因。

• **对语言特性的积极评价** ([ghurtado])：该评论者对OCaml的特性给予肯定，认为它具有许多现代和完整的功能，特别提到了它能够填补Python中一些已知的功能空白，对Python用户有吸引力。

• **对语言历史的调侃** ([bravesoul2])：该评论者以调侃的语气提到OCaml像是一种“从1993年开始的Go语言”，并指出其名称与现代JavaScript运行器有相似之处，暗示对语言名称和历史背景的某种戏谑态度。

• **对语言印象的意外** ([zem])：该评论者表示OCaml给他们带来了 pleasant 和 capable 的印象，这与他们之前对该语言作为游戏脚本语言的起源故事的预期不同，显示出对语言能力的意外惊喜。

• **对语言名称的情感反应** ([Lerc])：该评论者对“Animatek”这个名称表示了情感上的反应，提到看到这个名称让他们感到意外和悲伤，并表达了对困难时刻寻求帮助的建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：目前的主要争议在于OCaml的基准测试结果是否可信以及其性能是否真的低于Python或Ruby。评论者对实现细节表示关注，并希望进一步调查。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：评论中涉及了对OCaml特性的功能性评价、对语言名称和历史的调侃以及对语言能力的意外惊喜，显示出对OCaml不同方面的多样化看法。

Programming language Dino and its implementation
Develepment version of future release 0.98
Vladimir Makarov,
vmakarov@gcc.gnu.org
Apr 2, 2016
Description Layout
Introduction to Dino
History
Dino as a high-level scripting language
Dino as a functional language
Dino as an object-oriented language
Dino Implementation
Overall Structure
Used implementation tools
Byte code compiler (optimizations)
Byte code Interpreter (GC, Concurrency, REPL)
JIT, Type inference
Performance comparison with Python, PyPy, Ruby, JS, Scala, OCAML
on x86-64, AARH64, ARM, PPC64.
Some history
1993: Original language design and implementation
Was used in russian computer game company ANIMATEK as a simple
scripting language for describing dinosaurus movements
1998, 2002, 2007, 2016 : Major language and implementation revisions
This document describes the current state of Dino language and
its implementation.
The first taste of Dino
Eratosthenes sieve:
var i, prime, k, count = 0, SieveSize = 8191, flags = [SieveSize : 1];
for (i = 0; i < SieveSize; i++)
if (flags[i]) {
prime = i + i + 3;
k = i + prime;
for (;;) {
if (k >= SieveSize)
break;
flags[k] = 0;
k += prime;
}
count++;
}
putln (count);
DINO as a scripting language
Dino aims to look like C language
High-Level scripting object-oriented language:
Multi-precision integers
Heterogeneous extensible arrays, array slices
Associative tables with possibility to delete elements
Powerful and safe class composition operation for (multiple)
inheritance and traits description
First class functions, classes, and fibers with closures,
anonymous functions, classes, fibers
Exception handling
Concurrency
Pattern matching
Unicode 8 support
Arrays and Tables
Associative tables
elements can be added and deleted
elements can be any values, e.g. other tables
Implemented as hash tables without buckets for compactness
and data locality
Secondary hash for conflict resolutions
Murmur hash function for most values
Array Slices
Eratosthenes sieve with slices:
var i, prime, count = 0, SieveSize = 8191, flags = [SieveSize : 1];
for (i = 0; i < SieveSize; i++)
if (flags[i]) {
prime = i + i + 3;
flags[i + prime:SieveSize:prime] = 0;
count++;
}
putln (count);
Functions
Example:
fun even;
fun odd  (i) {i == 0 ? 0 : even (i - 1);}
fun even (i) {i == 0 ? 1 : odd (i - 1);}
putln (odd (1_000_000));
Anonymous functions:
filter (fun (a) {a > 0;}, v);
fold (fun (a, b) {a * b;}, v, 1);
Function closures:
fun incr (base) {fun (incr) {base + incr;}}
Threads
Fiber: a function with concurrent execution
fiber t (n) {for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) putln (i);}
t(100); // the following code don't wait for t finish
for (var i = 0; i < 1000; i++) putln (“main”, i);
Implemented as green threads:
Much faster than OS threads with Global Interpreter Lock (Python/Ruby)
Deterministic behaviour and automatic deadlock recognition
Plans to implement through OS threads without GIL for parallelism
There is a low level sync-statement wait
wait (cond) [stmt];
Simple statements are atomic
Object orientation
Class is just a special type of function:
Returns closure, public visibility by default
class num (i) {fun print {put (i);}}
class binop (l, r) { fun print_op;
fun print {l.print(); print_op (); r.print ();}
}
Special class/function composition:
emulates (multiple) inheritance, traits, and dynamic dispatching
class add (l, r) {
use binop former l, r later print_op;
fun print_op {put (“ + “);}
}
Object orientation -- continuation
A safe and powerful way to support object orientation

are inlayed
Declarations before the use rewrite corresponding inlayed
declarations mentioned in

-clause

• **对语言历史的调侃** ([bravesoul2])：该评论者以调侃的语气提到OCaml像是一种“从1993年开始的Go语言”，并指出其名称与现代JavaScript运行器有相似之处，暗示对语言名称和历史背景的某种戏谑态度。

• **对语言印象的意外** ([zem])：该评论者表示OCaml给他们带来了 pleasant 和 capable 的印象，这与他们之前对该语言作为游戏脚本语言的起源故事的预期不同，显示出对语言能力的意外惊喜。

• **对语言名称的情感反应** ([Lerc])：该评论者对“Animatek”这个名称表示了情感上的反应，提到看到这个名称让他们感到意外和悲伤，并表达了对困难时刻寻求帮助的建议。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：目前的主要争议在于OCaml的基准测试结果是否可信以及其性能是否真的低于Python或Ruby。评论者对实现细节表示关注，并希望进一步调查。

• 其他值得注意的讨论点：评论中涉及了对OCaml特性的功能性评价、对语言名称和历史的调侃以及对语言能力的意外惊喜，显示出对OCaml不同方面的多样化看法。

data.article_summary: Claude Composer 是一个用于增强 Claude Code 的工具，提供自动化配置、权限管理、工具管理和通知功能。它通过可配置的规则集自动处理权限对话框，支持灵活的控制和自定义工具集设置，并通过系统通知保持用户知情。主要功能包括减少中断、灵活控制、工具管理及增强的可见性。安装需 Node.js 18+ 和 Claude Code，全局安装命令为 `npm install -g claude-composer`。配置通过 `claude-composer cc-init` 完成，支持规则集和工具集的自定义。此外，还提供多种命令行选项和环境变量配置，便于开发和调试。

A tool for enhancing Claude Code with automation, configuration, and better UX
Features
Reduced interruptions

Flexible control

data.title: Tokasaurus: An LLM inference engine for high-throughput workloads
data.author: rsehrlich
data.article_summary: Tokasaurus是一个由斯坦福大学团队开发的LLM推理引擎，专为高吞吐量工作负载优化。对于小模型，Tokasaurus通过极低的CPU开销和动态前缀分组来提高效率，尤其在共享前缀的情况下表现优异。对于大模型，它支持GPU上的异步张量并行和无NVLink情况下的快速流水线并行。在吞吐量基准测试中，Tokasaurus的性能比vLLM和SGLang高出最多3倍。该引擎通过异步和自适应管理减少CPU开销，并利用深度优先搜索算法动态识别共享前缀，从而提升整体吞吐量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tokasaurus项目的性能、实现、适用场景及潜在问题

不同观点：
• Refibrillator对Tokasaurus在纯Python实现下能超越vLLM和SGLang表示惊讶，认为这得益于torch.compile的进步，但对动态形状问题仍感困扰，计划深入研究其实现方式。
• Nabakin指出，虽然Tokasaurus在吞吐量上有显著优势，但未与SOTA的TensorRT-LLM进行对比，暗示其在顶尖性能比较中的不足。
• Behnamoh认为，Tokasaurus的Async-TP虽然在吞吐量上表现出色，但对于常见场景过于复杂，只有在处理6k+ token的大批量时才显现优势，且需要NVLink连接的GPU，建议除非针对大规模批量优化，否则 simpler approaches 更合适，并担心可靠性问题。
• Szpadel关注延迟问题，询问吞吐量提升带来的延迟代价，强调这对于“软实时”应用的重要性，尤其是当用户在等待时。
• Radq对项目的简单和良好文档表示赞赏，认为其是高性能推理引擎实现的良好起点，尤其适用于批量推理生成RL rollouts的场景。
• AStonesThrow以幽默方式提到Tokasaurus的命名，并表示计划将该名称用于个人用途，同时提及Meta AI和Llama 4的成功案例，展示该项目的实际应用潜力。
• SymbolicAGI认为，对于低延迟需求，llama.cpp仍然是自托管模型的最佳选择，并提到Ollama在包装llama.cpp方面的领先地位，但对Tokasaurus相关repo曾404表示担忧，庆幸其重新上线。
• DiabloD3对项目用Python编写表示遗憾，认为这可能使其难以在非专家手中得到应用，希望llama.cpp团队能帮助其避免被遗忘。

补充讨论：
• 项目性能和实现的复杂性是主要讨论焦点，尤其是吞吐量和延迟之间的权衡。
• 不同评论者对Tokasaurus的适用场景有不同看法，有的认为其适用于大规模批量处理，有的则认为过于复杂，不适合常见场景。
• 项目的命名和趣味性也被提及，增加了讨论的轻松氛围。
• 项目的技术实现细节，如动态形状处理和Async-TP的具体效果，引发了一些技术上的探讨和兴趣。
• 项目的未来发展和应用潜力也被一些评论者关注，尤其是其在自托管模型和推理引擎实现中的地位。

Tokasaurus: An LLM Inference Engine for High-Throughput Workloads
Jordan Juravsky
Stanford
Ayush Chakravarthy

Stanford
TL;DR
We’re releasing Tokasaurus, a new LLM inference engine optimized for throughput-intensive workloads. With small models, Tokasaurus benefits from very low CPU overhead and dynamic
Hydragen
grouping to exploit shared prefixes. For larger models, Tokasaurus supports async tensor parallelism for GPUs with NVLink and a fast implementation of pipeline parallelism for GPUs without. On throughput-focused benchmarks, Tokasaurus can outperform vLLM and SGLang by up to 3x+.
Table of Contents
Intro
Optimizing Small Models
Optimizing Big Models
Try it Out
Benchmarking Details
Acknowledgements
Intro
As LLMs get
smarter, faster, and cheaper,
the community keeps finding new ways to use them. Our own recent work has explored using models to
scan every file in a codebase
,
sample 10,000 attempts for math and code problems
, and
collaborate with other models to minimize cloud costs
. Inference is now also an important part of the training process, where we use models to
generate synthetic data
or as part of
RL pipelines
that generate and train on model completions.
Crucially, these new inference workloads look quite different than the original LLM use case of serving a chatbot. Here, we care primarily about the total time and cost required to complete a large batch of sequences, and we care much less (if at all) about the individual latency of a single generation. In other words, we want high throughput!
Open-source inference engines (i.e. dedicated systems for running efficient LLM inference) like
FlexGen
,
vLLM
, and
SGLang
have been enormously valuable to the community. Inspired by and learning from these projects, we built a new engine,
Tokasaurus
, designed from the ground up to handle throughput-focused workloads. We’ve optimized Tokasaurus for efficiently serving large and small models alike, allowing it to outperform existing engines on throughput benchmarks. In the rest of this blog, we’ll walk through some of these optimizations and show off a few settings where Tokasaurus really shines.
Optimizing Small Models
To benchmark Tokasaurus with small models, we’ll use two workloads:
Completing chatbot prompts from the ShareGPT dataset (this is a common benchmark for testing inference engines).
Reproducing an experiment from
Large Language Monkeys
, where we take 128 problems from the
GSM8K
math dataset and sample 1024 answers to every problem. The distinguishing feature of this workload is that there’s a lot of prefix sharing across sequences.
Tokasaurus outperforms vLLM and SGLang on both of these benchmarks, in particular achieving over 2x the throughput of other engines on the Large Language Monkeys workload. Two main features contribute to these wins with small models:
Minimizing CPU Overhead
LLM engines perform many different tasks on the CPU, like handling web requests, tokenizing inputs/detokenizing outputs, managing KV cache allocation, and preparing inputs for the model. If these CPU-side tasks cause the GPU-side model to stall, throughput can take a
big hit
. To avoid these stalls, inference engines commonly make many CPU-side
tasks
asynchronous
: while the GPU runs a forward pass for batch N, the CPU-side of the engine post-processes the results from batch N-1 and prepares the inputs for batch N+1.
Tokasaurus goes one step further, making the CPU-side of the engine (what we call the manager) both asynchronous and adaptive. The manager’s goal is to maintain a deep queue of inputs for the model to run forward passes on. The manager monitors the size of this queue and can detect if the model is close to exhausting it (and therefore stalling the GPU). In these cases, the manager will automatically start skipping optional steps (like checking for stop strings and onboarding new sequences) until the model’s input queue is sufficiently deep again. This combination of asynchrony and adaptivity lets Tokasaurus serve small models with much less CPU overhead.
Dynamic Prefix Identification and Exploration
Prefix sharing comes up all the time in LLM inference — not just when repeatedly sampling like in the Large Language Monkeys benchmark, but also when asking many questions about a long document or reusing a system prompt across many chatbot conversations.
Shared prefixes allow attention to be computed more efficiently. We first explored this idea last year with
Hydragen
(aka
cascade attention
and
bifurcated attention
), but at the time we didn’t address the problem of detecting these shared prefixes in an engine where sequences are constantly starting and finishing. With Tokasaurus, we solve this detection problem by running a greedy depth-first search algorithm before every model forward pass that

• Szpadel关注延迟问题，询问吞吐量提升带来的延迟代价，强调这对于“软实时”应用的重要性，尤其是当用户在等待时。
• Radq对项目的简单和良好文档表示赞赏，认为其是高性能推理引擎实现的良好起点，尤其适用于批量推理生成RL rollouts的场景。
• AStonesThrow以幽默方式提到Tokasaurus的命名，并表示计划将该名称用于个人用途，同时提及Meta AI和Llama 4的成功案例，展示该项目的实际应用潜力。
• SymbolicAGI认为，对于低延迟需求，llama.cpp仍然是自托管模型的最佳选择，并提到Ollama在包装llama.cpp方面的领先地位，但对Tokasaurus相关repo曾404表示担忧，庆幸其重新上线。
• DiabloD3对项目用Python编写表示遗憾，认为这可能使其难以在非专家手中得到应用，希望llama.cpp团队能帮助其避免被遗忘。

补充讨论：
• 项目性能和实现的复杂性是主要讨论焦点，尤其是吞吐量和延迟之间的权衡。
• 不同评论者对Tokasaurus的适用场景有不同看法，有的认为其适用于大规模批量处理，有的则认为过于复杂，不适合常见场景。
• 项目的命名和趣味性也被提及，增加了讨论的轻松氛围。
• 项目的技术实现细节，如动态形状处理和Async-TP的具体效果，引发了一些技术上的探讨和兴趣。
• 项目的未来发展和应用潜力也被一些评论者关注，尤其是其在自托管模型和推理引擎实现中的地位。

44210689.article_content:
177950065
story
Meta's Facebook and Instagram apps "were
siphoning people's data through a digital back door
for months,"
writes a Washington Post tech columnist
, citing researchers who found no privacy setting could've stopped what Meta and Yandex were doing, since those two companies "circumvented privacy and security protections that Google set up for Android devices.
"But their tactics underscored some privacy vulnerabilities in web browsers or apps. These steps can reduce your risks."
Stop using the Chrome browser.
Mozilla's
Firefox
, the
Brave
browser and
DuckDuckGo
's browser block many common methods of tracking you from site to site. Chrome, the most popular web browser, does not... For iPhone and Mac folks, Safari also has strong privacy protections.
It's not perfect
, though.  No browser protections are foolproof. The researchers said Firefox on Android devices was partly susceptible to the data harvesting tactics they identified, in addition to Chrome. (DuckDuckGo and Brave largely did block the tactics, the researchers said....)
Delete Meta and Yandex apps on your phone, if you have them.
The tactics described by the European researchers showed that Meta and Yandex are unworthy of your trust. (Yandex is not popular in the United States.)    It might be wise to delete their apps, which give the companies more latitude to collect information that websites generally cannot easily obtain, including your approximate location, your phone's battery level and what other devices, like an Xbox, are connected to your home WiFi.
Know, too, that even if you don't have Meta apps on your phone, and even if you don't use Facebook or Instagram at all, Meta might still harvest information on your activity across the web.

data.author: romanhn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纪念和讨论Bill Atkinson的贡献与影响

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun分享了与Bill Atkinson的个人会面经历，描述了Atkinson在数字摄影方面的技术热情和专业知识，但也表达了对当时仅限于讨论工作相关话题的遗憾。JKCalhoun还反思了自己对Atkinson技术性摄影方式的初步判断，后来因了解Ansel Adams的技术能力而改变看法。

• dkislyuk引用了Walter Isaacson的《Steve Jobs》一书，强调了Atkinson在开发重叠窗口功能时的创新和决心，以及他在技术突破中的“天真”力量。

• matthewn幻想了一个HyperCard没有被忽视而是继续发展的平行时空，认为Atkinson预见了一个人人都能轻松塑造计算体验的世界。

• davisr分享了与Atkinson在视频聊天中建立的个人联系，尽管在软件方面有分歧，但他们在探索未知和人生意义上有一致的目标。

• fotta简短表达了对Atkinson的敬意和哀悼。

• thought_alarm推荐了Atkinson在2013年与Leo Laporte的采访，特别提到与Hypercard起源相关的内容。

• gavmor推荐了关于General Magic的纪录片，强调了Atkinson在这一未被广泛知晓但极具前瞻性的公司中的角色。

• WillAdams提供了几个关于Apple历史的 Folklore.org 链接，特别提到与Atkinson相关的故事，以反驳以代码行数作为衡量开发者贡献的标准。

• bigstrat2003指出Atkinson并非广为人知，因此在分享相关故事时应介绍他的背景和成就。

• bill_mcgonigle批评了当前桌面应用采用不适合WIMP界面的设计趋势，表达了对Atkinson经典WIMP界面设计的怀念和赞赏。

• wesnerm2强调了HyperCard在网络普及之前引入的交互概念对网络发展的影响。

• vercantez高度赞扬Atkinson对计算历史的重大影响，特别提到了Hypercard的超前性。

• agumonkey通过维基百科链接指出了Atkinson在技术领域的多方面贡献，包括Atkinson抖动算法。

• iainmerrick分享了Atkinson在MacPaint中未发布可编辑文本功能的故事，强调了他在技术实现和审美判断上的卓越能力。

• carlosdp重述了Atkinson在开发Mac GUI时因误解Xerox PARC演示而快速实现重叠窗口功能的经典故事。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中反复提及HyperCard及其对现代计算和网络的深远影响，显示出Atkinson工作的开创性意义。
• 多个评论强调了Atkinson在技术创新中的“天真”和直觉力量，以及他在技术开发中展现的判断力和品味。
• 讨论也涉及到Atkinson个人生活中的哲学兴趣和心理准备，特别是在面对生命终结时的态度。

UPDATE: Jun. 6, 2025, 12:05 p.m. EDT
This story has been updated with comments from Proton VPN.
A popular
VPN
service reported a 1,000 percent increase in registrations just 30 minutes after
Pornhub blocked access
in France this week. The adult site reportedly exited its second-biggest market because of a new French
age-verification law
that has a June 7 compliance deadline, per Mashable's
Anna Iovine
.
"5PM - PornHub blocks France from accessing its website," Proton VPN tweeted Wednesday. "5.30PM - @ProtonVPN registrations increase by 1,000%[.] For context, this is more than when TikTok blocked Americans."
This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.
Proton VPN previously
documented
a 490 percent increase in daily signups in mid-January when
TikTok briefly went offline
ahead of a possible ban in the U.S.

A Proton spokesperson tells Mashable that when it built its VPN "to help people in authoritarian countries with online censorship, an access gateway for porn was obviously not what we had in mind." Still, they add, "VPN can be used in this way and signups from France have temporarily increased by a factor of 10."
A
VPN
, or
virtual private network
, is a service that routes your internet traffic through an encrypted tunnel to a remote server before sending it out onto the web. The
main purpose of a VPN
is to reclaim some online privacy from your ISP and other prying eyes. But they're also commonly used to spoof one's location: A VPN can make it appear as though its user is visiting websites from a country they're not physically in.
SEE ALSO:
Why age-verification bills for porn sites won't work
Age-verification laws for adult content have been enacted abroad and in
nearly 20 U.S. states
. They typically require sites to verify their users' ages via facial recognition or government ID. Such laws are intended to restrict children's access to adult content (and in some cases social media), but experts have flagged
free speech and privacy concerns
. What's more, technology like VPNs makes enforcement difficult.
Related Stories
Do age-verification laws work? Not according to this study.
Proton VPN review: Premium, proven privacy and a free tier with no data limits
The best VPNs for 2025, tested by experts
Texas says goodbye to Pornhub — and hello to the top 10 VPNs
For its part, Proton shares these concerns. "There's no such thing as age verification for children only, it's age verification for everyone, and having offshore porn sites or any other third parties collect IDs from adults and becoming a repository of potential blackmail material comes with its own risks," said the company's spokesperson. "A more technically sound approach would be content controls directly implemented on the devices parents chose to give their children."
Founded in 2014, the Swiss-based Proton offers a suite of privacy-centric web services, including email and cloud storage. Its VPN service was launched in 2017 and currently maintains a massive network of more than 13,000 servers in 117 countries worldwide. To date, it's the only VPN we've tested that's won a Mashable Choice Award.

data.author: thomassmith65
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于卢旺达种族灭绝中媒体的作用及其更广泛背景的讨论

不同观点：
• **观点1**：[zahlman] 认为关闭广播电台不会阻止仇恨文化的传播。他指出，仇恨通过口口相传和行动传播，而不仅仅依赖于某个特定的表达渠道。他还提到，电台主持人在没有 censorship 威胁的情况下已经使用隐晦语言，这种“共享语言”有助于加强内部群体的归属感。
• **观点2**：[thomassmith65] 提供了与广播内容相关的音乐人 Simon Bikindi 的信息，指出他在卢旺达种族灭绝后的法律问题，并提供相关维基百科链接供进一步阅读。
• **观点3**：[ge96] 以幽默方式回应，提及音乐和广播的关系，但没有深入讨论核心问题。
• **观点4**：[themgt] 提出多个相关主题，包括“镜中指责”（accusation in a mirror）的概念，指出其在卢旺达种族灭绝宣传中的应用。此外，还讨论了双重种族灭绝理论（double-genocide theory）以及卢旺达爱国阵线（RPF）的战争罪行指控。他们还提到卡加梅（Kagame）的执政记录及其与政治对手失踪和暗杀事件的关联。
• **观点5**：[Barrin92] 认为口头文化相比文字文化在传播仇恨信息方面有更强的影响力。他们提出一种理论，认为现代视听媒介的复兴（如广播和播客）促进了仇恨信息的传播，因为这些媒介易于传播且参与度不批判性强。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：主要争议在于媒体（特别是广播）在传播仇恨和煽动暴力中的实际影响。 [zahlman] 认为关闭广播电台不会阻止仇恨文化的传播，而 [Barrin92] 则强调视听媒介在传播仇恨信息中的强大影响力。
• **其他讨论点**：
  - Simon Bikindi 的案例及其在种族灭绝后的法律问题（[thomassmith65]）。
  - “镜中指责”作为一种宣传手段在卢旺达种族灭绝中的作用（[themgt]）。
  - 关于 RPF 及其在种族灭绝后的战争罪行指控（[themgt]）。
  - 卡加梅的执政及其与政治对手失踪和暗杀事件的关联（[themgt]）。

这些观点和讨论展示了卢旺达种族灭绝及其后续影响的复杂性，并引发了对媒体在传播仇恨和暴力信息中角色的深入思考。

data.title: I'm Wirecutter's water-quality expert. I don't filter my water
data.author: rufus_foreman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自来水安全性及是否需要额外过滤

不同观点：
• [BugsJustFindMe] 认为即使自来水系统报告显示水质达标，用户仍不应完全信任这些报告。他们引用Flint, Michigan的铅管危机为例，强调自己过滤水的重要性。即使水质达标，他们也不喜欢自来水的味道，因此选择安装过滤器。
• [cypherpunks01] 支持使用RO（反渗透）系统过滤水，认为这是比依赖不断变化的专家意见更安全的选择。虽然初期成本较高，但长期来看是值得的投资。
• [dbcooper] 质疑文章作者的资质，认为如果没有相关专业背景（如化学或化学工程学位），作者的长篇大论就不值得信赖。
• [StopDisinfo910] 指出，虽然水质在法律限制内，但这些限制可能过高，特别是对于PFAS（全氟烷基物质和多氟烷基物质）而言，这是对供水方的便利，而非真正保障公众健康。
• [ghostly_s] 和 [calmbonsai] 都对Wirecutter（文章引用的专家来源）的评测质量表示怀疑，认为其已失去可信度。
• [Arch-TK] 来自英国，指出当地自来水有明显的氯味，需要过滤才能饮用，特别是用于制作咖啡时。

补充讨论：
• [timerol] 提到老旧建筑中的铁锈水问题，尽管铁不是有害污染物，但仍然不喜欢看到锈水出现在玻璃杯中。
• [knappe] 提到当地市政水报告不可全信，引用了一些水污染事件，如矿山清理失败导致的水污染，强调水过滤的必要性。
• [storus] 分享个人经历，指出在COVID后饮用自来水导致健康问题，后来发现居住地区PFAS含量高，安装RO系统后问题解决。
• [bilsbie] 担心自来水中的药物残留和微塑料污染。
• [vsskanth] 认为过滤水主要是为了改善口感，而非安全性。
• [internet_points] 质疑普通水过滤器是否会增加水中的PFAS含量，并比较塑料瓶装水和金属管道自来水的PFAS含量。
• [doug-moen] 强调水质因地区而异，其所在地区水中有氯胺，偶尔还有铁锈，使用过滤器能显著改善饮水体验。

争议焦点：
• 市政水报告的可信度：一些人认为不应完全信任市政水质报告，因为历史上曾有水污染危机（如Flint, Michigan的铅污染）。
• 过滤水的必要性：部分人认为过滤水主要是为了改善口感，而非安全性；另一部分人则担心水中的化学物质和微塑料，认为过滤是必要的。
• 专家意见的可信度：一些评论者质疑文章作者的资质和Wirecutter评测的可靠性。

整体来看，讨论围绕自来水是否需要额外过滤展开，涵盖水质安全性、市政报告可信度、个人口感偏好以及对微塑料和化学物质污染的担忧。

data.title: EFF to the FTC: DMCA Section 1201 Creates Anti-Competitive Regulatory Barriers
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了联邦贸易委员会（FTC）为推动 deregulation 而请求公众指出任何“反竞争”法规。电子前沿基金会（EFF）与作者联盟（Authors Alliance）合作，指出《数字千年版权法》第1201条的三年度豁免及其繁琐的申请程序实际上具有反竞争性。第1201条禁止规避版权作品技术保护措施的公平使用，尽管有三年度豁免程序作为补救，但其繁琐的行政流程反而阻碍了公众的合法公平使用。EFF呼吁FTC建议国会废除或改革第1201条，或至少对2026年的下次三年度规则制定过程进行根本性修订，以恢复版权法支持竞争和创新的初衷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何平衡公众权利与版权保护之间的冲突

不同观点：
• mjevans认为，应该采用“失败开放”（fail open）的策略，即让那些有利益相关的人证明公众不应该拥有某些权利，而不是让用户的权利轻易被剥夺。这种观点倾向于保护公众和终端用户的权利，认为在争议中应优先考虑用户的自由，除非有明确的理由限制这些权利。

• hello_computer则对这种观点表示怀疑，提到Yasha Levine的研究揭示了大科技公司与电子前哨基金会（EFF）之间的联系。他们指出大科技公司在版权问题上的双重标准：对于自己的版权非常重视，而对于他人的版权却可能采取漠视态度。这暗示了可能存在的虚伪和利益冲突，尤其是大科技公司可能利用版权作为工具来巩固自己的权力。

补充讨论：
• mjevans的观点反映了对于用户权利的重视，主张改变现状，使权利限制的举证责任归于那些有利益相关的人。

• hello_computer的评论则引入了对大科技公司和版权保护组织的动机质疑，提出了对大科技公司双重标准的担忧，暗示版权问题可能被用作政治和商业工具。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡公众权利与版权持有者的利益，以及大科技公司在其中的角色和动机。mjevans强调用户权利优先，而hello_computer则质疑相关组织和企业的真诚性和一致性。

44210441.article_content:
As part of multi-pronged effort towards deregulation, the Federal Trade Commission has asked the public to identify any and all “anti-competitive” regulations. Working with our friends at Authors Alliance, EFF answered, calling attention to a set of anti-competitive regulations that many don’t  recognize as such: the
triennial exemptions
to Section 1201 of the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, and the cumbersome process on which they depend.
Copyright
grants exclusive rights to creators, but only as a means to serve the broader public interest.
Fair use
and other limitations play a critical role in that service by ensuring that the public can engage in commentary, research, education, innovation, and repair without unjustified restriction. Section 1201 effectively forbids fair uses where those uses require circumventing a software lock (a.k.a. technological protection measures) on a copyrighted work.
Congress realized that Section 1201 had this effect, so it adopted a safety valve—a triennial process by which the Library of Congress could grant exemptions. Under the current rulemaking framework, however, this intended safety valve functions more like a chokepoint. Individuals and organizations seeking an exemption to engage in lawful fair use must navigate a burdensome, time-consuming administrative maze. The existing procedural and regulatory barriers ensure that the rulemaking process—and Section 1201 itself—thwarts, rather than serves, the public interest.
The FTC does not, of course, control Congress or the Library of Congress. But we hope its investigation and any resulting report on anti-competitive regulations will recognize the negative effects of Section 1201 and that the triennial rulemaking process has failed to be the check Congress intended. Our comments urge the FTC to recommend that
Congress
repeal or reform Section 1201. At a minimum, the FTC should advocate for fundamental revisions to the Library of Congress’s next triennial rulemaking process, set for 2026, so that copyright law can once again fulfill its purpose: to support—rather than thwart—competitive and independent innovation.
You can find the full comments
here
.

data.title: My experiment living in a tent in Hong Kong's jungle
data.author: 5mv2
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一项住在帐篷中以节省开支的实验的不同看法和评价

不同观点：
• [Hnrobert42] 赞赏该实验的细节，认为学校环境使实验与普通的帐篷生活有所不同。学费类似于房租，提供了洗澡、电力以及有空调的公共空间（如图书馆），且学校和社区提供了支持。尽管如此，实验仍有其价值，但需要放在具体背景下理解。

• [paxys] 认为仅从投资回报率（ROI）角度分析过于短视。学费本身已经是一笔投入，预期通过教育偿还贷款。为了基本生存（如住房）而增加开销是理所当然的，且能提高教育的投资回报率。长期生活在艰苦条件下会影响学业表现，实验无法持续。

• [iainctduncan] 指出该实验并非真正的无家可归，而是“流浪式露营”（bandit camping）。称之为无家可归是对真正无家可归者的侮辱，因为他们并非出于优化时间的奢侈选择而露营。

• [neilv] 强调了贫穷导致的昂贵风险，如因节省开支导致的伤病可能抵消节省的金额，甚至带来更大的损失。回顾过去的节俭经历，许多节省在当时是必要的，但长远来看并不值得。

• [verall] 对实验地点（假设为UST）的美丽景色表示羡慕，并对实验者的勇气表示赞赏。

• [throe83949449] 批评实验者的“野营”方式不当，尤其是在香港，不当的帐篷搭建（高2.5米且白天不拆除）会影响他人对野营的容忍度。正确的做法应是低姿态帐篷，天黑搭建，天亮前撤离。

• [msgodel] 认为帐篷不是长期居住的好选择，无法有效抵御动物，车辆会是更好的选择。

补充讨论：
• [ambicapter] 对文章中提到的“社区支持”部分表示感动。
• [m3kw9] 和 [hooverd] 对实验表示欣赏和乐观态度。
• [ejoso] 认为实验者的选择大胆且激励人心。
• [Profan] 对实验的性质表示困惑，称之为“无家可归角色扮演”（homeless larping），质疑其实际意义。

争议焦点：该实验是否真正反映了无家可归的现实，以及其实际价值和长期可行性。

data.title: Chimera – a Linux that isn't GNU/Linux
data.author: leephillips
data.article_summary: Chimera Linux是一个正在开发的新Linux发行版，不同于典型的GNU/Linux，它不使用GNU组件，也不使用systemd。该项目由捷克程序员Daniel "q66" Kolesa于2021年中开始，目标是在今年春季达到alpha测试阶段。Chimera使用LLVM编译，musl C库，Dinit初始化系统，并从FreeBSD引入大量用户态组件。它保持与Linux的二进制兼容性，但试图在设计上引入BSD的简洁性。Kolesa还开发了chimerautils以替代GNU coreutils。尽管项目仍在初期，但它已经支持ppc64le、x86_64、aarch64和RISC-V_64四种架构，并提供live media和根文件系统下载。目前桌面环境仅提供GNOME on Wayland。

Spotted in the wild: Chimera – a Linux that
isn't
GNU/Linux
78
It's not yet reached alpha, but it's already breaking new ground
Liam Proven
Mon 13 Feb 2023
//
11:42 UTC
FOSDEM
Chimera Linux is a new distro under construction that is not only systemd-free, it's GNU-free as well. Its creator hopes to reach alpha testing this spring.
Chimera Linux
is a new project which began in mid-2021, but has already made considerable progress. Its solo developer is Czech programmer Daniel
"q66"
Kolesa, who gave a
talk
about his project at FOSDEM last weekend.
His talk was part of the FOSDEM's BSD program stream, which itself is a hint that this is not a typical Linux distribution. This is reflected in its name: the original
chimera
was a mythical creature whose body was made up of parts of different animals. There's a certain kind of Unix geek who insists that
Linux should properly be called GNU/Linux
, because the kernel is built with the
GNU C Compiler
, everything is linked against the
GNU C library
, uses the
GNU coreutils
, and usually multiple other components from the GNU Project.
Chimera Linux is an existence proof that this is not a hard requirement: it avoids all of these. Chimera is compiled with LLVM, uses the same
musl
C library and packaging tools as the
lightweight Alpine Linux distro
, the new
Dinit
init
system, and much of the rest of the userland is drawn from
the current version of FreeBSD
. If things go according to plan, Kolesa hopes to release the first alpha version around the same time as the planned FreeBSD
version 13.2
, so that he can rebase on that version of the underlying tools.
Kolesa's talk is recommended, but be warned, it's very technical. For a quick overview, you can read his
presentation
(PDF).
One of the things that BSD fans tend to praise is the sort of somewhat abstract virtue that appeals to hardcore Unix types: each BSD keeps the source code of the core OS in a single directory tree, making it possible to build the entire thing in a single operation. Third-party components are relegated to an external "ports tree". A Linux distro, on the other hand, is not so much "an operating system" as several thousand separately-developed OS components all flying in
extremely
close formation.
Chimera is an attempt to bring some of that design clarity to Linux. It's not all FreeBSD all the way down: this is still a Linux-based OS, and it remains binary-compatible with Linux. In a way, Chimera is the inverse of the now unmaintained
Debian GNU/kFreeBSD
. That project put the GNU userland and Debian tools on top of a BSD kernel.
Instead, Chimera puts a ported version of quite a lot of the FreeBSD userland on top of the Linux kernel, with a native Linux, but non-GNU, C library. Another distro that uses the musl libc is
the minimalist rolling-release Void Linux
, of which Kolesa is a former developer.
An important part of this is replacing the GNU coreutils. Before attempting to port the FreeBSD equivalent across himself, he found an existing such project:
bsdutils
. He upstreamed some fixes for this, but ended up forking it to create his own version:
chimerautils
.
Aside from the these, the C library and the init system, Chimera uses several other non-FreeBSD tools. Although he is offering his patches to the FreeBSD code back upstream, and some are being picked up, he tried and then discarded FreeBSD's
pkg
tool, commenting that "it's quite obvious that it's mainly all geared towards FreeBSD usage right now." (To be fair, that does seem reasonable enough to us.)
Instead, he uses
apk
, which is short for
Alpine Package Keeper
and which he says "ended up proving to be a great fit". Even here, though, he's ahead of the curve, with his
apk
command based on APK version 3, which is not yet used in Alpine itself. APK 3 moves away from using tarballs and "has its own, custom, structured package format, which should help with avoiding vulnerabilities in the package manager."
There are many signs of this kind of attention to detail in his talk: checking for existing work, evaluating alternatives with an open mind, and cherry-picking then adapting the best bits.
For now, Chimera is still in its preliminary stages, but astonishingly, the project already supports four architectures. Kolesa told us:
ppc64le
is my workstation, so that's the primary development target;
x86_64
, for most people's computers;
aarch64
for my single-board systems; and RISC-V_64, because I thought it would be cool to have it early while most distros are still figuring it out. (And also, I own the
HiFive Unmatched
board from SiFive, and thought it would be sad to leave it mostly unused.)
There are live media and root filesystems available for
download
. It's significant that the only desktop on offer right now is GNOME on Wayland (although other desktops will be supported later) – it's one of the bigger and more complex desktops out there, with significant dependencies, including on parts of sy

data.title: Why Pandas feels clunky when coming from R (2024)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 这篇文章比较了使用R语言的tidyverse和Python的pandas进行数据分析的体验。作者作为一个R语言的坚定支持者，在必须使用Python工作五年后，仍然觉得pandas操作不如tidyverse流畅。文章通过一个简单的购买数据分析示例，逐步展示了如何在R和Python中完成相同的任务。在R中，使用tidyverse的管道操作符可以很直观地进行数据处理、分组和汇总，而在Python中，尽管pandas也能完成相同任务，但代码较为冗长，且有多种实现方式，不如R直观。作者认为，对于习惯tidyverse的人来说，解释pandas的不足之处往往是困难的，因为pandas在Python数据科学中已被广泛接受为强大工具，但其使用体验仍不如tidyverse流畅。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python与R在数据科学和科学计算中的优缺点，以及可能的改进方向

不同观点：
• [支持Python但指出其问题] dleather认为Python在工业界和包生态系统中有优势，但其数据科学和科学计算的工作流很麻烦。每个包都有自己的语法，Pandas中Series和DataFrames的区别让人困惑。他建议需要一个统一的核心数据科学/科学计算栈。
• [R的怀旧与尝试改进] emehex怀念R的dplyr和hadleyverse，并尝试通过创建"redframes"包来解决Pandas中的问题，但未获广泛接受。
• [R的局限性] BDPW从Python转向R的经历表明，R在处理复杂或不寻常的数据操作时令人沮丧，数据访问不透明，难以理解底层操作。
• [Polars的比较] great_wubwub使用Polars代替Pandas，感觉更流畅，并询问Polars与R的比较。
• [Ibis的推荐] dkdcio推荐尝试Ibis，认为它解决了Pandas的许多问题，由Pandas的创建者 originally 开发。
• [书籍作者的观点] __mharrison__提到其书籍读者反馈Effective Pandas帮助他们更适应R的操作方式，但他本人未使用过R。
• [RStudio的优点] wodenokoto强调RStudio在自动完成和理解dplyr DSL方面的优势。

补充讨论：
• [Pandas的问题] smabie指出Pandas的"原罪"是行索引，暗示这是许多问题的根源。
• [包的生态与选择] 讨论中多次提到各种包（如dplyr、Pandas、Ibis、Polars）的优缺点和使用体验，反映出在数据科学中包的选择和适应性是一个重要讨论点。
• [行业使用情况] BDPW询问当前研究领域中R的使用情况，显示出对不同语言在实际研究中应用的关注。

争议焦点：
• Python与R在数据科学中的优劣：dleather和emehex等对Python和R的不同看法，以及各自包的优缺点，构成了主要争议点。

44210614.article_content:
Five years ago I started a new role and I suddenly found myself, a
staunch R fan, having to code in Python on a daily basis. Working with
data, most of my Python work involved using
pandas
, the Python data frame library,
and initially I found it quite hard and clunky to use, being used to the
silky smooth
API of R’s
tidyverse
. And
you know what? It still feels hard and clunky, even now, 5 years later!
But, what seems even harder, is explaining to “Python people” what they
are missing out on. From their perspective, pandas is this fantastic
tool that makes Data Science in Python possible. And it is a fantastic
tool, don’t get me wrong, but if you, like me, end up in many “pandas is
great, but…”-type discussions and are lacking clear examples to link to;
here’s a somewhat typical example of a simple analysis, built from the
ground up, that flows nicely in R and the tidyverse but that becomes
clunky and complicated using Python and pandas.
Let’s first step through a short analysis of purchases using R and the
tidyverse. After that we’ll see how the same solution using Python and
pandas compares.
Analyzing
purchases
in R
We’ve been given a table of
purchases
with different
amount
s, where the customer could have received a
discount
and where
each purchase happened in a
country
. Finance now wants to know: How
much do we typically sell in each country? Let’s read in the data and
take a look:
library
(tidyverse)
purchases
<-
read_csv
(
"purchases.csv"
)
purchases
|>
head
()

country amount discount
<chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>

3 USA       3000       20

here’s how a quick pipeline could be built up, answering Finance’s
question.
“How much do we sell..? Let’s take the total sum!”
purchases
$
amount
|>
sum
()

purchases

(country)

that changed/moved)

data.title: Low-cost Android devices turn home networks into crime platforms
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了数百万低成本Android设备感染了名为BadBox的恶意软件，该软件源自2016年发现的Triada恶意程序。BadBox能将消费者网络变成传播恶意软件和进行非法活动的平台，包括广告欺诈和创建虚假账户。尽管谷歌曾采取措施阻止Triada，但2019年和2023年此类攻击再次出现，影响了成千上万台设备。2023年，安全公司Human Security报告了预装在大批中国制造设备上的BigBox恶意软件。FBI警告消费者警惕设备感染迹象，如自动连接恶意应用市场和请求关闭Play Protect。建议消费者注意15种受影响电视型号，并小心来自未知来源的低成本设备。

Millions of low-cost devices for media streaming, in-vehicle entertainment, and video projection are infected with malware that turns consumer networks into platforms for distributing malware, concealing nefarious communications, and performing other illicit activities, the FBI has warned.
The malware infecting these devices, known as BadBox, is based on Triada, a malware strain
discovered
in 2016 by Kaspersky Lab, which called it "one of the most advanced mobile Trojans" the security firm's analysts had ever encountered. It employed an impressive kit of tools, including rooting exploits that bypassed security protections built into Android and functions for modifying the Android OS's all-powerful Zygote process. Google eventually updated Android to block the methods Triada used to infect devices.
The threat remains
A year later, Triada returned, only this time, devices came pre-infected before they reached consumers’ hands. In 2019, Google
confirmed
that the supply-chain attack affected thousands of devices and that the company had once again taken measures to thwart it.
In 2023, security firm Human Security reported on BigBox, a Triada-derived backdoor it found preinstalled on
thousands of devices
manufactured in China. The malware, which Human Security estimated was installed on 74,000 devices around the world, facilitated a range of illicit activities, including advertising fraud, residential proxy services, the creation of fake Gmail and WhatsApp accounts, and infecting other Internet-connected devices.
In March, Google and a consortium of other Internet organizations took part in a
coordinated action
to disrupt BadBox 2.0, a new campaign affecting more than 1 million low-priced, off-brand Android devices. The infected devices were based on the Android Open Source Project, not the Android TV OS. They also weren't certified under Google’s Play Protect security program. Human Security identified more than a dozen TV models that were impacted. It was the second BadBox disruption action in as many years.
On Thursday, the FBI
warned
that the BadBox threat remained and urged consumers to look for signs their devices may be infected.
“The public is urged to evaluate IoT devices in their home for any indications of compromise and consider disconnecting suspicious devices from their networks,” the public service announcement stated.
Unfortunately, there are few visible signs of such infections that can be spotted by average consumers. The FBI said possible signs are automatic connections to malicious app markets and requests to disable Play Protect. The better course of action is to look for any of the 15 models identified by Human Security and replace any that are found. People should be extra wary of low-cost devices from unknown sources.

data.title: Cloudflare Warns EU About Extensive Piracy Overblocking, Calls for Safeguards
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary: Cloudflare警告欧盟关于打击盗版的过度封锁问题，呼吁建立保障措施。欧盟此前建议成员国迅速下架盗版直播，但未采取强制措施。权利持有人希望推行更强大的立法和半自动化封锁机制，类似措施已在意大利、西班牙和法国实施。然而，Cloudflare反对自动化封锁，指出这会导致合法用户和企业受到重大附带损害。例如，封锁一个IP地址可能导致成千上万个域名无法访问。Cloudflare强调，不应将封锁扩展至全球DNS解析器和VPN，这些服务在全球运营，地域限制困难，且干涉这些服务可能侵犯隐私和言论自由。Cloudflare建议，封锁应作为最后手段，并呼吁提高透明度、建立保障措施和加强合作来应对盗版问题。

44210491.article_content:
Cloudflare Warns EU About Extensive Piracy Overblocking, Calls for Safeguards
Two years ago, the European Commission published a non-binding recommendation to tackle the problem of live-streaming piracy, sports in particular.
For instance, the EU encouraged member states to introduce measures to facilitate prompt takedowns of live streams, while service providers and rightsholders were encouraged to tackle challenges through collaboration.
To the disappointment of many rightsholders, the recommendation required no mandatory action by EU member states. So, when the Commission recently launched an evaluation asking stakeholders to share their views on the recommendation, many asked for more robust legislation.
Advanced piracy blocking systems are high on the agenda. Semi-automated mechanisms capable of blocking sources quickly are preferred. These should be implemented by ISPs, but rightsholders see a role for DNS services and VPNs too.
Variations on this type of mechanism are currently active in Italy, Spain and France. Rightsholders, including the MPA and DAZN, mentioned this in their responses to the Commission, calling for expansion in the EU. However, not everyone agrees that broader and more automated blocking efforts are the right path forward.
Cloudflare Issues Stark ‘Blocking’ Warning
American tech giant Cloudflare, which provides CDN, proxy and DNS services, is fiercely against automated blockades. The company has been at the center of various blocking actions in recent months, as its infrastructure was targeted in Italy, Spain, and France.
In some instances, this has led to overblocking where legitimate Cloudflare customers (and their users) were hit as collateral damage.
“Over the past two years, we have witnessed disproportionate and damaging efforts by rightsholders to use blocking measures to tackle piracy online, particularly in relation to unauthorized live streaming of sports,” Cloudflare writes.
From Cloudflare’s submission
Cloudflare notes that pressure from rightsholders has led some European national governments to implement “problematic and imprecise” blocking mechanisms. It says that these blocking tools “often lack due process” and result in “significant collateral damage” for legitimate internet users and businesses across the EU.
As an intermediary, Cloudflare’s infrastructure and IP-addresses are used by pirate sites and services. However, since these are shared with innocent sites, blocking renders those inaccessible too.
“Blocking one IP address, thus can render thousands, tens of thousands, or even hundreds of thousands of domains unreachable,” Cloudflare warns.
Italy, Spain, and France
Cloudflare specifically highlights Italy, Spain, and France as countries where problems have emerged. The Italian
“Piracy Shield” law
has resulted in “overblocking on a massive scale,” the company says, adding that it violates the Charter of Fundamental Rights and EU law.
In Spain, blocking orders also caused substantial
collateral damage
. Cloudflare explains that, due to a broad court order that included Cloudflare IP-addresses, millions of Spanish users were blocked from accessing thousands of non-targeted websites.
“This blunt approach not only demonstrates a fundamental misunderstanding of how the Internet works, it also raises significant questions about compliance with the European Union’s Open Internet Regulation,” Cloudflare writes.
In France, meanwhile, courts have
ordered VPN providers
and
DNS resolvers
to block pirate sites. At the same time, there are plans to update the law to enable blockades of pirated live sports broadcasts in real-time, which also raises overblocking concerns.
No VPN and DNS Blocking
Cloudflare urges the EU to tread with caution going forward. Instead of updating the law to enable broader blocking powers, it calls for limiting the blocking efforts.
For example, it argues that blocking orders should never extend to core, global Internet technologies such as global DNS resolvers and VPNs. These services operate globally and can’t easily restrict blocking measures geographically, the company notes.
“Blocking applied to an ISP-owned DNS resolver will have a geographically restricted effect, since an ISP typically only serves users in one country. In contrast, public DNS resolvers or VPN providers operate globally.”
Aside from the technical challenges, Cloudflare notes that VPNs and proxies are widely used to protect free expression. Interfering with these services through onerous regulation could amount to a violation of privacy and freedom of expression.
Transparency, Safeguards and Compensation
Cloudflare recognizes that piracy is a real problem that needs to be addressed. However, it believes that more extensive blocking is not necessarily the answer. Instead, it calls for more transparency, proper safeguards, and cooperation between all stakeholders.

The soft, waxy "solid refrigerant" being investigated in a U.K. laboratory may not look very exciting, but its unusual properties promise an air-conditioning revolution that could eliminate the need for greenhouse gases.
The substance's temperature can vary by more than 50 degrees Celsius (90 degrees Fahrenheit) under pressure, and unlike the gases currently used in appliances solid refrigerants, it does not leak.
"They don't contribute to global warming, but also they are potentially more energy efficient," said Xavier Moya, a professor of materials physics at the University of Cambridge.

data.title: Unfit for Work – The startling rise of disability in America
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary:
过去30年，美国领取残疾补助的人数大幅增加，尽管医疗进步让许多人可以继续工作，且新法律禁止职场歧视残疾人。目前，每月有1400万人领取政府残疾补助，联邦政府在残疾补助上的支出超过食品券和福利总和。然而，这些依赖残疾支付的人往往在社会安全网的讨论中被忽视，绝大多数人不工作，也不被计入失业者。

在阿拉巴马州的黑尔县，近四分之一劳动年龄的成年人领取残疾补助。许多人因背痛等问题被判定为残疾，但具体标准模糊，依赖医生和法庭的判断，尤其是背痛和精神疾病等。医生佩里·廷伯莱克常被提及，他在贫困地区工作，根据病人的教育程度等因素判断他们是否能工作。这一现象反映了美国老龄化劳动力及隐藏的、日益昂贵的社会安全网问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于残疾状态、残疾福利制度（如SSDI）、以及替代方案（如UBI）的讨论。

不同观点：
• AndrewKemendo认为，尽管自己有合法的残疾身份，但周围有不少能力和体力不如自己的人并未被视为残疾。他认为大多数人缺乏独立生活和自我提升的能力，甚至可以被视为“残疾”。他提出理想状态是100%的人类都享受残疾福利或类似的全民基本收入（UBI），因为自动化系统能够替代人力劳动。
  
• lokar和pragmatic提到该评论可能源自2013年，暗示讨论内容可能已过时。

• olalonde提到关于残疾工人的数据，指出如果他们恢复工作会失去残疾身份，认为这是一种“贫困陷阱”，因为冒着失去终身免费收入的风险去从事不稳定的低薪工作并不划算。

• nlh分享了一个个人经历，指出有人通过虚假声称获得永久残疾身份，批评了系统的漏洞。

• cebert支持引入全民基本收入（UBI），认为这能帮助那些无法找到合适工作的人，而不必让他们通过宣告残疾来获取基本收入。他还提到AI可能取代大量工作，未来对社会安全网的需求将更加迫切。

• sgnelson指出，现代经济对低技能劳动力的需求减少，导致那些智力或教育水平较低的人更难找到合适的工作。

• Hilift提供了关于美国各州 Medicaid 预算压力的数据，强调需要通过要求受助者上学或从事志愿活动来减少开支，认为当前的医疗补助制度不可持续。

• wyldfire提到Eric Conn的欺诈案件，指出残疾福利系统中存在腐败问题。

• dhosek引用Last Week Tonight节目，指出了SSDI制度在实践中的负面问题。

• Animats认为，过去30年经济发生了根本性变化，许多人因缺乏技能和教育而无法适应新经济，并对UBI表示了一定支持。

• vjvjvjvjghv指出，残疾身份往往是人们在没有任何其他福利选项时获取支持的唯一途径。

By Chana Joffe-Walt
In the past three decades, the number of Americans who are on disability has skyrocketed. The rise has come even as medical advances have allowed many more people to remain on the job, and new laws have banned workplace discrimination against the disabled. Every month, 14 million people now get a disability check from the government.
The federal government spends more money each year on cash payments for disabled former workers than it spends on food stamps and welfare combined. Yet people relying on disability payments are often overlooked in discussions of the social safety net. The vast majority of people on federal disability do not work.
[1]
Yet because they are not technically part of the labor force, they are not counted among the unemployed.
In other words, people on disability don't show up in any of the places we usually look to see how the economy is doing. But the story of these programs -- who goes on them, and why, and what happens after that -- is, to a large extent, the story of the U.S. economy. It's the story not only of an aging workforce, but also of a hidden, increasingly expensive safety net.
For the past six months, I've been reporting on the growth of federal disability programs. I've been trying to understand what disability means for American workers, and, more broadly, what it means for poor people in America nearly 20 years after we ended welfare as we knew it. Here's what I found.
One In Four
Credit: Brinson Banks for NPR
Hale County, Alabama
In Hale County, Alabama, nearly 1 in 4 working-age adults is on disability.
[2]
On the day government checks come in every month, banks stay open late, Main Street fills up with cars, and anybody looking to unload an old TV or armchair has a yard sale.
Sonny Ryan, a retired judge in town, didn't hear disability cases in his courtroom. But the subject came up often. He described one exchange he had with a man who was on disability but looked healthy.
"Just out of curiosity, what is your disability?" the judge asked from the bench.
"I have high blood pressure," the man said.
"So do I," the judge said. "What else?"
"I have diabetes."
"So do I."
There's no diagnosis called disability.  You don't go to the doctor and the doctor says, "We've run the tests and it looks like you have disability."  It's squishy enough that you can end up with one person with high blood pressure who is labeled disabled and another who is not.
I talked to lots of people in Hale County who were on disability. Sometimes, the disability seemed unambiguous.
"I was in a 1990 Jeep Cherokee Laredo," Dane Mitchell, a 23-year-old guy I met in a coffee shop, told me. "I flipped it both ways, flew 165 feet from the Jeep, going through 12 to 14,000 volts of electrical lines.  Then I landed into a briar patch. I broke all five of my right toes, my right hip, seven of my vertebrae, shattering one, breaking a right rib, punctured my lung, and then I cracked my neck."
Other stories seemed less clear. I sat with lots of women in Hale County who told me how their backs kept them up at night and made it hard for them to stand on the job. "I used to cry to try to work," one woman told me. "It was so painful."
People don't seem to be faking this pain, but it gets confusing. I have back pain.  My editor has a herniated disc, and he works harder than anyone I know.  There must be millions of people with asthma and diabetes who go to work every day. Who gets to decide whether, say, back pain makes someone disabled?
As far as the federal government is concerned, you're disabled if you have a medical condition that makes it impossible to work. In practice, it's a judgment call made in doctors' offices and courtrooms around the country. The health problems where there is most latitude for judgment -- back pain, mental illness -- are among the fastest growing causes of disability.
Source: Social Security Administration
Credit: Lam Thuy Vo / NPR
In Hale County, there was one guy whose name was mentioned in almost every story about becoming disabled: Dr. Perry Timberlake. I began to wonder if he was the reason so many people in Hale County are on disability. Maybe he was running some sort of disability scam, referring tons of people into the program.
After sitting in the waiting room of his clinic several mornings in a row, I met Dr. Timberlake. It turns out, there is nothing shifty about him. He is a doctor in a very poor place where pretty much every person who comes into his office tells him they are in pain.
"We talk about the pain and what itâs like," he says. "I always ask them, 'What grade did you finish?'"
What grade did you finish, of course, is not really a medical question. But Dr. Timberlake believes he needs this information in disability cases because people who have only a high school education aren't going to be able to get a sit-down job.
Dr. Timberlake is making a judgment call that if you have a particular back problem and a college degree, you're not disab

过去30年，美国领取残疾补助的人数大幅增加，尽管医疗进步让许多人可以继续工作，且新法律禁止职场歧视残疾人。目前，每月有1400万人领取政府残疾补助，联邦政府在残疾补助上的支出超过食品券和福利总和。然而，这些依赖残疾支付的人往往在社会安全网的讨论中被忽视，绝大多数人不工作，也不被计入失业者。

在阿拉巴马州的黑尔县，近四分之一劳动年龄的成年人领取残疾补助。许多人因背痛等问题被判定为残疾，但具体标准模糊，依赖医生和法庭的判断，尤其是背痛和精神疾病等。医生佩里·廷伯莱克常被提及，他在贫困地区工作，根据病人的教育程度等因素判断他们是否能工作。这一现象反映了美国老龄化劳动力及隐藏的、日益昂贵的社会安全网问题。

data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高级语音模式（Voice Mode）的质量和问题

不同观点：
• zaptrem：承认在高级语音模式中仍然存在罕见的"幻觉"问题，即产生意外的声音如广告、胡言乱语或背景音乐。他认为这可能是模型在播客数据上训练以获得自然语调的副作用。他还表示希望听到这些"幻觉"现象的样本，提到在最初的发布直播中曾有类似的背景音乐幻觉现象。

• TheTaytay：更喜欢早期的纯文本到语音和语音到文本的模式，认为虽然声音质量不如现在，但更为智能和稳定。他指出，当前的高级语音模式经常出错，并且会重复犯错，而纯文本版的高级大语言模型已经很久没有出现这些问题了。

• kubb：注意到高级语音模式的质量相比之前有所下降，特别是在语调和情感表达方面。他提到声音变得冷漠且语调怪异，尤其在用于外语对话练习时，质量明显变差。

• tallytarik：对高级语音模式中出现的幻觉问题感到无奈，认为这种情况在现实生活中发生并不好笑，暗示这种问题应该尽快解决。

补充讨论：
• 用户对高级语音模式的期望和实际体验之间的差距是讨论的焦点之一。
• 幻觉问题（产生意外声音）是用户关注的一个技术问题，zaptrem甚至对这一现象表现出一定的好奇心，希望听到更多实例。
• 不同的用户对语音模式的变化和质量下降有不同的感受，部分用户（如 TheTaytay 和 kubb）对当前版本的性能表示不满，怀念早期版本的稳定性。
• 整体来看，用户对高级语音模式的改进有较高的期待，特别是对其稳定性和准确性的要求。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Atkinson dithering算法的应用及其相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• AndrewStephens认为该实现很棒，并提到Atkinson dithering让他想起过去的界面，特别提到该算法在旧款Mac等清晰显示器上的表现非常酷，具有80年代的风格。他提到在自己的游戏项目中使用了该算法，并注意到他的Atkinson dithering相关项目今天访问量增加，感到有些悲伤。

• JKCalhoun分享了个人经历，表示Atkinson dithering是他最喜欢的黑白抖动算法，回忆了在大学时使用该算法扫描图像并制作Mac游戏logo的经历。他后来尝试了其他算法，认为Atkinson的扩散效果非常出色。最近在一个eInk日历项目中再次使用了类似的Atkinson dithering效果处理月相图片。

• throwanem从技术角度提出改进建议，指出可以通过给下载文件指定默认名称和.png扩展名来优化实现，并提供了一个开发者文档链接供参考。

• ddingus简短提到自己刚转换了家庭立体声音响，在2560x1440分辨率下效果非常好，称赞了dithering的效果。

• amelius提供了Python中实现Atkinson dithering的库链接，并提醒查看帮助文档以获取更多信息。

• larodi提出了一个问题，询问该讨论是否与当天去世的Atkinson有关，并质疑这是否是一种致敬。这一问题引发了对该技术讨论背景的关注，可能涉及对技术先驱的悼念。

争议焦点：

Self-Host & Tech Independence: The Joy of Building Your Own
A personal journey.
Productivity
2025-06-07
2168 words
11 minutes
Contents
After watching the two
PewDiePie
videos where he learned about
installing Arch
(something considered quite hard, even for Linux enthusiasts) and
building three products
(camera for the dog, weather/drinking/meditation device, and who knows what comes next) based on open-source, 3D-printed parts, I started wondering about building things yourself, self-hosting, and tech independence. Something dear to my heart for a while.
If people ask me how they should start writing or how to get a job, I always say to buy a domain first. Secondly, host your own blog website if you have the technical skills (although it’s not so hard anymore). Because all of this compounds over time. Of course, you can start with a ready-made blog and a URL not yours, but if you want to do it long term, I saw many people changing from
WordPress
to Medium to Substack to Ghost, so what’s next? Over that time, sometimes they didn’t migrate their long-effort blog posts but started new.
Every time they had a new domain. To me, that’s so sad. Of course, you have learned a lot, and sometimes it’s also good to start new, but imagine instead if that happened over 10 years. If you compare that 10-year blog that has the same domain, keeping hard-earned backlinks, showcasing your long-term investment with old blog posts, even though they might not be as good as current ones (but doesn’t that happen all the time), what a huge difference that would be?
As someone who has hosted my own stuff for quite a while, and has been adding more every year, I thought I would write a short article about it.
My Own Story
I self-host
my blog
,
my second brain
,
my book
,
my subscriber list
(with
Listmonk
), implemented my own paywall with
Memberstack
, and have had my own website and blog for almost all my life (started my own domain, built WordPress,
moved
to
GoHugo
).
Lately, I also went into Homelab and built my own Home Server with SSH, backup, photos, Gitea, etc. Setting up my own configuration for Reverse Proxy and SSL Certificates for my Homeserver, creating SSL certificates, setting up SSH keys to SSH into without a loginâall great things you learn along the way.
Initially everything seems hard, but once you know how, it’s kind of obvious and less hard. It’s also, as ThePrimeagen
says
, that there is always a big part of
ignorance
where one tells themselves, “Oh that can’t be that hard”. But then you realize it’s much harder than you thought. But once you overcome the first hurdles, it’s really rewarding, and once working, it just works!
Most of what inspires me to do more is the joy of using something you built yourself, and usually not paying for it. Maybe this is also because of the subscription hell we are living in, where every single app or service can’t be used without a subscription.
How it Started for Me
When I got into
vim
, and especially
Neovim
, all of a sudden I lived in the terminal and knew some of the commands that usually only Linux wizards or nerds know, but now I am one myself :) But with great pride. Find more on my journey on my
PKM Workflow Blog
.
Tech Independence
Tech Independence is something I
learned
from Derek Sivers, and basically means that you do
not depend on any particular company or software
.
The premise is that by learning some of the fundamentals, in this case
Linux
, you can host most things yourself. Not because you need to, but because you want to, and the feeling of using your own services just gives you pleasure. And you learn from it. Derek goes deep in his article. He self-hosts email, contacts & calendar, and your own backup storage. But you can start small. We always believe we just have to use what’s out there to buy, but there are other ways.
Start by buying your own domain today. Put some thought into the name, but don’t overcomplicate it. If you have any success or links whatsoever, you can always move the domain later if you don’t like it (and forward existing blogs to a new domain with not much lost). But you can’t do it if you don’t have your own domain or own hosted server.
Open-Source
Most of it is
Open-Source
and comes when you dabble in Linux. As the story of PewDiePie shows, once you learn Linux, you want to build everything yourself and not pay for anything ð.
Open-source and open-source code is beautiful. It’s much more than just using someone else’s software, but it’s all the millions of people who just give away their work for free. It’s a community of people working for everyone. By putting it on GitHub, people can give feedback (issues) or contribute (Pull Requests), and you as the owner can or cannot listen to it. It’s your choice. Like in the real world.
But most of all, everyone can use your code for free. Some nuances on the licensing, but if you have MIT or some other permissive
License
, everyone can use it.
