data.title: BorgBackup 2 has no server-side append-only anymore
data.author: jaegerma
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了BorgBackup项目中移除对仅追加（append-only）存储支持的更改。仅追加功能依赖于服务器端组件来强制执行，因为这只能在服务器端控制，而不能在客户端控制。在Borg 1.x中，只有使用SSH的仓库支持该功能，而在Borg 2中，包括文件系统、SFTP、Rclone、S3/B3等仓库类型并不具备服务器端强制执行的能力。目前的解决方案建议通过存储层限制删除权限来实现仅追加功能，例如`borg create`使用无删除权限的凭证，而`borg compact`则使用有删除权限的凭证。有开发者对该方案的安全性提出疑问，认为需要某种形式的仅追加支持以防止数据被恶意篡改。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：备份工具的选择与使用，特别是Borg和Restic的优缺点及安全性讨论。

不同观点：
• homebrewer支持使用Restic的append-only模式，结合rest-server后端，通过nginx和HTTPS进行保护，并分享了自己的systemd配置，称已使用五年无问题。
• dblitt提出质疑，认为即使使用无删除权限的凭证来防止客户端被攻破后删除数据，但无法防止客户端覆盖文件。
• puffybuf则提到自己使用device mapper和加密方式进行备份，并编写脚本自动处理异常情况，质疑是否有必要使用BorgBackup，除非是为了节省空间。
• nathants主张备份方案应该简单，并分享了自己的简单备份方案链接，认为备份不应过于复杂。
• neilv分享了自己使用BorgBackup结合append-only和受限SSH的经验，认为这种方法能有效防止设备损坏导致的数据丢失。
• aborsy关心Borg2的beta测试进度，询问何时能正式发布。

Some features like append-only repositories rely on a server-side component that enforces them (because that shall only be controllable server-side, not client-side).
So, that can only work, if such a server-side component exists, which is the case for borg 1.x ssh: repositories (but not for borg 1.x non-ssh: repositories).
For borg2, we currently have:
fs repos
sftp: repos
rclone: repos (enabling many different cloud providers)
s3/b3: repos
ssh: repos using client/server rpc code similar as in borg 1.x
So, only for the last method we have a borg server-side process that could enforce some features, but not for any of the other repo types.
For append-only the current idea is that this should not be done within borg, but solved by a missing repo object delete permission enforced by the storage.
borg create could then use credentials that miss permission to delete, while borg compact would use credentials that include permission to delete.

data.title: Discovering a JDK Race Condition, and Debugging It in 30 Minutes with Fray
data.author: aoli-al
data.article_summary:
文章描述了在使用Fray工具对Fray进行集成测试时，意外发现JDK中的一个死锁问题。问题出现在`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`中，当一个任务被调度而另一个线程同时执行关闭操作时，可能导致任务被无限期阻塞。

具体来说，当`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`处于`SHUTDOWN`状态时，`FutureTask.get`方法可能会无限期等待任务完成。问题源于`schedule`方法在检查执行状态时，假设如果处于`SHUTDOWN`状态，任务会被终止，但实际上任务可能未被处理也未被终止，导致死锁。

Fray通过其确定性回放和调度可视化功能，帮助开发者快速定位问题。在`schedule`和`shutdown`方法的交错执行中，任务未被正确添加到工作线程，且执行状态被错误地设置为`TERMINATED`，导致任务永远不会被执行。

这个问题揭示了JDK中一个潜在的竞态条件，虽然设计上有一些保护机制，但在特定时序下仍可能出现问题。
data.comments_summary:

44211779.article_summary:
文章描述了在使用Fray工具对Fray进行集成测试时，意外发现JDK中的一个死锁问题。问题出现在`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`中，当一个任务被调度而另一个线程同时执行关闭操作时，可能导致任务被无限期阻塞。

具体来说，当`ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor`处于`SHUTDOWN`状态时，`FutureTask.get`方法可能会无限期等待任务完成。问题源于`schedule`方法在检查执行状态时，假设如果处于`SHUTDOWN`状态，任务会被终止，但实际上任务可能未被处理也未被终止，导致死锁。

Fray通过其确定性回放和调度可视化功能，帮助开发者快速定位问题。在`schedule`和`shutdown`方法的交错执行中，任务未被正确添加到工作线程，且执行状态被错误地设置为`TERMINATED`，导致任务永远不会被执行。

这个问题揭示了JDK中一个潜在的竞态条件，虽然设计上有一些保护机制，但在特定时序下仍可能出现问题。

data.author: cinquemb
data.article_summary: PyOpticL是一个用于光学系统布局的Python库，通过代码实现光学元件的自动布局和动态光路计算。它支持无需预先指定坐标的模块化光学系统设计，适用于构建如激光冷却、 trapped ion量子比特等复杂光学系统。该工具可与FreeCAD集成，允许用户通过简单的代码实现光学元件的放置和光路模拟，支持多种光学现象如反射、折射和衍射。此外，PyOpticL还提供了模块化基板和子系统的示例，如激光、饱和吸收光谱和拉曼子系统，适用于原子物理和量子计算实验平台。社区贡献者包括MIT、UC Berkeley等高校的研究人员。

About PyOpticL (Python Optics Layout)
PyOpticL is a Python library for optics layout which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling dynamic layouts with automatic routing and connectivity.
The beam paths are automatically calculated as components are placed in the layout. Component placement can be defined "along beam" to remove the need for hard-coded coordinates. Beam calculations include reflection, transmission, refraction, and diffraction (limited). This library enables a new paradigm of optical engineering using modular sub-systems of modular baseplates with commerical optical elements (see abstraction layers below).
Demonstration with Trapped Ion Qubits:
See our recent preprint for more details about our results using these laser sources and baseplates in our lab:
arXiv:2501.14957 - Qubit operations using a modular optical system engineered with PyOpticL: a code-to-CAD optical layout tool

Install FreeCAD, Python, and Git
Add PyOpticL as an custom addon repository in FreeCAD
Under

enter the following information:
Repository URL:

In the Addon Manager
(Tools>Addon Manager),
search for "PyOpticL" and click install.
Check everything is setup correctly
You should now be able to re-launch FreeCAD and see the "PyOpticL" workbench in the dropdown

data.title: Hollywood Is Already Using AI (and Hiding It)
data.author: 1sembiyan
data.article_summary: 文章描述了在洛杉矶东部一个新的人工智能工作室Asteria Film Co.的开幕活动。该工作室由企业家Bryn Mooser和他的女友、演员兼作家Natasha Lyonne创立。活动展示了由AI生成的诡异短片，引发对AI在好莱坞应用的讨论。Lyonne提到，许多人隐瞒使用AI技术，但她认为应面对而非回避这一趋势。现场的多位业内人士认为，AI在影视行业的应用已是不可避免的趋势，尽管有人担忧其道德和法律问题，如版权侵犯。AI被视为既是好莱坞危机的加速器，也可能为其带来一线生机，因其能生成电影制作的各个元素。然而，行业对AI的态度复杂，有人抗拒，有人则暗中使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在创意产业（如电影、动画等）中的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• **AI对创意工作的影响是正面的**：一些评论认为，AI工具可以作为辅助，帮助创意工作者更快地生成概念和草案，但最终作品的原创性和艺术价值仍然依赖于艺术家的再创作。例如，[bredren]提到自己使用AI生成生日卡概念，然后手动绘制，认为作品的艺术价值不会因AI的参与而降低。

• **AI可能导致某些创意工作的消失**：[bredren]引用一位制片厂高管的话，指出故事板艺术家可能会因为AI的普及而失业，但同时也提到如果艺术家能熟练掌握AI工具，他们可能会获得更多机会。这一观点强调了AI对某些职业的威胁，但也提供了适应和进阶的可能性。

• **AI在创意产业中的应用早有先例**：[simonw]提到《指环王：王者归来》和《复仇者联盟：终局之战》中使用的早期AI特效软件MASSIVE，认为AI技术在创意产业中的应用并不是新现象，且过去并未引发争议。

• **艺术家与科技公司对AI的态度差异**：[est31]观察到科技公司热衷于展示AI的应用，而艺术家则普遍批评和排斥AI，认为这种态度差异值得注意。

• **AI带来的新机遇与可能性**：[AndrewKemendo]对AI创造电影的可能性表示兴奋，并提出谁在开发开源AI工具的问题。此外，[jmugan]认为如果AI能帮助创造更好的故事，那么新一代的创作者将会崛起，传统从业者可能会被取代。

补充讨论：
• **AI对电影质量和行业趋势的影响**：[mwkaufma]提到詹姆斯·卡梅隆与Stability AI合作的项目遭到观众批评，指出AI技术在实际应用中的潜在问题。而[calvinmorrison]则观察到AI可能影响电影拍摄手法和节奏。

• **AI带来的道德和透明度问题**：[throwaway743]质疑是否应该对AI生成的媒体进行标注，并预测AI将导致超个性化、按需生成的媒体消费模式。此外，[antithesizer]提到当AI的使用涉及商业利益时，消费者可能会被误导。

• **AI可能导致行业质量下降**：[leptons]认为AI可能引发行业内的“逐底竞争”，导致整体电影质量下降，并引用《Idiocracy》电影来比喻当前娱乐行业的趋势，表达对AI自动生成内容的担忧。

争议焦点：
• **AI对创意工作的影响是积极还是消极**：一方面，AI可能提升效率并创造新机会；另一方面，它可能导致某些职业的消失和行业质量的下降。

One recent evening on the Eastside of Los Angeles, a couple hundred people gathered in a cavernous old soundstage to celebrate the arrival of a new AI studio — one of the nearly 100 now operating in Hollywood. Called Asteria Film Co., it was founded by Bryn Mooser, a serial entrepreneur, and his girlfriend, the actress and writer Natasha Lyonne. Mooser, 45, is tall with a sculpted jaw and salt-and-pepper beard; he fits the role of a rumpled yet elegant pitchman so well that Cartier shot an advertorial of him titled “The Entrepreneur.” He led me through the studio: a 25,000-square-foot collection of soundstages and a workshop built in 1916 by the producer Mack Sennett, who pioneered new uses of scenic backdrops in early filmmaking. In the lobby, he paused at a glass-encased architectural model of the studio as it looked when it was first built. “There was no roof because they were just using sunlight,” he told me. “It was before electricity.” As Mooser saw it, Asteria fit into a lineage of creatives who had ushered in new eras of filmmaking. He reminded me that Walt Disney was a technologist. So was George Lucas. “The story of Hollywood is the story of technology,” he said.
We met Lyonne in a corner of the studio where uncanny clips generated by Asteria’s AI model were playing on a dozen old-school televisions. The footage was unnerving. Robots with smooth, blank faces typed blindly in an old-fashioned office. Disembodied mannequin heads drifted in space. Lyonne was drinking a sugar-free Red Bull and wearing a structured black velvet jacket with a plunging neckline. She was fresh off a plane from Seattle, where she had done a talk with the science-fiction author Ted Chiang, who has written at length about why AI will never create great art. Over the past few years in Hollywood, it had become clear to Lyonne that many people were not being forthright with how often they were using the technology. “If I’m directing an episode, I like to get really into line items and specifics,” she said. “And you find out that there’s a lot of situations where they’re calling it machine learning or something but, really, it’s AI.” She had begun to do her own research. She read the Oxford scholar Brian Christian and the philosopher Nick Bostrom, who argues that AI presents a significant threat to humanity’s long-term existence. Still, she had come to feel it was too late to “put the genie back in that bottle.” “It’s better to get your hands dirty than pretend it’s not happening,” she said.

This seemed to be the general opinion of those milling around at the party. Many of Lyonne’s frequent collaborators and close friends were in attendance: the director Janicza Bravo, the actresses Clea DuVall and Tessa Thompson. As I wandered past clusters of studio executives in suits and filmmakers in baseball caps and jeans, I heard the word
inevitable
five times. A creative director in a cowboy hat said, “It’s happening whether we like it or not.” Waiting on line by the bar, I asked the comedian Tim Heidecker for his thoughts. “My thoughts are too complicated for a conversation at a party,” he replied. I found a CAA agent sitting in a mostly empty row of vintage wooden theater seats. At CAA, she said, the subject of AI comes up every day. Back in 2023, the agency had launched a project, called the CAA Vault, to capture the likeness of all its clients so it could own and control the rights to their images. “Everyone’s using it,” the agent said. “They just don’t talk about it.” Nearby, a former Netflix exec and current independent producer sipped red wine. She hadn’t told some of her colleagues she was attending the party that night. A director she works with recently told her if anyone at her production company used AI for any part of the process, he would leave. “If they hear me being curious,” she said, “they’re going to be so mad.”
Hollywood has lately been in what media observers have described as an “existential crisis,” an implosion, and a “death spiral.” Studios were making fewer films, and fewer people were watching the ones that got made. Layoffs were mounting. Depending on whom you asked, AI was either hastening the end or offering a lifeline. It had brought a proliferation of tools that were capable, to varying degrees of success, of creating every component of a film: the script, the footage, the soundtrack, the actors. Among the many concerns rattling nerves around town, one significant issue was that nearly every AI model capable of generating video had been trained on vast troves of copyrighted material scraped from the internet without permission or compensation. data.title: Log-Linear Attention
data.author: sva_
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为“对数线性注意力”（Log-Linear Attention）的新机制，以解决Transformer模型中注意力机制存在的计算二次复杂度和内存线性复杂度的问题。对数线性注意力通过使用对数增长的隐藏状态集合替代固定大小的隐藏状态，从而在保持线性注意力高效性的同时，提升了其表达能力。该方法的计算成本是对数线性关系，并且可以应用于现有的线性注意力变体。实验显示，这种方法在性能上优于传统的线性时间变体模型，如Mamba-2和Gated DeltaNet。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Log-linear attention机制的优点和潜在影响，特别是对模型大小和速度的影响]

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：Log-linear attention机制可能不仅能提升模型速度，还能减小模型大小。**iknownothow**提出，既然log-linear attention用对数增长的隐藏状态集替代固定大小的隐藏状态，这是否意味着模型可以变得更小，而不仅仅是在速度上有所提升。这个观点暗示了该机制在模型压缩方面的潜在优势。

• 第二种观点：隐含的不同意见是，log-linear attention的主要优势在于速度提升，而非直接针对模型大小的优化。虽然**iknownothow**提出了模型可能变小的假设，但这一点在原文中未被明确验证或支持，因此可能存在争议。该观点更关注机制在计算效率上的改进，而非存储效率。

补充讨论：
• Log-linear attention机制的核心优势被认为是速度提升，即通过使用对数增长的隐藏状态集来替代传统的固定大小隐藏状态，从而加快模型处理速度。
• 关于模型大小是否会因此减小，目前在讨论中只是一个推测，尚未有明确的数据或结论支持这一观点。因此，模型大小的变化可能需要进一步的实验或理论验证。
• 争议的焦点在于log-linear attention机制是否能在保证性能的前提下，同时实现速度提升和模型大小缩减。这涉及到对新机制在不同应用场景中的实际效果的验证。

Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled Log-Linear Attention, by Han Guo and 5 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
The attention mechanism in Transformers is an important primitive for accurate and scalable sequence modeling. Its quadratic-compute and linear-memory complexity however remain significant bottlenecks. Linear attention and state-space models enable linear-time, constant-memory sequence modeling and can moreover be trained efficiently through matmul-rich parallelization across sequence length. However, at their core these models are still RNNs, and thus their use of a fixed-size hidden state to model the context is a fundamental limitation. This paper develops log-linear attention, an attention mechanism that balances linear attention's efficiency and the expressiveness of softmax attention. Log-linear attention replaces the fixed-size hidden state with a logarithmically growing set of hidden states. We show that with a particular growth function, log-linear attention admits a similarly matmul-rich parallel form whose compute cost is log-linear in sequence length. Log-linear attention is a general framework and can be applied on top of existing linear attention variants. As case studies, we instantiate log-linear variants of two recent architectures -- Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet -- and find they perform well compared to their linear-time variants.

data.title: Who Needs a Belt 3D Printer When You Have a Treadmill?
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 大约五年前，配备传送带的“皮带”3D打印机开始受到关注。与传统固定Y轴不同，这种打印机的Y轴是传送带，可以无限延长，适合打印长物体。尽管仍属小众，但其应用潜力吸引人。为了打印全尺寸皮划艇，Ivan Miranda与Jón Schone合作，将一台跑步机改造成大型皮带3D打印机。打印机并非简单替换Y轴，而是与X、Z轴协作，以一定角度（通常45度）打印，确保每层完整。为实现此几何结构，他们进行了大量定制，如使用定制钢支柱和重型线性导轨。打印机配备了大功率步进电机和定制散热器，以防止过热。最终，他们在布拉格Maker Faire上成功展示了这台打印机及打印出的皮划艇。

44211681.article_content:
About five years ago, “belt” 3D printers starting gaining traction. Instead of a conventional Y axis with a rigid bed, they have a conveyor belt. That enables infinite printing in the Y axis, so it is possible to print very long objects. Belt 3D printers are still pretty niche, but the utility is appealing. Unfortunately, most of them are still desktop-oriented and that limits the size of the objects in the X and Z axes. In order to print an entire full-size kayak, Ivan Miranda teamed up with Jón Schone to
turn a treadmill into an oversized belt 3D printer
.
A belt 3D printer is actually a bit more complicated than described in the introduction. The belt doesn’t replace the Y axis entirely, but rather acts in concert with what would normally be the X and Z axes to print at an angle (usually 45 degrees). That angle is important, because it lets the machine finish an entire layer on top of the belt. Otherwise, the whole part (which could be several feet long) would need to move off of and back on to the belt with every layer — ruining adhesion to the belt.
In this case, Miranda and Schone had to replicate that geometry on the treadmill. The finished printer still looks a lot like a treadmill, which is intentional. But a lot of custom fabrication went into the design in order to achieve the proper geometry. The Z axis, for example, is made of custom steel uprights with heavy duty linear rails. The X axis gantry is also custom and has a beefy linear rail of its own.
That is a lot of weight to move around, so the printer has large, powerful stepper motors. Miranda even had PCBWay mill custom heat sinks to help keep the motors cool, which was important to stop them from melting their 3D-printed mounting brackets. Even the extruder was scaled-up to huge proportions, giving it the ability to push the ridiculous amount of filament necessary to form a kayak through a 1mm nozzle.
To control it all, they used a Duet 3 Main Board paired with a Duet 3 Tool Board. The latter is on the extruder carriage and communicates with the former through a CAN-FD connection, reducing the number of wires going to the extruder.
There were, predictably, lots of challenges to overcome. But Miranda and Schone were successful in the end. The treadmill 3D printer worked and they launched the kayak at Maker Faire Prague earlier this month.

• uaas认为Prometheus和Grafana组合（结合Loki和Tempo）是小型项目的理想选择，尤其在搭配OpenTelemetry进行复杂处理时更为强大。他还警告不要轻信那些声称性能更好、资源占用更少的新兴小项目，因为它们通常伴随着其他成本。

• herbst推荐Shynet作为轻量级的网站访问者追踪系统，强调其简单易用，适合不需要复杂功能的场景。

• Fizzadar支持使用VictoriaMetrics来替代Prometheus，因为其内存使用量显著减少（约为Prometheus的七分之一），同时仍在评估VictoriaLogs。他认为VictoriaMetrics非常出色，并继续使用Grafana作为用户界面。

• bitbasher则提出了更为传统的解决方案，使用logrotate、systemd和`journalctl`命令来管理和查询日志，显示出对简单工具和命令行操作的偏好。

补充讨论：
• uaas强调了OpenTelemetry在监控堆栈中的潜在作用，以及对新兴小项目的谨慎态度。
• Fizzadar通过具体数据（7倍内存减少）来支持VictoriaMetrics的优势，同时也表明了对日志管理工具的持续评估。
• bitbasher的观点展示了使用系统自带工具和命令来进行监控和日志管理的可行性，强调简单和直接。

争议的焦点：
• 选择成熟的Prometheus和Grafana堆栈还是尝试新兴工具如VictoriaMetrics，是讨论中的一个争议点。
• 使用复杂但功能丰富的堆栈还是选择简单轻量的工具（如Shynet或logrotate等）也是讨论中的一个分歧点。

data.title: Meta: Shut down your invasive AI Discover feed
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: Meta正在未经用户明确同意的情况下，将私人AI聊天内容变为公共内容，侵犯用户隐私。Mozilla社区呼吁Meta：立即关闭Discover feed，直到建立有效的隐私保护措施；默认将所有AI互动设为私人，除非用户明确同意公开分享；透明披露有多少用户无意中分享了私人信息；创建简单易用的 opt-out 系统，防止用户数据被用于AI训练；通知并允许受影响用户永久删除其公开内容。Meta正在模糊公私界限，牺牲用户隐私，必须加以制止。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta新推出的独立AI应用中的隐私问题及用户对其功能的理解争议

不同观点：
• 一些用户认为Mozilla对该问题的描述不清晰，甚至有误导之嫌。例如，[mgraczyk]指出Mozilla的批评不实，因为该应用的分享功能操作明确，且隐私保护措施已经到位，默认情况下聊天是私密的。[mgraczyk]还提到Mozilla的许多要求实际上已经实现了。
• 相反，[boroboro4]认为该应用的界面设计存在“暗模式”（dark pattern），因为点击“分享”按钮后必须将聊天公开才能分享，这与用户对“分享”功能的常规理解不符。他指出，用户可能在不知情的情况下将私人聊天公开。
• 另有用户如[iambateman]和[gojomo]要求更多具体例子和上下文来理解Mozilla的担忧，认为当前的信息不够具体，无法明确问题所在。
• [tacker2000]质疑为何Mozilla选择关注这一特定问题，而不是其他更广泛的隐私问题，并对Mozilla作为“隐私守护者”的身份表示怀疑。
• [udev4096]和[DeepYogurt]等用户对Mozilla自身的隐私政策及其技术问题提出批评，认为Mozilla在处理隐私问题时存在虚伪性或技术缺陷。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户如[paxys]和[alex1138]认为，Meta作为一个常有“暗模式”设计历史的公司，出现这种问题并不意外，并对媒体报道中的煽动性语言和缺乏细节表示不满。
• [Sanzig]提到Mozilla自身曾因Firefox的使用条款更改和后续反转事件而受到质疑，认为Mozilla在隐私问题上的立场有些虚伪。
• 还有技术性讨论，如[djaychela]对网页自动填充邮箱时去除尾随空格的技术要求，以及[joshstrange]对“AI Discover Feed”功能的具体信息和操作示例的请求。

争议焦点：Mozilla对Meta AI应用隐私问题的批评是否合理，以及该应用的界面设计是否误导用户公开分享私人聊天。

Meta: Shut Down Your Invasive AI Discover Feed. Now.
Meta is quietly turning private AI chats into public content — and too many people don’t realize it’s happening.
That’s why the Mozilla community is demanding that Meta:
Shut down the Discover feed
until real privacy protections are in place.
Make all AI interactions private by default
with no public sharing option unless explicitly enabled through informed consent.
Provide full transparency
about how many users have unknowingly shared private information.
Create a universal, easy-to-use opt-out system
for all Meta platforms that prevents user data from being used for AI training.
Notify all users whose conversations may have been made public
, and allow them to delete their content permanently.
Meta is blurring the line between private and public — and it’s happening at the cost of our privacy. People have the right to know when they’re speaking in public, especially when they believe they’re speaking in private.

data.title: Swift and the Cute 2d game framework: Setting up a project with CMake
data.author: pusewicz
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何使用CMake搭建一个结合Swift和Cute Framework的游戏项目。Cute Framework是一个用于构建2D游戏的C/C++框架，而Swift则是一种更现代化且更安全的编程语言。文章详细说明了项目设置的步骤，包括安装必要工具（Swift、CMake、Ninja），创建项目目录结构，配置CMake文件以支持C、C++和Swift，设置Swift与C互操作性，以及编写简单的游戏逻辑。最终，通过CMake配置和构建项目，生成可执行的游戏应用。整个过程旨在利用Swift编写游戏逻辑，同时借助C/C++处理性能关键任务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在不同平台和开发环境中配置和使用C++、SDL3、Lua、Swift等语言和工具进行游戏开发的体验与选择

不同观点：
• [90s_dev] 认为在Windows上使用C++、SDL3和Lua开发时，配置过程过于复杂，文档繁多且不易找到相关信息。最终选择了Visual Studio、CMake和vcpkg的组合来简化配置过程。
• [v1sea] 支持使用Swift进行跨平台开发，认为Swift不应仅限于Apple平台，并提到Swift与C++的互操作性在计算机视觉项目中表现良好。
• [DavidPiper] 分享了自己使用Swift与CMake进行跨平台开发的经验，并认为SourceKit LSP和VS Code的组合提供了一个可行的开发环境。
• [corytheboyd] 选择了C#和MonoGame进行2D游戏开发，看重其良好的IDE支持、调试器和热重载功能。尽管如此，他计划在熟悉游戏开发后转向基于SDL3的自定义开发环境，并提到对C/C++项目热重载功能的疑虑。

补充讨论：
• [90s_dev] 询问Cute（类似于SDL或SFML）的实际使用体验，并提供了一个参考链接。
• [titouanch] 提出Swift是否可用于非MacOS和iOS平台游戏开发的疑问，反映了对Swift跨平台能力的关注。
• [taylorallred] 比较了Cute和Raylib，询问两者的优劣。
• [krzat] 认为使用Swift开发应优先选择Swift Package Manager (SPM) 而非CMake。
• [kookamamie] 对可变时间步长在游戏开发中的适用性提出异议，认为其并非最佳选择。
• [shortrounddev2] 质疑为何CMake仍是主流构建工具，暗示可能有更好的替代方案。
• [Kon-Peki] 对语法使用提出修正意见，指出"voilà"的正确用法。

争议焦点：
• 不同工具和语言的选择及其实际开发体验，如C++与Swift的配置复杂性、Swift是否应使用SPM或CMake、以及C#与MonoGame的实际开发体验等。
• 热重载和IDE支持在游戏开发中的重要性，以及C/C++项目中热重载的可行性。

这些观点反映了开发者在选择游戏开发工具和环境时的多样化需求和偏好。

44199699.article_content:
Swift and Cute Framework: Setting up a project with CMake
Jun 6
·
5 min read
·
cute
·
cute-framework
·
cmake
·
swift
·
game-development
Cute Framework
is a simple, yet powerful C/C++ framework for building 2D games using the modern GPU pipeline. While C or C++ is fine,
Swift
is a modern language that many developers prefer for its safety and expressiveness. In this post, we will explore how to set up a project using Cute Framework with
CMake
, enabling you to write your game logic in Swift while leveraging the performance of C/C++ for rendering and other performance-critical tasks.
Prerequisites
Before we begin, ensure you have the following installed:
Swift
(latest version, preferably Swift 6 or later)
CMake
(we are going to use the most recent version 4.0, but 3.20+ should work just fine)
Ninja
(required for building Swift with CMake)
Setting Up the Project Structure
Create a new directory for your project and navigate into it:
mkdir
MyCuteGame
cd
MyCuteGame
Create the following directory structure:
mkdir
src include
touch
CMakeLists.txt
# Our CMake configuration file
touch
src/main.swift
# Our main Swift file
touch
include/shim.h
# Our C header file for Swift interoperability
touch
include/module.modulemap
# Our C module map for Swift interoperability
The next step is to configure the
CMakeLists.txt
file. Open it in your favorite text editor and add the following content:
cmake_minimum_required
(
VERSION 4.0
)
# Set the project name and languages
project
(
MyCuteGame
LANGUAGES C CXX Swift
# Ensure we include C, C++, and Swift
)
# Set our game sources
file
(
GLOB_RECURSE SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS src/*.swift
)
# Set our executable target
add_executable
(
MyCuteGame
${
SOURCES
}
)
# Include FetchContent to download Cute Framework
include
(
FetchContent
)
# Define cute as our Cute Framework dependency
FetchContent_Declare
(
cute
GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/RandyGaul/cute_framework
)
# Fetch the Cute Framework
FetchContent_MakeAvailable
(
cute
)
# Add the Cute Framework as a dependency
target_include_directories
(
MyCuteGame PUBLIC $<BUILD_INTERFACE:
${
CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR
}
/include>
)
target_link_libraries
(
MyCuteGame cute
)
The
CMakeLists.txt
file defines few key components:
It sets the project name and specifies that we will be using C, C++, and Swift. We use C and C++ as Cute Framework is written in C/C++.
It collects all Swift source files in the
src
directory.
It sets up the Cute Framework as a dependency using
FetchContent
, which allows us to download and include it directly in our project.
It creates an executable target named
MyCuteGame
and links it with the Cute Framework.
It includes the
include
directory for header files, which will be used for Swift interoperability.
Setting Up Swift Interoperability
To enable Swift to call C functions, we need to create a C header file and a module map. Open
include/shim.h
and add the following content:
#pragma once
#include
<cute.h>
The
shim.h
file includes the Cute Framework header, allowing Swift to access its functions.
Next, create the module map in
include/module.modulemap
:
module CCute [extern_c] {
header "shim.h"
export *
}
This module map tells Swift how to import the C header file. The
extern_c
attribute indicates that this module is a C module, which is necessary for Swift interoperability.
With all that in place, we can now write our Swift code in
src/main.swift
. Open this file and add the following content:
import
CCute
// Center the window on the screen
let
options
:
CF_AppOptionFlags
=
Int32
(
CF_APP_OPTIONS_WINDOW_POS_CENTERED_BIT
.
rawValue
)
let
width
:
Int32
=
800
let
height
:
Int32
=
600
// Create the Cute Framework app
let
result
=
cf_make_app
(
"MyCuteGame"
,
0
,
0
,
0
,
width
,
height
,
options
,
CommandLine
.
unsafeArgv
[
0
])
if
cf_is_error
(
result
)
{
fatalError
(
"Failed to create Cute Framework app"
)
}
// Create a demo girl sprite
var
sprite
=
cf_make_demo_sprite
()
// Play the "spin" animation
cf_sprite_play
(
&
sprite
,
"spin"
)
// Make the sprite 4x larger
sprite
.
scale
=
CF_V2
(
x
:
4.0
,
y
:
4.0
)
while
cf_app_is_running
()
{
// Update internal app state without a callback
cf_app_update
(
nil
)
// Update the sprite state
cf_sprite_update
(
&
sprite
)
// Draw the sprite
cf_sprite_draw
(
&
sprite
)
// Draw the app onto the screen with clearing enabled
cf_app_draw_onto_screen
(
true
)
}
cf_destroy_app
()
Configure and Build the Project
Now that we have our project structure and code set up, we can configure and build the project using CMake. Open a terminal in the root directory of your project and run the following commands:
mkdir
build
# Create a build directory
cd
build
cmake
-G
Ninja ..
# Configure the project using CMake with Ninja as the generator
cmake
--build
.
# Build the project
All that’s left is to run the executable. You can do this by executing:
./MyCuteGame
This should launch your Cute Framework application, displaying a window with a spinning girl sprite.
Et voilà! You have successfully set up a C

• [krzat] 认为使用Swift开发应优先选择Swift Package Manager (SPM) 而非CMake。

• 不同工具和语言的选择及其实际开发体验，如C++与Swift的配置复杂性、Swift是否应使用SPM或CMake、以及C#与MonoGame的实际开发体验等。

data.author: pseudolus

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：种族与 ancestry（祖先血统）的关系，以及其在科学研究和医学中的应用

不同观点：
• Metacelsus认为，尽管种族的生物学基础不强，但在医学研究中使用种族作为分类方式仍然有其价值。他主张医学研究应更多关注细致的基因差异，而非传统的种族分类，这样能带来更好的医疗效果。
• notepad0x90指出，种族并不是由生物学差异支撑的概念，而是基于祖先血统的分类。他认为科学不应依赖种族分类，而应更深入地研究具体的遗传差异。他将种族分类比作编程语言的简化分类，认为这是过时且不准确的。
• duxup通过讲述关于克里奥尔人和卡津人的历史背景，展示了种族和文化身份的复杂性，并指出某些群体身份可能会随时间演变和误解。
• like_any_other认为，尽管种族与基因 ancestry 并不完全匹配，但它们仍有一定的对应关系，尤其是在美国不同种族群体间的基因混合程度上。他质疑文章标题的准确性，认为研究并没有完全颠覆种族分类。
• rayiner从个人经验出发，认为种族作为一种粗略的代理在医学上有其价值，特别是在识别不同群体的健康差异时。
• southernplaces7对基于DNA ancestry测试的流行持怀疑态度，认为许多人基于不准确的家庭传说做出种族或民族身份声明。
• systemstops承认种族是社会构建的，但同时也指出它基于一定的生物学现实。他认为随着对古代DNA的研究，人类起源的复杂性正在被揭示，未来的种族差异叙述将更加复杂。
• ilamont指出，便宜的DNA测试导致人们自我识别为多民族，这在人口普查数据中得到体现，并可能在健康应用中造成问题。
• MrDrDr通过引用一篇关于进化压力的论文，说明不同遗传祖先可能在相同环境下演化出相同表型，暗示地理上不同的人类群体可能也会如此。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于种族分类在科学和医学研究中的有效性和适当性。一些人认为种族是过时的分类，应被基因 ancestry 取代；另一些人则认为种族在某些情况下仍有其应用价值。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是自我报告的种族身份与基因 ancestry 之间的差异，以及这种差异对医学和人口统计学研究的影响。
• 历史和社会背景对种族身份的形成和演变的影响也被多次提及，尤其是在不同文化和地理背景下的群体身份认同问题。

data.title: ThornWalli/web-workbench: Old operating system as homepage
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: "web-workbench" 是一个模拟旧操作系统（如 Amiga）界面的网页项目，托管在 lammpee.de。项目包含多个应用，如时钟、计算器、云存储、文档编辑器等，用户可以通过 URL 参数控制启动行为，如禁用启动序列、运行指定应用等。项目使用 Nuxt 构建，代码托管在 GitHub，拥有 57 个星标和 2 个分支。主要开发语言为 TypeScript 和 Vue。用户可以访问不同应用，如合成器、月球城市、绘画工具等，通过特定链接参数启动。项目遵循 MIT 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于设备前盖完整性的惊讶与怀旧情感]

不同观点：
• [selcuka] 对1084设备的前盖保持完整表示惊讶，暗示这可能是不常见的现象，可能因为设备年代久远，前盖通常容易损坏或丢失。
• [krunck] 表达了对CRT显示效果的喜爱，特别是同步线和隔行扫描效果，同时提到了对Amiga 1000的怀旧情感，表明对这种老旧技术有积极的情感联系。

补充讨论：
• [selcuka] 的评论聚焦于设备的物理状态，特别是前盖的完整性，可能暗示了对设备耐用性或保存状态的关注。
• [krunck] 的评论更多是对技术本身的怀旧和美学欣赏，特别是CRT显示器的独特视觉效果，以及Amiga 1000带来的个人回忆。
• 争议的焦点可能在于对老旧设备的不同关注点：一方关注设备的物理保存状态，另一方关注设备的技术和美学价值。

总结来看，这两个评论反映了人们对老旧技术设备的两种不同关注角度：物理保存和情感怀旧。

data.title: Cloudlflare builds OAuth with Claude and publishes all the prompts
data.author: gregorywegory
data.article_summary: `cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` 是一个用于 Cloudflare Workers 的 OAuth 2.1 提供者库，用 TypeScript 编写并支持 PKCE。该库作为 Worker 代码的包装器，自动处理授权和令牌管理，开发者只需编写常规的 API 处理函数，并接收已验证的用户信息。它不限定用户认证方式和 UI 框架，且不存储秘密信息，仅保存其哈希值。使用时需配置 API 路由、授权和令牌端点等，并可选择支持动态客户端注册。该库仍处于测试阶段，API 可能会变动。

OAuth 2.1 Provider Framework for Cloudflare Workers
This is a TypeScript library that implements the provider side of the OAuth 2.1 protocol with PKCE support. The library is intended to be used on Cloudflare Workers.
Beta
As of March, 2025, this library is very new, prerelease software. The API is still subject to change.
Benefits of this library
The library acts as a wrapper around your Worker code, which adds authorization for your API endpoints.
All token management is handled automatically.
Your API handler is written like a regular fetch handler, but receives the already-authenticated user details as a parameter. No need to perform any checks of your own.
The library is agnostic to how you manage and authenticate users.
The library is agnostic to how you build your UI. Your authorization flow can be implemented using whatever UI framework you use for everything else.
The library's storage does not store any secrets, only hashes of them.
Usage
A Worker that uses the library might look like this:
import
{
OAuthProvider
}
from
"my-oauth"
;
import
{
WorkerEntrypoint
}
from
"cloudflare:workers"
;
// We export the OAuthProvider instance as the entrypoint to our Worker. This means it
// implements the `fetch()` handler, receiving all HTTP requests.
export
default
new
OAuthProvider
(
{
// Configure API routes. Any requests whose URL starts with any of these prefixes will be
// considered API requests. The OAuth provider will check the access token on these requests,
// and then, if the token is valid, send the request to the API handler.
// You can provide:
// - A single route (string) or multiple routes (array)
// - Full URLs (which will match the hostname) or just paths (which will match any hostname)
apiRoute
:
[
"/api/"
,
// Path only - will match any hostname
"https://api.example.com/"
// Full URL - will check hostname
]
,
// When the OAuth system receives an API request with a valid access token, it passes the request
// to this handler object's fetch method.
// You can provide either an object with a fetch method (ExportedHandler)
// or a class extending WorkerEntrypoint.
apiHandler
:
ApiHandler
,
// Using a WorkerEntrypoint class
// For multi-handler setups, you can use apiHandlers instead of apiRoute+apiHandler.
// This allows you to use different handlers for different API routes.
// Note: You must use either apiRoute+apiHandler (single-handler) OR apiHandlers (multi-handler), not both.
// Example:
// apiHandlers: {
//   "/api/users/": UsersApiHandler,
//   "/api/documents/": DocumentsApiHandler,
//   "https://api.example.com/": ExternalApiHandler,
// },
// Any requests which aren't API request will be passed to the default handler instead.
// Again, this can be either an object or a WorkerEntrypoint.
defaultHandler
:
defaultHandler
,
// Using an object with a fetch method
// This specifies the URL of the OAuth authorization flow UI. This UI is NOT implemented by
// the OAuthProvider. It is up to the application to implement a UI here. The only reason why
// this URL is given to the OAuthProvider is so that it can implement the RFC-8414 metadata
// discovery endpoint, i.e. `.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.
// Can also be specified as just a path (e.g., "/authorize").
authorizeEndpoint
:
"https://example.com/authorize"
,
// This specifies the OAuth 2 token exchange endpoint. The OAuthProvider will implement this
// endpoint (by directly responding to requests with a matching URL).
// Can also be specified as just a path (e.g., "/oauth/token").
tokenEndpoint
:
"https://example.com/oauth/token"
,
// This specifies the RFC-7591 dynamic client registration endpoint. This setting is optional,
// but if provided, the OAuthProvider will implement this endpoint to allow dynamic client
// registration.
// Can also be specified as just a path (e.g., "/oauth/register").
clientRegistrationEndpoint
:
"https://example.com/oauth/register"
,
// Optional list of scopes supported by this OAuth provider.
// If provided, this will be included in the RFC 8414 metadata as 'scopes_supported'.
/
44159166.article_summary: `cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider` 是一个用于 Cloudflare Workers 的 OAuth 2.1 提供者库，用 TypeScript 编写并支持 PKCE。该库作为 Worker 代码的包装器，自动处理授权和令牌管理，开发者只需编写常规的 API 处理函数，并接收已验证的用户信息。它不限定用户认证方式和 UI 框架，且不存储秘密信息，仅保存其哈希值。使用时需配置 API 路由、授权和令牌端点等，并可选择支持动态客户端注册。该库仍处于测试阶段，API 可能会变动。

data.title: Dystopian tales of that time when I sold out to Google
data.author: stego-tech
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是一位前谷歌员工对在该公司工作经历的反思，重点揭示了谷歌光鲜外表下的阴暗面。作者描述了2007年加入谷歌时对“20%时间”的期待——员工可以利用20%的工作时间自由探索新项目，但实际上这一政策形同虚设，几乎无人能真正享受这一福利。作者因抱怨工作压力和无趣的任务而遭到管理层的责备，因为谷歌希望保持“最佳工作场所”的形象，不允许员工表达不满。文章探讨了资本主义、职场监控和表面进步的虚伪，并通过个人经历揭示了大公司如何通过宣传理想化的形象来吸引和控制员工。
data.comments_summary:

• awbvious认为这篇长文写得非常好，批评该文章的评论可能出于认知失调或因长文阅读能力下降所致，也可能是有偿引导舆论。他还质疑当前是否还能区分真人评论和机器人评论。
• pnathan从个人经历出发，认为文章中提到的问题可能只是阶级流动中常见的困惑，特别是对那些从非白领背景进入白领世界的人而言。他还指出，社会中不同职业的人都应得到尊重，问题在于是否将他们视为低于自己。
• QuercusMax反驳文章中对Google将临时工视为二等公民的解释，认为这是为了规避劳动法，而非简单的为了抬高工程师的地位。他还指出，这种阶级划分是故意制造的。
• arolihas以讽刺的口吻批评了对办公室中一些小问题的过度关注，认为这些问题被夸大为一种“反乌托邦”的现象。

• sa-code质疑为什么软件工程领域没有更多的合作社形式出现。

• jeffbee认为“带完整的自己来工作”这一理念初衷良好，但实际上只需要带工作中所需的部分自我即可。

• 科技公司中的阶级差异，尤其是临时工与正式员工的待遇问题，是否如QuercusMax所说的是故意制造的阶级分化。
• Google是否应对巴西社会的不平等问题负责，neves认为这是文化问题，而不应归咎于Google。

44200773.article_content:
Deep in Mordor where the shadows lie: Dystopian tales of that time when I sold out to Google
4. Juni 2025
I will do something I normally never do here, and make my first ever blog post on the topic of, long sigh: tech. I’ve already talked about Google a number of times on Mastodon which is, blessedly, by design, not discoverable; but I’ve decided to commit the full story to print.  Hopefully this won't come back to bite me in the ass but eh it’s the apocalypse, who cares at this point. At least Wordsmith Dot Social is half-abandoned and has no comment system, so I won’t have to deal with techbros batting for billionaires or preaching the power of Open Source (™ Open Source Initiativeⓡ).
But if you clicked this, Dear Reader, then you wanted the tea; and I am nothing if not forthcoming with tea-spilling. The fact that Google fired me with shut-up money only makes it more fun to do it. So go get some chamomile and sit comfortably, for this is an old woman reminiscing; let’s talk about capitalism and anarchism, about the precariat and surveillance, plush dolls and churrascarias and gay argots; let us go back in time and space, and journey to tropical Brazil in the distant time of 2007…
1. Treason
2007 wasn’t a good year to start a new career, as it turned out.
Google back then prided itself on broadcasting its Best Place To Work award, won year after year after year.  Younger people will have trouble picturing this, but Google used to nurture an image of being the “good one” among megacorps; they championed open standards (except when they didn’t), supported open source projects (until they backstabbed them), and used language that corporate wasn’t supposed to use, like “don’t be evil” (until they, infamously and in a true dark comedy move, retracted that motto). The work environment was all colourful, nerdy cool, not a single necktie in sight—this was seen as brave and refreshing rather than cringe and tired, you see.  And they made a big deal out of something called “20% time”: Every engineer was promised 1/5 of their work time for themselves, to do anything they want. (Google owners will still own whatever you create during your 20% time, natürlich).  Famously, Gmail came out of someone exploring their interests during 20% time.
I don’t think much of anything else came out of it, though.
I found out I was always overworked on drudgery; my main job was to fix boring bugs on the Ruby on Rails internal user accounting system that someone else had developed.  When I complained that this was a far cry from the academia-like, exciting research environment I had been promised, and asked to be assigned to a more challenging project, I was told the following rationale against it: “no”.   Moreover the deadlines and expectations were such that even if I worked (unpaid) overtime every day, I was still was at risk of a performance review.  Making actual use of the “20% time” felt like a pipe dream.
And all that with wages well below even the local market in our crumbling Third World economy. With no exciting research positions nor self-managed time nor compensation, what was the advantage over a high-paying job at Microsoft or IBM? A bright blue vinyl floor and WarioWare Wii in the cafeteria? Well we were the hip tech vanguard, we were all geniuses, we were paid in prestige and promises and ego massages.  Perform good enough and you might be awarded a smattering of shares at some point, get some crumbs from the bountiful capitalists' table.
Like most employees I blamed myself for not working hard enough to get good compensation—or to have time to exercise my right of 20% free time… Until I saw in the “Googlegeist” statistics that some 95% of employees never use their “20% time” at all, being trapped under the same pressures as I was.
I started a discussion about how the recruiter's promise of “20% free time” could maybe be this little thing that the forgotten priestesses of ancient Samarkand called a “lie”.  There was an internal Blogger system, only available for other employees and bosses; and I wrote a post arguing that if no one feels able to use their 20% time, then it’s not much of a perk, is it.
The result of this was my boss having a fit over me “backstabbing” him. See, me complaining about the unfulfilled recruiter promises marked me as an Unhappy Googler. And Google, if you remember, was the Best Place To Work.  It was very important that every promising young engineer thought of Google as the dream job where everyone is happy.  Unhappiness isn't allowed.  My manager was severely scolded by
his
manager for having
dissatisfaction
(gasp) within his team.
I said, “But the issue is real and not my fault, don’t you agree? I just used the data to bring it to attention.  Didn't you say we operate under 'radical transparency'?” (I was young and believed in this kind of slogan. Yes, I was a sitting duck and didn’t stand a chance.)
Boss replied,
Radical transparency doesn't mean you get to say negative things.
